你听过那句老话“你会嫁给你的父亲”吗？我嫁给了我的母亲！乔显然不像我母亲那样抑郁——事实上，我爱他的地方就在于他开心的时候精力充沛。但他情绪阴晴不定，忽高忽低。他叹气的方式，甚至难过的时候都会躲进房间躺下，都跟我母亲一模一样。每当他这样做的时候，我以前教他的所有应对方法就都派上了用场。乔总是说他觉得我能读懂他的心思。每当他看起来很伤心的时候，我似乎总能看出他到底出了什么问题，或者能像其他人一样把他的问题摆到台面上来。我们刚在一起的时候，我喜欢那种我们很合拍的感觉，我能让他开心。但他开始期待我能读懂他的心思，这让我很厌烦。

Being with him is like being with a little kid in a toy store. You know how some kids pick up something expensive—that you didn’t come for—and cling to it like it belongs to them? And then they look like you’ve taken away their best friend when you put it back on the shelf? I’m the one who would just buy the damn thing to make the kid smile. Is that so awful?

跟他在一起就像跟个小孩在玩具店里。你知道有些小孩会拿起一件很贵的东西——你本来就没打算买——然后像宝贝一样抱着不放吗？等你把玩具放回货架上，他们就好像你夺走了他们最好的朋友一样？而我，就是那种会买下那件玩具，只为了让孩子开心的人。这有什么错吗？

There are big payoffs for being a bleeding heart, the one who can bring happiness to a poor suffering soul. You escort the other person from the depths of despair back to the land of the living, an almost mythological journey. The joy of “helping” often blinds us to the fact that so much pity-evoking behavior is manipulative: Give the sufferers what they want and voilà! they’re cured.

做一个心软的人，给可怜的受苦之人带来快乐，确实能获得巨大的回报。你仿佛将他人从绝望的深渊中拯救出来，带回人间，这几乎是一段神话般的旅程。然而，“帮助”带来的喜悦常常蒙蔽了我们的双眼，让我们看不到许多博取同情的行为其实是一种操控：满足受苦者的愿望，瞧！他们就痊愈了。

Again, ironies abound when sufferers meet targets who are bleeding hearts. The targets feel helpless in the face of suffering, so rush in to stop it. But by saying yes to every tear-stained demand, they become even more helpless, unable to stop the personal suffering that comes of ignoring their own needs.

讽刺的是，当受苦之人遇到那些心软无助的人时，往往会产生诸多问题。这些人面对苦难感到无能为力，于是急于出手相助。然而，他们对每一个泪流满面的要求都一一应允，反而变得更加无助，因为忽视自身需求而导致的痛苦，他们根本无力阻止。

The Good Girl Syndrome

乖乖女综合症

When Zoe looked back at her life for a place where a hot button might have formed, she didn’t find any particular traumas. Her childhood was happy, she said, and her family was supportive.

佐伊回顾自己的人生，试图寻找可能引发她内心创伤的契机，但她并没有发现任何特别的创伤经历。她说，她的童年很幸福，家人也很支持她。

The only reason I didn’t fit in perfectly was that I wasn’t as quiet as girls were supposed to be. I was really competitive, and I have always liked to win. That made my parents pretty upset. When I did well in school, they called me a show-off. My sisters got the message, and they never seemed to push themselves very hard, but I was just different. My family always said they were proud of me, but it wasn’t ladylike to call attention to myself in such a loud way.

我唯一格格不入的原因就是我不像女孩子那样安静。我好胜心很强，总是喜欢赢。这让我的父母很不高兴。我学习成绩好的时候，他们会说我爱炫耀。我的姐妹们都明白这一点，她们似乎从来不怎么努力，但我就是不一样。我的家人总是说他们为我感到骄傲，但像我这样大声炫耀自己，在当时看来并不符合淑女的形象。

Zoe spent years keeping her head down, trying not to “come on too strong” in environments that were slow to encourage women to contribute. But her work didn’t go unnoticed, and though she’d never expected to become a manager, she now has 10 people working for her.

佐伊多年来一直低调行事，尽量避免在那些不太鼓励女性贡献的环境中“表现得过于强势”。但她的工作并没有被忽视，尽管她从未想过自己会成为一名经理，但现在她手下有10名员工。

The path has been so rough for women, and for me personally, that I’ve always sworn that I will do things differently. I think there’s plenty of room for decency and compassion in the working world, and I’ve always wanted the people under me to think of me as a friend as well as a boss. I’m not interested in throwing my weight around or imposing my will on my team. We’re colleagues, not master and slave. Who says you have to leave your humanity at the door when you’ve got a corner office?

这条路对女性来说如此艰难，对我个人而言更是如此，所以我一直发誓要以不同的方式行事。我认为职场中仍然有很多空间容纳体面和同情心，我一直希望我的下属不仅把我当老板，也把我当朋友。我不想摆架子，也不想把我的意志强加给团队。我们是同事，不是主仆。谁说坐上高管办公室就必须把人性抛在脑后呢？

Zoe had always taken pride in her ability to advise and support other women. In that arena, she was comfortable. Zoe the noble and compassionate. Zoe the mentor. Zoe the ever-available friend. She unapologetically excelled at being a bleeding heart, and she didn’t want to leave what she considered to be her best qualities behind as she moved up the ladder.

佐伊一直以自己能够指导和支持其他女性而自豪。在这个领域，她游刃有余。她是高尚而富有同情心的佐伊，是良师益友，是随时可以伸出援手的朋友。她毫不掩饰自己善良的本性，即使事业蒸蒸日上，她也不愿放弃自己最宝贵的品质。

In her determination to be a good person as well as a boss, Zoe made friends with some of her staff, especially Tess. The two women had dinner together regularly and often went to the theater, a passion they shared. Because of their social relationship, it was especially difficult for Zoe to “play boss” with Tess and to say no to her. As we saw with Charles and Sherry, being involved with someone on both a professional and personal level, even if it’s a friendship and not a romance, is always tricky and usually ends badly, especially when one person has more authority than the other.

为了做一个好人好老板，佐伊和一些员工成了朋友，尤其是苔丝。两人经常一起吃饭，也经常一起去看戏——这是她们共同的爱好。正因为她们的这种社交关系，佐伊很难对苔丝“摆出领导的姿态”，也很难对她说“不”。正如我们在查尔斯和雪莉的例子中看到的，即使只是朋友而非恋人，在工作和私人层面都与人保持联系也总是很棘手，而且通常不会有好结果，尤其是在一方比另一方更有权力的情况下。

In Charles and Sherry’s situation, the boss was the emotional blackmailer, an expected and typical scenario. But in Zoe’s case, the boss had some very sensitive hot buttons, which set her up to become the target of her employee’s blackmail.

在查尔斯和雪莉的案例中，老板是情感勒索者，这是一种意料之中的典型情况。但在佐伊的案例中，老板有一些非常敏感的弱点，这使她成为了员工勒索的目标。

She just won’t let up on wanting me to give her more responsibility. She says I’m supposed to be her friend, and how can I not help her? When I try to reason with her that friendship has nothing to do with my responsibilities to the company, she tells me that I’ve let my position go to my head and I’m just on a power trip. Oh boy, does that sound familiar to me. I don’t want people to be afraid of me or think I’m unfeeling. AAGH! It’s making me crazy!

她就是不肯放过我，非要我给她更多责任。她说我应该是她的朋友，我怎么能不帮她呢？我跟她讲道理，友情和我在公司的责任无关，她却说我仗着职位就飘了，仗着职权就胡作非为。哎，这话听起来是不是很耳熟？我不想别人怕我，也不想别人觉得我冷酷无情。啊！真是要把我逼疯了！

Zoe had not yet resolved the conflict inside herself between the part of her that wanted to be successful and the part that cared more about being liked. She was suffering from the Good Girl syndrome—a malady that affects many contemporary women who still harbor deep concerns about their ability to be powerful and successful and still be loved. Because of her ambivalence about how she was “supposed” to behave, Zoe opened the door wide to blackmail and Tess walked right in.

佐伊内心深处一直存在着矛盾：一方面她渴望成功，另一方面她更在意别人的喜欢。她患上了“乖乖女综合症”——这种病症困扰着许多当代女性，她们仍然深深担忧自己能否在拥有权力、获得成功的同时，还能被人爱戴。由于她对自己“应该”如何表现感到矛盾，佐伊给了别人勒索的机会，而苔丝正是利用了这一点。

Tess found Zoe to be an ideal dumping ground, willing to listen to her endless litany of complaints. But when Zoe had something pressing to do, or wasn’t able to spend time with Tess, she would be reminded: “You’re the only one who can help me. I’m not going to make it without you.” This was music to Zoe’s ears. This was how she had gotten love in the past—with her caring, compassion and warmth, always being there for people who needed her. But the music was full of sour notes for anyone who wanted to avoid emotional blackmail. Zoe needed to broaden her definition of compassion to include herself.

苔丝发现佐伊是个理想的倾诉对象，她愿意倾听佐伊没完没了的抱怨。但每当佐伊有急事要办，或者没时间陪苔丝时，她就会提醒苔丝：“只有你能帮我。没有你我活不下去。” 这话对佐伊来说简直是天籁之音。过去，她就是这样获得爱的——用她的关心、同情和温暖，总是在需要她的人身边。但对于任何想要避免情感勒索的人来说，这其中都充满了刺耳的音符。佐伊需要拓宽她对同情的定义，把自己也包括在内。

THE SELF-DOUBTER

自我怀疑者

Knowing that we’re not perfect and that we’re capable of making mistakes is healthy. But healthy self-evaluation can easily become self-deprecation. In the face of criticism from someone else, we may disagree at first, then come to believe that our sensors and gauges are faulty. How can we be right if someone important to us says we’re wrong? Maybe we’re just deluded. We know what we see and experience, but we don’t trust it, and frequently we discount the truth of our own ideas, feelings and insights, letting others define how we should be.

认识到我们并不完美，也会犯错，这本身是件好事。但健康的自我评估很容易演变成自我贬低。面对他人的批评，我们起初可能并不认同，但随后会开始怀疑自己的感知和判断是否出了问题。如果重要的人都说我们错了，我们又怎么可能是对的呢？或许我们只是自欺欺人。我们明明知道自己所见所闻，却不相信，常常会忽略自己的想法、感受和洞察力，任由他人来定义我们应该如何。

This is common when we interact with authority figures, especially our parents. It’s “Father Knows Best” all over again. But it can also happen with a lover or a friend we admire, who happens to be a blackmailer. We invest these idealized beings with power and wisdom and believe that they’re smarter, wiser, more “right” than we are. We may not like what they do, or see the fairness in what they ask of us, but lacking confidence in ourselves, we let them have their way, never questioning their demands or their version of reality. (This is particularly true for women who got the message early on that they were creatures of emotion and therefore couldn’t know anything important, while men were superior, the masters of reason and logic.)

这种情况在我们与权威人物互动时很常见，尤其是在与父母相处时。这不就是“父亲最懂”的翻版吗？但这种情况也可能发生在我们仰慕的爱人或朋友身上，而他们恰好是个勒索者。我们赋予这些理想化的人物以权力和智慧，并相信他们比我们更聪明、更有智慧、更“正确”。我们可能不喜欢他们的所作所为，或者不认同他们要求的合理性，但由于缺乏自信，我们任由他们摆布，从不质疑他们的要求或他们对现实的解读。（对于那些从小就被灌输“自己是感性生物，因此无法了解任何重要的事情，而男性才是优越的，是理性和逻辑的主宰”这种观念的女性来说，这种情况尤其如此。）

If we assign wisdom and intelligence to another person, which we’re bound to do if we don’t trust ourselves, it’s simple for them to keep our self-doubt active. They know best, and what’s more, they know what’s best for us.

如果我们把智慧和才智赋予他人（如果我们不信任自己，就必然会这样做），那么他们很容易让我们持续产生自我怀疑。他们自认为最了解情况，而且更重要的是，他们知道什么对我们最好。

When Knowledge Feels Dangerous

当知识令人感到危险时

Self-doubt can take the form of the statement “I know what I know, but I can’t know it.” Our knowledge feels uncomfortable, dangerous, and we feel we can’t face the changes we’d have to make if we accepted our perceptions as true.

自我怀疑可能表现为这样一种说法：“我知道我知道的事情，但我无法真正知道。”我们的认知让我们感到不舒服、危险，我们觉得如果接受自己的认知为真，就无法面对必须做出的改变。

For my client Roberta, who’d been severely beaten by her father and then pressured by her family when she decided to tell, it was painfully difficult to hold on to her reality. “The whole family says I’m wrong,” Roberta told me. “What if they’re right? How can I be the only one who’s right? What if I’ve just imagined all this? What if I’ve just exaggerated it?”

对于我的委托人罗伯塔来说，她曾遭受父亲的毒打，后来在决定说出真相时又受到家人的压力，因此她很难坚持自己的真实想法。“全家人都说我错了，”罗伯塔告诉我，“如果他们是对的呢？怎么可能只有我是对的？如果这一切都只是我的想象呢？如果这一切都是我夸大其词呢？”

Abuse victims often rely on self-doubt to insulate themselves from the horror of their pasts. Among the statements I’ve heard most often are “Maybe it wasn’t as bad as I thought,” “Maybe I’m overreacting,” “Maybe it didn’t happen at all,” “Maybe it was just a dream.” Roberta needed to cling to reality, but at times her grip was tenuous.

受虐者常常依靠自我怀疑来逃避过往的恐怖经历。我最常听到的几句话是：“也许没我想的那么糟”、“也许我反应过度了”、“也许根本没发生过”、“也许只是一场梦”。罗伯塔需要紧紧抓住现实，但有时她却难以自拔。

I can’t lose my whole family because of this. My whole life I’ve tried to do something important for them to notice me, but they never did. My brother was the apple of my parents’ eye because he was the first son, but when I came, I was just a chubby little girl, and my father couldn’t handle that. He hated me from day one. Everything I do is wrong. No one believes me. I just want them to like me, and they hate me now. I must be crazy to go through this. Maybe they’re right.

我不能因为这件事失去整个家庭。我这辈子都在努力做些有意义的事，想让他们注意到我，但他们从来没注意到过。哥哥是父母的掌上明珠，因为他是长子，但我出生的时候，只是个胖乎乎的小女孩，父亲无法接受。他从我出生第一天起就恨我。我做什么都是错的。没有人相信我。我只是想让他们喜欢我，可现在他们却恨我。我一定是疯了才会经历这一切。也许他们是对的。

Under the pressure from her family to recant or face exile, Roberta nearly buckled. She had become the family scapegoat.

在家人要求她收回之前的言论，否则将被流放的压力下，罗伯塔几乎屈服了。她成了家里的替罪羊。

It’s not uncommon for one person to become the representative of everything that goes wrong in a family. Roberta was the repository for the family’s denial and secrecy, and she had to absorb its blame, tension, guilt and anxiety in order to keep everyone else in balance. That way, no one in the family had to look at how unhealthy they were.

一个人成为家庭中所有问题的代表并不罕见。罗伯塔成了家庭否认和秘密的载体，她不得不承受所有的责备、紧张、内疚和焦虑，才能维持家庭的平衡。这样一来，家里的其他人就不必面对他们自身的不健康状态。

It’s especially tough to believe that your own perceptions are valid when people you love are telling you how crazy, wrong or sick you are, but with support and hard work, Roberta did find the courage to hold her ground; her recovery would have been impossible if she hadn’t shed the self-doubt that had clung to her for so long. Like all of the behavioral styles we’ve looked at, it hadn’t kept her safe—it had locked her in prison.

当身边的人都说你疯了、错了或者病了的时候，你很难相信自己的感觉是正确的。但在支持和努力下，罗伯塔最终鼓起勇气坚持己见；如果她没有摆脱长期以来困扰她的自我怀疑，她的康复是不可能的。就像我们之前探讨过的所有行为模式一样，自我怀疑并没有保护她，反而把她困在了牢笼里。

Your fight to hold on to what you know, or even just to realize that you’ve locked away the perceptive center of yourself, may not be as dramatic as Roberta’s, but it’s every bit as important. Just as owning her own truth was a matter of psychic survival for Roberta, for most of us it’s the only way to end emotional blackmail.

你为守护已知而进行的抗争，或者仅仅是意识到自己已经封闭了内心深处的感知中心，或许不像罗伯塔那样戏剧化，但同样重要。正如罗伯塔为了保全性命而坚守真相一样，对我们大多数人来说，这也是摆脱情感勒索的唯一途径。

A MATTER OF BALANCE

平衡问题

All of the behavioral styles we’ve seen are survival mechanisms that we’ve chosen to keep ourselves safe. The problem is, most of them are antiquated, and we’ve never stopped to review and update them. When kept in balance and alternated with other behavior, none of these styles dooms you to the status of “preferred target” of an emotional blackmailer. Avoiding conflict, making peace, even feeling a little self-doubt won’t hurt you—as long as you don’t make them the armor that’s supposed to protect you from feelings you think you can’t stand. If you’re a peacemaker but don’t compromise when you feel strongly that you cannot do what another person asks—no problem. But if you consistently let these traits run the show, you’re holding on to a tow rope that will pull you straight into a sea of emotional blackmail.

我们所见的所有行为模式都是我们为了保护自己而选择的生存机制。问题在于，其中大多数都已过时，我们从未停下来审视和更新它们。如果保持平衡并与其他行为交替使用，这些模式都不会让你成为情感勒索者的“首选目标”。避免冲突、化解矛盾，甚至偶尔的自我怀疑都不会伤害你——只要你不把它们当作保护自己免受难以承受的情绪伤害的盔甲。如果你是一个和平缔造者，但当你强烈地感到自己无法满足他人的要求时，你不会妥协——这没问题。但如果你总是让这些特质主导你的行为，你就如同抓住一根牵引绳，它会把你直接拉入情感勒索的汪洋大海。

TRAINING THE BLACKMAILER OURSELVES

训练我们自己去勒索勒索者

Emotional blackmail takes training and practice. Who provides the training? You do. Who else could tell a blackmailer with absolute certainty and precision: This is what works on me. This is the kind of pressure I always give in to. This is the tool that was custom-designed to probe my most sensitive spot.

情感勒索需要训练和练习。谁来提供这种训练？当然是你自己。还有谁能如此肯定和精准地告诉勒索者：这招对我管用。这种压力我总会屈服。这是专门为我量身打造的，用来探查我最敏感的部位。

You probably don’t remember giving a private tutorial in emotional blackmail, but emotional blackmailers take their cues from our responses to their testing, and they learn from both what we do and what we don’t do. The following lists will help you identify how accomplished you’ve become as a personal trainer for the blackmailers in your life.

你可能不记得自己曾私下教授过情感勒索技巧，但情感勒索者会从我们对他们试探的反应中获取线索，他们会从我们的一言一行中学习。以下列表将帮助你了解自己作为情感勒索者私人教练的水平如何。

When faced with a blackmailer’s pressure, do you:

面对勒索者的压力，你会怎么做？

  • Apologize
    道歉
  • “Reason”
    “原因”
  • Argue
    争论
  • Cry
    哭
  • Plead
    恳求
  • Change or cancel important plans or appointments
    更改或取消重要计划或预约
  • Give in and hope it’s the last time
    屈服吧，希望这是最后一次。
  • Surrender
    投降

Do you find it difficult or impossible to:

您是否觉得以下情况难以或不可能做到：

  • Stand up for yourself?
    敢于维护自己的权益吗？
  • Confront what’s going on?
    直面正在发生的事情？
  • Set limits?
    设定限制？
  • Let blackmailers know that their behavior is unacceptable?
    让勒索者知道他们的行为是不可接受的？

If you answered yes to any of these questions, you are acting as coach and co-star in the blackmail drama. Every day of our lives, we teach people how to treat us by showing them what we will and won’t accept, what we refuse to confront, what we’ll let slide. We may believe that we can make another person’s troublesome behavior disappear if we just ignore it or don’t make a fuss, but the message we send when we’re not forthright about what’s unacceptable is “It worked. Do it again.”

如果你对以上任何一个问题的回答是肯定的，那么你就是在这场勒索闹剧中扮演着教练和联合主演的角色。我们每天都在潜移默化地教别人如何对待我们，通过展现我们能接受什么、不能接受什么，我们拒绝面对什么，以及我们会对什么睁一只眼闭一只眼。我们或许认为，只要置之不理或不予理睬，就能让别人的麻烦行为消失，但如果我们不直截了当地表明自己的不可接受之处，我们传递的信息就是“这招管用，再来一次”。

It Starts with the Little Things

一切始于小事

What many of us don’t realize is that emotional blackmail is built on a series of tests. If it works on a small scale, we’ll see it again in a more significant arena. When we give in to pressure or discomfort, we’re providing positive reinforcement, a reward for bad behavior. The hard truth is that every time we let someone undercut our dignity and integrity, we are colluding—helping them hurt us.

很多人没有意识到，情感勒索是建立在一系列考验之上的。如果它在小范围内奏效，我们会在更大的范围内再次看到它的身影。当我们屈服于压力或不适时，我们实际上是在给予这种行为正向强化，奖励其不良行为。残酷的现实是，每当我们允许他人践踏我们的尊严和正直时，我们都在助纣为虐——帮助他们伤害我们。

We live with the illusion that emotional blackmail springs full-blown into our lives like a whirlwind, coming from nowhere and knocking us over with its force and fury. “How could the other person have changed so dramatically?” we ask ourselves. “How could things have suddenly become so strained?” And sometimes the entrance of emotional blackmail into a relationship is sudden, but just as often it builds slowly, gaining ground over time because we let it.

我们常常误以为情感勒索会像旋风一样突然降临，毫无预兆地以迅雷不及掩耳之势将我们击倒。“对方怎么会变化如此之大？”我们不禁自问，“事情怎么会突然变得如此紧张？”有时，情感勒索的确会突然闯入一段关系，但更多时候，它会在我们纵容下慢慢滋生，日积月累。

Liz began telling me about her problems with her husband, Michael, by describing how frightened his threats of punishment made her feel. But as she looked back, she realized that long before the big crisis between them, she had been letting Michael get away with numerous incidents of more subtle emotional blackmail.

莉兹开始向我倾诉她和丈夫迈克尔之间的问题，她描述了迈克尔威胁要惩罚她让她感到多么恐惧。但回想起来，她意识到，早在他们之间爆发这场大危机之前，她就已经对迈克尔多次更为隐晦的情感勒索行为睁一只眼闭一只眼了。

Michael’s always been Mr. Perfect. He’s one of those guys who’d make a date to meet you and then leave if you were even five minutes late—just to make sure you knew you should’ve been on time. I should’ve had a clue when he started lining up my magazines on the coffee table and complaining when they weren’t just so. His rules—and he does have a rule for every little thing—were a source of tension between us from the moment we started living together. And when we had the twins, forget it. Just try to keep a house spotless with toddlers. But reality meant nothing to Michael. He kept letting me know he wanted the house kept a certain way. How did he let me know? He had his ways.

迈克尔一直都是个完美先生。他就是那种会跟你约好时间，然后如果你迟到哪怕五分钟，他都会走人的人——就为了确保你知道自己应该准时。他开始把我的杂志整齐地摆放在咖啡桌上，如果没摆放整齐他还会抱怨，我当时就应该有所警觉。他的规矩——而且他事事都有规矩——从我们开始同居的那一刻起，就成了我们之间矛盾的根源。等我们有了双胞胎，那就更糟了。想想看，带着两个蹒跚学步的孩子，想把家里打扫得一尘不染都难。但现实对迈克尔来说根本不算什么。他总是让我知道他想要家里保持某种特定的状态。他是怎么让我知道的？他有他自己的一套方法。

I remember one day when I left a few dishes in the sink instead of putting them in the dishwasher. When I came home, Michael had piled them on the floor. I could hardly believe it—but I didn’t say anything. I just swallowed hard and picked them up.

我记得有一天，我把几个碗碟留在水槽里，没有放进洗碗机。回家后，迈克尔把它们堆在了地板上。我简直不敢相信——但我什么也没说。我只是咽了口唾沫，把它们捡了起来。

Liz jumped to the conclusion that she’d been wrong and deserved Michael’s anger, but she was the one doing the training. Michael couldn’t fail to notice how effective his punishment had been.

莉兹立刻认定自己错了，活该承受迈克尔的怒火，但明明是她负责训练的。迈克尔不可能没注意到他的惩罚有多么有效。

Now that I think about it, it seems like he was always finding a way to correct my lapses. Once I left without closing the garage door, and when I got home, Michael had unhooked the automatic door opener so I had to get out of the car and open the door myself. It was like one of those punishments your parents dream up that you’re supposed to never forget. He had me convinced that I was a slob, irresponsible and a bad mother, and I felt guilty as hell and ended up apologizing.

现在想想，他好像总想方设法纠正我的错误。有一次我出门忘了关车库门，等我到家的时候，迈克尔已经把自动车库门的遥控器拆掉了，害得我不得不下车自己开门。这就像父母精心设计的那种惩罚，让你永远都忘不了。他让我觉得我邋遢、不负责任，还是个糟糕的母亲，我为此感到无比愧疚，最后不得不向他道歉。

Petty punishments like Michael’s strip us of our adult dignity and power. They’re the emotional equivalent of spankings, and they work to infantilize us—reduce us to bad little children who need to learn a lesson. As Liz found, the guilt we feel easily becomes a sense that “I’m bad, so I deserve this treatment.”

像迈克尔那样的轻微惩罚剥夺了我们成年人的尊严和力量。它们在情感上等同于体罚，会让我们变得幼稚——把我们贬低成需要接受教训的坏孩子。正如莉兹所发现的，我们感受到的内疚很容易演变成一种“我做错了，所以我活该受罚”的想法。

With her hot buttons buzzing, Liz didn’t even consider letting Michael see how upset she was, and she never thought of confronting him. But by hiding her feelings, she was training him to escalate his punishing behavior to keep her in line. Blackmailers learn how far they can go by observing how far we let them go. We don’t know what would have happened if Liz had nipped this behavior in the bud. We do know Liz taught him that if he infantilized her, insulted her and threatened her, he’d get what he wanted. Michael’s punishments were repeated, ever escalating, finally reaching a painful and frightening apex when he threatened to cut her off financially and take the children if she tried to leave him.

莉兹怒火中烧，根本没想过让迈克尔看出她有多难过，也从未想过要和他对质。但她隐藏自己的感受，却反而让他学会了不断升级惩罚手段来控制她。勒索者会通过观察我们容忍他们的底线来摸索自己的底线。我们不知道如果莉兹当初及时制止这种行为会发生什么。但我们知道，莉兹教会了他，只要他把她当小孩一样对待，侮辱她，威胁她，就能达到目的。迈克尔的惩罚不断升级，最终达到了一个痛苦而可怕的顶峰：他威胁说，如果莉兹试图离开他，就断了她的经济来源，夺走孩子。

On the surface there doesn’t seem to be much of a relationship between disconnecting a garage opener and the bolder threats that came later, but the early incidents were like the cold that can lead to pneumonia—dangerous when ignored and untreated.

表面上看，断开车库门遥控器和后来更大胆的威胁之间似乎没有什么联系，但早期的事件就像感冒会导致肺炎一样——如果忽视和不治疗，就会很危险。

As all targets find, in emotional blackmail the present is a prologue to the future. What you teach today will come back to haunt you tomorrow.

所有受害者都会发现，在情感勒索中，当下只是未来的序幕。你今天所教的，明天就会反过来困扰你。

SELF-BLACKMAIL

自我勒索

Despite the title of this chapter, sometimes blackmail only takes one. We can easily stage every element of the blackmail drama alone—from request through resistance, pressure and threats, acting as both blackmailer and target. This happens when our fear of other people’s negative responses is strong, and our imagination takes over. We assume that if we ask for what we want, they’ll disapprove, withdraw, be angry, and we’re so adamant about protecting ourselves that we don’t let ourselves take any chances, even the minimal risk of asking the other person “How would you feel if I . . .”

尽管本章标题如此，但有时勒索只需一人即可完成。我们完全可以独自一人策划勒索的每一个环节——从提出要求到遭到拒绝，再到施压和威胁，既是勒索者又是受害者。这种情况发生在我们极度害怕他人负面反应，想象力占据主导的时候。我们假定，如果我们提出自己的要求，对方会反对、疏远、生气，我们如此执着于保护自己，以至于不敢冒任何风险，哪怕只是问对方“如果我……你会作何感想？”这样微不足道的问题。

Let me show you what I mean.

让我来解释一下我的意思。

My friend Leslie has been dreaming about taking a trip to Italy for more than a year, making arrangements with friends and lining up tickets for the opera. But six months ago, her daughter, Elaine, went through a rough divorce, and Leslie has been helping her out with an occasional loan and by babysitting for Elaine’s two small children. Leslie and Elaine have been through their share of rough times, but they’ve gotten closer since Elaine’s divorce, and Leslie is thrilled about the new friendship that’s bloomed between them.

我的朋友莱斯利一年多来一直梦想着去意大利旅行，她和朋友们商量着行程，甚至订好了歌剧票。但六个月前，她的女儿伊莱恩经历了一场痛苦的离婚，莱斯利开始不时地借钱给她，并帮忙照看伊莱恩的两个孩子。莱斯利和伊莱恩都经历过不少磨难，但自从伊莱恩离婚后，她们的关系反而更加亲密了，莱斯利也为她们之间萌生的这份新友谊感到无比欣慰。

“I couldn’t possibly do anything to jeopardize that,” Leslie told me, “and I just know that if I take the trip, she’ll get angry and think I’m being selfish. How can I go on this vacation when she’s struggling and needs my help?” Leslie’s daughter would probably cope perfectly well if her mother told her about the trip, but Leslie refuses to give herself a reality check, preferring to postpone a much-needed holiday.

“我绝对不能做任何危及她的事情，”莱斯利告诉我，“而且我知道，如果我去了，她会生气，会觉得我自私。她现在很艰难，需要我的帮助，我怎么能去度假呢？”如果莱斯利告诉女儿她的旅行计划，女儿或许能很好地接受，但莱斯利却拒绝面对现实，宁愿推迟这个急需的假期。

How often do we deprive ourselves of something that’s reasonable and well within our means simply because we fear another person’s reaction? We shelve our dreams and plans because we’re “sure” someone will object—though we’ve never tried bringing up our ideas. We want something, we resist, we pressure ourselves by making up the negative consequences, and we keep ourselves from doing what we want to do. We create our own FOG. That’s self-blackmail.

我们常常因为害怕别人的反应，而放弃一些合理且完全在我们能力范围之内的事情。我们搁置梦想和计划，因为我们“确信”有人会反对——尽管我们从未尝试提出过自己的想法。我们想要什么，却又抗拒，我们臆想负面后果来给自己施加压力，最终阻碍自己去做想做的事。我们自己制造了迷雾。这就是自我勒索。

We may have a history with other people that justifies our apprehension about their reactions, but often we make completely unrealistic assumptions. We may even come to resent people for keeping us from doing something they didn’t know about. We step carefully around our hot buttons and lock ourselves in a safe, airless pattern of self-blackmail.

我们或许与他人有过一些过往经历，这些经历让我们对他们的反应感到担忧，但很多时候，我们的假设完全不切实际。我们甚至可能因为别人阻止我们去做他们不知情的事情而心生怨恨。我们小心翼翼地避开自己的敏感点，把自己锁进一个安全却窒息的自我勒索模式中。

A NOTE OF CAUTION

注意事项

Please don’t use this chapter as a way of beating up on yourself. Until now, you’ve done the best you could with what you knew. You’ve been a member of the PTA—that vast group of people whose behavior took shape Prior To Awareness. Look compassionately at the person you’ve been, and then use this chapter to give yourself a deeper understanding of the emotional blackmail transaction and the role you have played in it.

请不要把这一章当作自我责备的借口。到目前为止，你已经尽了全力，运用了你所掌握的知识。你一直是“家长教师协会”（PTA）的一员——这个庞大的群体，他们的行为模式在觉醒之前就已经形成。请以同情的目光审视过去的自己，然后利用这一章更深入地理解这种情感勒索行为以及你在其中扮演的角色。

# ↩

7

The Impact of Blackmail

勒索的影响

Emotional blackmail may not be life-threatening, but it robs us of one of our most precious possessions—our integrity. Integrity is that place inside where our values and our moral compass reside, clarifying what’s right and wrong for us. Though we tend to equate integrity with honesty, it’s actually much more. The word itself means “wholeness,” and we experience it as the firm knowledge that “This is who I am. This is what I believe. This is what I am willing to do—and this is where I draw the line.”

情感勒索或许不会危及生命，但它会剥夺我们最宝贵的财富之一——正直。正直是我们内心深处价值观和道德准则的所在，它指引我们分辨是非对错。虽然我们往往将正直等同于诚实，但它的含义远不止于此。“正直”一词本身就意味着“完整”，它让我们坚定地认识到：“这就是我。这就是我的信仰。这就是我愿意做的事——而这就是我的底线。”

Most of us would have no problem listing the do’s and don’ts or “Thou shalt” and “Thou shalt not”s that guide us. But weaving those beliefs into the fabric of our lives, and defending them under the pressure of emotional blackmail, is far more difficult. Many times we capitulate and compromise our integrity, losing our ability to remember how it feels to be whole.

我们大多数人都能毫不费力地列出那些指导我们行为的准则，比如“该做”和“不该做”。但要将这些信念融入我们生活的方方面面，并在情感勒索的压力下捍卫它们，却要困难得多。很多时候，我们屈服于诱惑，损害了自己的正直，最终失去了完整自我的感觉。

What does integrity feel like? Take a moment to look at the following list—you might want to read it aloud—and imagine that each of the statements is true for you most of the time.

正直是什么感觉？请花点时间看看下面的清单——你可以大声朗读——并想象一下，清单上的每一项在大多数情况下都符合你的实际情况。

  • I take a stand for what I believe in.
    我坚持自己的信念。
  • I don’t let fear run my life.
    我不会让恐惧主宰我的生活。
  • I confront people who have injured me.
    我会质问那些伤害过我的人。
  • I define who I am rather then being defined by other people.
    我定义自己，而不是被别人定义。
  • I keep the promises I make to myself.
    我信守对自己许下的承诺。
  • I protect my physical and emotional health.
    我注重保护我的身心健康。
  • I don’t betray other people.
    我不会背叛他人。
  • I tell the truth.
    我说的是实话。

These are powerful, liberating statements to apply to ourselves, and when they genuinely reflect our way of being in the world, they give us a balance point, a sure sense of equilibrium that keeps us from being pushed off center by the stresses and pressures that are constantly coming at us. When we give in to emotional blackmail, we cross off the items on this list, one by one, by forgetting what’s right for us. And each time we do, we sacrifice a little bit more of our wholeness.

这些话语充满力量，能解放我们的心灵。当它们真正反映出我们为人处世的方式时，就能为我们带来平衡点，一种稳固的平衡感，使我们不至于被不断袭来的压力和焦虑所扰乱。当我们屈服于情感勒索时，我们就像在忘记什么才是真正对我们有益的，一步步地践踏着这份清单上的每一项。每一次，我们都在牺牲自己的一部分完整性。

When we violate this essential sense of ourselves, we lose one of the clearest guiding forces in our lives. We’re set adrift.

当我们违背这种对自我的基本认知时，我们就失去了生活中最清晰的指引力量之一。我们会迷失方向。

THE IMPACT ON OUR SELF-RESPECT

对我们自尊的影响

Wimp. Gutless wonder. Failure. Chump. We have dozens of ways of describing ourselves as we walk away from an emotional blackmailer, having given in once more. Our judgment about ourselves becomes cloudy as we endure the blackmail FOG: “If I had any backbone, I wouldn’t be giving in” we say to ourselves. “Am I really this weak? What’s the matter with me?”

懦夫。没胆的家伙。失败者。笨蛋。当我们再次屈服于情感勒索者，转身离开时，我们有无数种方式来形容自己。在勒索的迷雾中，我们对自己的判断变得模糊不清：“如果我有点骨气，就不会屈服，”我们对自己说。“我真的这么软弱吗？我到底怎么了？”

There’s no need to be inflexible or to beat yourself up if you give in to someone over relatively minor issues. Most of us realize that we often have to bend a little and make compromises, and there are plenty of times when giving in to pressure doesn’t mean that much. But falling into patterns of giving in to things that aren’t good for you takes its toll on your self-image. There is always a bottom line, a point at which to give in is to violate our most important principles and beliefs.

即使因为一些小事而向他人妥协，也不必固执己见或自责。我们大多数人都明白，很多时候需要做出一些让步和妥协，而且很多时候，屈服于压力也并非意味着什么大不了的事。但是，如果总是向对自己不利的事情妥协，就会损害你的自我认知。凡事都有底线，一旦妥协，就意味着违背我们最重要的原则和信念。

How We Let Ourselves Down

我们是如何让自己失望的

The price we pay for acting as though that point does not exist became painfully clear to Maria over time. Some months after we began working together, she was unusually quiet in one of our sessions, a change from her typically outgoing manner. When I asked her what was going on, she answered slowly.

随着时间的推移，玛丽亚痛苦地意识到，如果我们假装这个问题不存在，将会付出怎样的代价。在我们开始合作几个月后，有一次咨询中，她异常安静，这与她平日里外向的性格截然不同。当我问她发生了什么事时，她缓缓地回答道。

I’m angry about many, many things. Of course I’m not happy about what Jay’s done. But what bothers me the most is what I have done to myself. I know that we’ve talked a lot about family, family, family and how I’ve always honored that and made it come first in my life. But when I look in the mirror, I see a woman who has not respected herself enough to tell her husband, “I will not let you degrade me or my marriage by being unfaithful.” I feel as though I’ve really let myself down. I have done everything but stand up for myself. I might as well be wearing a sign that says, “Kick me.”

我有很多很多事都让我生气。当然，杰伊的所作所为让我很不高兴。但最让我难过的是我自己对自己的所作所为。我知道我们谈了很多关于家庭、家庭、家庭的话题，也知道我一直以来都非常重视家庭，把它放在我生命中的首位。但是当我照镜子的时候，我看到的却是一个连对自己都不尊重，以至于不敢对丈夫说“我不会让你用不忠来玷污我和我的婚姻”的女人。我觉得自己真的辜负了自己。我什么都做了，就是没有为自己挺身而出。我感觉自己就像是挂了个牌子，上面写着“来踢我吧”。

I pointed out to Maria that, though it didn’t seem like it to her, she’d come a long way, and I reminded her that she’d worked hard to reach a point where she recognized her own needs and could push back against the pressures of her upbringing and environment. Part of the intense self-reproach she was feeling was the result of seeing clearly, for the first time in years—or maybe ever—that she’d managed to have a strong, conscious sense of values that respected and protected the rights of everyone but herself.

我向玛丽亚指出，虽然她自己可能感觉不到，但她已经走了很远的路。我提醒她，她付出了很多努力才走到今天这一步，能够认识到自己的需求，并能抵制成长环境带来的压力。她强烈的自我责备，部分原因在于她多年来——或许是生平第一次——如此清晰地意识到，她曾经拥有过一套强大而自觉的价值观，这套价值观尊重并维护了所有人的权利，唯独忽略了她自己。

A Vicious Cycle

恶性循环

Honoring and protecting our integrity isn’t easy. Blackmailers shout down our inner guidance by creating confusion and uproar, and as they do, we seem to lose contact with the knowing parts of ourselves, only to kick ourselves when we realize we’ve given in again.

坚守和捍卫我们的正直并非易事。勒索者通过制造混乱和骚动来压制我们内心的指引，在这个过程中，我们似乎与自己清醒的认知失去了联系，最终在意识到自己再次屈服时，只能懊悔不已。

Patty, who let her husband, Joe, persuade her to ask her hospitalized aunt for a loan, epitomized the plight of the target who’s being heavily pressured to give in to blackmail.

帕蒂在丈夫乔的劝说下，向住院的姑姑借钱，她的经历充分体现了遭受重创而被迫屈服于勒索的受害者的困境。

It was a totally no-win situation. If I didn’t make the call, I would have felt like just this horrible, horrible person letting joe down. He’s the breadwinner, and here he is asking me this little favor when he does everything. It seemed so reasonable. But after I’d done it, I felt just awful . . . horrible, worthless. I felt used, like I had no spine, which was true.

这完全是个进退两难的局面。如果我不打那个电话，我会觉得自己像个罪人，辜负了乔。他是家里的顶梁柱，现在却来求我帮个小忙，而他平时什么都做。这事儿听起来合情合理。但打完电话之后，我感觉糟透了……糟糕透了，觉得自己一文不值。我觉得自己被利用了，像个没骨气的人，而事实也的确如此。

Patty was caught in the classic “damned if you do, damned if you don’t” dilemma that drowns so many blackmail targets in waves of self-condemnation. As long as she accepted Joe’s premise that what he wanted so urgently was a “little favor” that she owed him, she couldn’t bring herself to resist doing what he asked—even though, as she put it, “I’m not the kind of person who would do something like that. Who in their right mind would call someone who just had surgery and beg for money?”

帕蒂陷入了典型的“进退两难”的困境，这种困境让许多被勒索的人深陷自我谴责的漩涡之中。只要她接受了乔的说法，即他如此迫切地想要的是她欠他的“一个小忙”，她就无法拒绝他的要求——尽管正如她所说，“我不是那种会做这种事的人。谁会正常地打电话给一个刚做完手术的人乞讨钱财呢？”

Patty didn’t lose her sense of what was appropriate, but in her need to keep the peace with Joe, she acted as though she had. As a result, she was filled with remorse and self-contempt.

帕蒂并没有丧失判断力，但为了和乔维持和平，她却装作丧失了判断力。结果，她充满了悔恨和自责。

The unfortunate result of such self-flagellation, however, is that it creates a vicious cycle. Under pressure, we do something that doesn’t fit with our sense of who we are. In shock and disbelief, we realize what we’ve done and begin to believe that we are actually as deficient as blackmailers make us out to be. Then, having lost our self-respect, we’re even more vulnerable to emotional blackmail because now we’re especially desperate for the approval of our blackmailers—which would prove that we’re really not so bad. We may not be able to uphold our own standards, but maybe we can meet theirs.

然而，这种自我鞭笞的不幸后果是，它会形成恶性循环。在压力之下，我们会做出一些与自我认知不符的事情。震惊和难以置信之后，我们意识到自己做了什么，并开始相信自己真的像勒索者所描述的那样糟糕。然后，由于失去了自尊，我们更容易受到情感勒索，因为我们现在格外渴望得到勒索者的认可——这可以证明我们其实并没有那么糟糕。我们或许无法坚守自己的标准，但也许可以满足他们的要求。

As Patty put it,

正如帕蒂所说，

I was afraid that if I didn’t make the call, he wouldn’t love me, that I wasn’t a good wife. And I needed him. He wouldn’t love me, and I would be letting him down.

我害怕如果我不打电话，他就不会爱我了，我就不是一个好妻子。而我需要他。他就不会爱我了，我会让他失望。

Even though Patty felt terrible about making that phone call, it was more comfortable for her than saying no to Joe. Given a choice between violating her own sense of right and wrong and looking like a bad wife, we know what choice she made.

尽管帕蒂对打那个电话感到非常懊悔，但对她来说，这比拒绝乔要舒服得多。如果要在违背自己的道德准则和被视为坏妻子之间做出选择，我们都知道她会选择哪一个。

Rationalizing and Justifying

合理化和正当化

Protecting our integrity can be frightening and lonely. It puts us at risk of incurring the disapproval of people we care about, and it may even jeopardize a relationship. Margaret wanted to hold on to Cal—no matter what—so she did what many blackmail targets do given a choice between being true to themselves and complying with what someone else wants: she rationalized.

捍卫自身正直可能令人恐惧且孤独。它使我们面临被所爱之人否定甚至危及一段关系的风险。玛格丽特无论如何都想留住卡尔，所以她像许多被勒索者一样，在忠于自我和屈从于他人意愿之间做出选择时，会选择为自己的行为辩解。

Margaret tried to come up with “good reasons” for doing what Cal wanted. She told herself that group sex was no big deal—maybe she was being old-fashioned and prudish. After all, he was so wonderful in so many other ways. Margaret’s need for such extensive rationalizing should have been a tip-off to her that she was stepping outside the boundaries of what she knew to be true and healthy.

玛格丽特试图为自己满足卡尔的要求找“合理的理由”。她告诉自己，群交没什么大不了的——也许是她太老派、太保守了。毕竟，卡尔在其他方面那么优秀。玛格丽特如此费尽心思地为自己的行为辩解，这本该让她意识到，她正在越过自己所知的真理和健康的界限。

It takes a lot of mental and emotional energy to persuade ourselves that we can accept something that’s not OK for us. An internal war rages between our integrity and the blackmailer’s pressure, and as in any war there are losses and casualties. Margaret paid an agonizing price for her rationalizations, and we worked together to rebuild her self-respect, silence the criticism she was blasting herself with and strengthen her connection to that guiding voice inside.

要说服自己接受一些不适合自己的事情，需要耗费大量的精力和情感。一场内心的战争在我们的正直和勒索者的压力之间激烈展开，而任何战争都会造成损失和伤亡。玛格丽特为她的自我辩解付出了惨痛的代价，我们共同努力，帮助她重建自尊，平息她自我批判的声音，并加强她与内心指引之声的联系。

No matter how confused, self-doubting or ambivalent we are about what’s happening in our interactions with other people, we can never entirely silence that inner voice that always tells us the truth. We may not like the sound of the truth, and we often let it murmur just outside our consciousness, not stopping long enough to listen. But when we pay attention to it, it leads us toward wisdom, health and clarity. That voice is the guardian of our integrity.

无论我们对与他人互动中发生的事情感到多么困惑、自我怀疑或矛盾，我们都无法完全压制内心那个始终告诉我们真相的声音。我们或许不喜欢真相的声音，常常任由它在意识之外低语，却从未停下来认真倾听。但当我们关注它时，它会引领我们走向智慧、健康和清明。那声音是我们正直的守护者。

Eve had signed up for classes that would help her get a job and gain some financial security as she worked to build her art career. But under pressure from Elliot, her optimistic plan crumbled.

伊芙报名参加了一些课程，希望能找到工作，在发展艺术事业的同时获得一些经济保障。但在埃利奥特的压力下，她乐观的计划破灭了。

All I want to do is get some skills so that I don’t always have to be dependent on someone. I thought I’d take some computer graphics courses, a little bit of illustration, so I don’t always have to hope for some big commission to come along. But he really, really hated that, and one day, literally the day I was going to take this silly computer test, he threatened to overdose. I was so stunned, it was almost like my ultimate nightmare had come true. He was sitting there with a bottle of liquor and a whole lot of bottles of pills. How could I go back to school after that? I told myself, Don’t do it, Eve, stay in the classes, but . . . I just. . . collapsed. I just said, Look, to hell with it.

我只想学点技能，这样就不用总是依赖别人了。我本来想学些电脑绘图课，再学点插画，这样就不用总是盼着能接到什么大单子了。但他真的非常非常讨厌这样，有一天，就在我要参加那个愚蠢的电脑考试的那天，他威胁要服药过量自杀。我当时震惊极了，感觉就像我最可怕的噩梦成真了。他坐在那里，手里拿着一瓶酒和一大堆药片。我怎么还能继续上学？我告诉自己，别这样，伊芙，继续上课，但是……我……就崩溃了。我对自己说，算了，去他的吧。

Like most blackmail targets, Eve lost sight of the fact that some of the most important promises we make are to ourselves. Compared with Elliot’s pressure, and her belief that she was responsible for his very survival, those promises seemed almost trivial.

和大多数被勒索的对象一样，伊芙忘记了我们做出的一些最重要的承诺其实是对自己许下的。与埃利奥特施加的压力，以及她认为自己有责任保住埃利奥特性命的想法相比，这些承诺显得微不足道。

Elliot’s threats were dire, and Eve wasn’t ready yet to deal with them, but even when the pressure is less intense, many targets will cop out on themselves. One of the most serious effects of emotional blackmail is the way it narrows our world. We often give up people and activities we love in order to please our blackmailers, especially if they are controlling or overly needy.

埃利奥特的威胁十分严重，伊芙还没做好应对的准备，但即便压力没那么大，许多受害者最终也会屈服。情感勒索最严重的后果之一就是它会让我们的世界变得狭隘。为了取悦勒索者，我们常常会放弃自己热爱的人和事，尤其当他们控制欲强或过度依赖时。

But every time you don’t take the class you want to take, every time you stop pursuing an interest or stop seeing people you care about in order to make a blackmailer happy, you are giving up an important part of yourself and diminishing your wholeness.

但是，每次你为了取悦勒索者而放弃自己想上的课，每次你为了满足自己的兴趣而停止追求自己的兴趣或停止与自己关心的人见面，你都在放弃自己重要的一部分，削弱自己的完整性。

THE IMPACT ON OUR WELL-BEING

对我们身心健康的影响

Emotional blackmail leaves us full of unexpressed smouldering feelings. Patty was highly resentful of Joe’s manipulations—and her feelings were perfectly natural—but even though she was aware of how she felt, she couldn’t get the relief that would come from venting her anger and frustration. Most blackmail targets tend to stuff these feelings, only to have them surface in all kinds of distressing forms: depression, anxiety, overeating, headaches—an entire spectrum of physical and emotional manifestations that take the place of directly expressing the way we feel.

情感勒索会让我们内心充满未曾表达的压抑情绪。帕蒂对乔的操纵深恶痛绝——她的感受完全可以理解——但即便她清楚自己的感受，也无法通过发泄愤怒和沮丧来获得解脱。大多数被勒索的人往往会压抑这些情绪，最终它们会以各种令人痛苦的形式爆发：抑郁、焦虑、暴饮暴食、头痛——一系列身心症状，取代了我们直接表达感受的方式。

When Catherine’s therapist used emotional blackmail to pressure her into joining a group, Catherine was full of anger, not only at the therapist but also at a close friend who had been drawn into the situation.

当凯瑟琳的治疗师使用情感勒索迫使她加入一个小组时，凯瑟琳充满了愤怒，不仅对治疗师，也对被卷入此事的亲密朋友感到愤怒。

My friend was in the group and she started to pressure me, too. Later I found out that Rhonda had told her to work on me. So I had both of them. I really felt double-teamed and very angry. But it was anger I didn’t feel safe to express directly. In fact, I didn’t even know if I had a right to be angry. So I just got more depressed instead. The whole experience was really awful.

我的朋友也在那个小组里，她也开始给我施加压力。后来我才知道，是朗达让她去对付我的。所以，我同时要应付她们两个。我感觉自己被她们俩夹击，非常生气。但我又觉得不能直接表达这种愤怒。事实上，我甚至不知道自己有没有资格生气。所以，我只能更加沮丧。整个经历真的糟透了。

Rhonda did me a lot of harm. I was very vulnerable at the time, and she never supported or validated me. She made me feel worse about myself—more inadequate and more unlovable. Thank God I had the wisdom to see what was going on and get away.

朗达对我的伤害很大。那时我非常脆弱，她从来没有支持过我，也没有肯定过我。她让我更加自卑——觉得自己更差劲，更不值得被爱。感谢上帝，我足够明智，看清了真相，并离开了她。

Like Catherine, many targets of emotional blackmail question their right to even have certain feelings—especially angry ones. They may turn their anger inward, where it can become depression, or they may rationalize to cover up how angry they are. Catherine was fortunate because she finally was able to move past her depression and self-doubt and get out of an unhealthy situation.

和凯瑟琳一样，许多情感勒索的受害者都会质疑自己是否有权拥有某些情绪——尤其是愤怒的情绪。他们可能会将愤怒内化，最终导致抑郁；或者他们会为自己的行为寻找理由来掩盖内心的愤怒。凯瑟琳很幸运，因为她最终克服了抑郁和自我怀疑，摆脱了那种不健康的处境。

When Mental Health Is on the Line

当心理健康受到威胁时

Eve was so enmeshed in her destructive relationship with Elliot that she believed her sanity was being threatened.

伊芙深陷于与艾略特的这段毁灭性关系中，以至于她觉得自己的精神状态受到了威胁。

I knew I had really gotten myself in trouble. My emotions were so frazzled I was afraid they were gonna have to take me in and put me in the rubber room. I literally had to get in a rocking chair and rock. It really felt like I was just gonna go bananas, and I couldn’t get any emotional distance from him. It was that horrible combination of rage and love and guilt.

我知道自己真的闯了大祸。我的情绪崩溃了，害怕他们会把我送进精神病院。我只能坐在摇椅上摇来摇去。我感觉自己快要疯了，而且根本无法和他保持任何情感上的距离。那种愤怒、爱和愧疚交织在一起，真是糟糕透了。

When emotional blackmail is as oppressive and omnipresent as it was for Eve, it creates emotions of such intensity that we do sometimes believe we are “going crazy.” I assured Eve that many people confuse strong emotions with going crazy and that there was much we could do to diminish those fears for her. She was right—there did need to be some emotional distance before she could begin to deal effectively and calmly with the soap opera her life had become. And together we would create it.

当情感勒索像伊芙经历的那样，无处不在且令人窒息时，它会引发如此强烈的情绪，以至于我们有时会觉得自己“快要疯了”。我向伊芙保证，很多人都会把强烈的情绪误认为是精神错乱，而且我们可以做很多事情来减轻她的这种恐惧。她是对的——在她能够有效且冷静地应对她生活中这出闹剧之前，确实需要保持一定的情感距离。而我们将共同创造这种距离。

As Eve so clearly illustrates, emotional blackmail can be dangerous to your mental health. It can also be dangerous to your physical health, especially if you try to push yourself past your physical limits to please a blackmailer.

正如伊芙的例子清楚地表明的那样，情感勒索会对你的心理健康造成危害。它也会危害你的身体健康，尤其当你为了取悦勒索者而勉强自己超越身体极限时。

Physical Pain as a Warning

身体疼痛是一种警告

Kim, the magazine editor who was working punishing hours in response to pressure from her boss, woke up in the middle of the night with shooting pains from her shoulders to her wrists.

杂志编辑金（Kim）迫于老板的压力，长时间工作，一天半夜，她突然感到肩膀到手腕一阵剧痛，然后惊醒过来。

I feared something like this was coming, but it’s always a shock when it hits you. I don’t know why I couldn’t say, “My arms are beginning to hurt and I have to slow down a little — do one person’s work instead of two or three people’s.” But I hear Ken’s voice in my head telling me how great Miranda was, and I’m determinied to prove to him that I’m just as good. And that son-of-a-bitch knows just how to get to me. The really scary thing is, I did this to myself.

我早就预料到会有这样的事发生，但真正面对时还是会感到震惊。我不知道为什么我当时没能说：“我的胳膊开始疼了，我得慢点儿——一个人干完的工作，而不是两三个人干完。”但我脑海里一直回响着肯的声音，他告诉我米兰达有多棒，我决心要向他证明我也一样出色。而那个混蛋，他太了解我的感受了。真正可怕的是，这一切都是我咎由自取。

When we don’t protect our bodies, they signal us with pain until we pay attention. For Kim, repetitive strain injuries mean that there may be crippling consequences for giving in to pressures to work too hard.

如果我们不保护好自己的身体，它就会发出疼痛信号，直到我们重视为止。对金来说，重复性劳损意味着，屈服于工作压力而过度劳累可能会带来严重的后果。

In Kim’s situation, cause and effect were pretty obvious. Too much work, long hours and the pressure to excel exhausted her, and her body rebelled.

金的情况，因果关系显而易见。过多的工作、长时间的工作以及追求卓越的压力让她精疲力竭，最终身体出现了问题。

I certainly don’t go along with the idea that every physical ailment is psychosomatic, but there is ample evidence that the mind, emotions and body are intimately connected. Emotional distress can significantly increase our vulnerability to headaches, muscle spasms, gastrointestinal problems, respiratory disorders and a host of other ailments. I believe strongly that the stress and tension that accompany emotional blackmail may manifest themselves in physical symptoms when other outlets of expression are blocked or shut down.

我当然不认同所有身体疾病都是心因性的这种观点，但有大量证据表明，心理、情绪和身体之间存在着密切的联系。情绪困扰会显著增加我们患头痛、肌肉痉挛、肠胃问题、呼吸系统疾病以及其他诸多疾病的风险。我坚信，当其他表达途径受阻或关闭时，伴随情绪勒索而来的压力和紧张情绪可能会以身体症状的形式表现出来。

BETRAYING OTHERS TO PLACATE THE BLACKMAILER

为了安抚勒索者而背叛他人

We know that capitulation to emotional blackmail causes us to betray ourselves and our integrity. But we tend to overlook the way that, by trying to calm blackmailers or avoid disapproval, we may also be betraying people we care about.

我们知道，向情感勒索屈服会让我们背叛自己和自己的正直。但我们往往忽略了，试图安抚勒索者或避免被责备，也可能是在背叛我们所关心的人。

We’ve seen many examples in this book of how blackmail affects the other people in the target’s life. Josh is betraying Beth by telling his parents he’s not seeing her anymore, and she is deeply hurt. She feels unprotected by him. She also knows that when the time comes, as it always does, and the truth comes out, there will probably be even more uproar than there would have been if he had dealt with the situation in a more courageous way in the first place.

本书中有很多例子说明了勒索如何影响受害者生活中其他人的行为。乔什告诉父母他不再和贝丝来往，这背叛了她，也让贝丝深受伤害。她感觉自己失去了乔什的保护。她也知道，真相总会水落石出，到时候可能会比他一开始就勇敢处理这件事时更加轩然大波。

Karen found herself caught in the middle between her mother and her daughter, faced with having to hurt one or the other.

凯伦发现自己夹在母亲和女儿中间，不得不伤害其中一方。

I had been planning a little party to celebrate Mom’s 75th birthday. When Mom asked who was coming, I ran down the list, but when I got to Melanie she stopped me in my tracks. “I don’t want Melanie there,” she told me. “I know she’s your daughter, but she’s been just terrible to me lately—absolutely disrespectful. The last time I called her, she was too busy to even talk to me. She’s just nice when she wants something.”

我原本计划给妈妈办个小派对，庆祝她75岁生日。妈妈问谁会来，我便开始念名单，但念到梅兰妮的时候，她突然打断了我。“我不想让梅兰妮来，”她告诉我，“我知道她是你的女儿，但她最近对我太差劲了——简直毫无尊重可言。上次我给她打电话，她忙得连话都懒得接。她只有想要什么东西的时候才会对我好。”

I tried to smooth things over and tell her that Melanie has had a lot of things on her mind lately, but Mom wouldn’t hear it. “If you don’t tell Melanie not to come,” she said, “I don’t want your party. You can have it without me. I’ve spent other birthdays by myself, and I can spend this one alone too.” So I had to tell my own daughter that she wasn’t welcome at her grandmother’s party.

我试图缓和气氛，告诉她梅兰妮最近心事重重，但妈妈根本听不进去。“如果你不告诉梅兰妮别来，”她说，“我就不参加你的派对。你可以自己办，不用我。我以前也一个人过过生日，这次也可以。” 所以，我不得不告诉自己的女儿，她不欢迎来参加奶奶的派对。

Karen allowed herself to get pulled into the conflict between her mother and Melanie, and she became the conduit and messenger for all the bad feelings between two adult women. Like most of us, she hadn’t learned any effective strategies for dealing with emotional blackmail, and she assumed that she had only two choices—to give in to her mother and hurt her daughter or to stand fast and risk hurting her mother—a real lose-lose position.

凯伦让自己卷入了母亲和梅兰妮之间的冲突，成了两个成年女性之间所有负面情绪的传声筒和信使。和我们大多数人一样，她没有学会任何有效应对情感勒索的策略，她认为自己只有两个选择——要么向母亲屈服，伤害女儿；要么坚持立场，冒着伤害母亲的风险——真是进退两难。

Many of us have been in an impossible situation like Karen’s, asked to choose between two people we care about, because of a particular blackmailer’s needs. “It’s your kids or me” is a common demand. That was the choice Alex gave Julie when he decided her son was taking too much attention away from him.

我们很多人都曾像凯伦一样陷入进退两难的境地，因为勒索者的需求，被迫在两个自己关心的人之间做出选择。“要么选你的孩子，要么选我”是常见的勒索手段。亚历克斯就曾这样逼迫朱莉，因为他觉得朱莉的儿子抢走了他太多的注意力。

Another familiar scenario may involve various family members who pressure one another to ally with one parent against the other, especially after a divorce. If the divorce has been a bitter one, a typical form of emotional blackmail will be “If you continue to speak to your father/mother you’re out of my life [or my will] and I’ll never speak to you again.” It’s a painful dilemma. Whatever choice the target makes, someone will be betrayed, adding to the already heavy load of guilt and self-reproach.

另一种常见的情况是，家庭成员之间互相施压，要求他们站在父母一方反对另一方，尤其是在离婚之后。如果离婚过程充满怨恨，一种典型的情感勒索方式是：“如果你继续和你的父亲/母亲联系，你就从我的生活中彻底消失（或者说，从我的遗嘱中彻底消失），我永远不会再和你说话。”这是一个痛苦的两难选择。无论被针对者做出何种选择，都会有人感到被背叛，这无疑会加重他们本已沉重的内疚和自责。

THE IMPACT ON THE RELATIONSHIP

对关系的影响

Emotional blackmail sucks the safety out of any relationship. By safety I mean goodwill and trust—the elements that allow us to open ourselves to someone without fear that our innermost thoughts and feelings will be treated with anything but care. Remove those elements and what’s left is a superficial relationship empty of the emotional candor that enables us to be our true selves with another person.

情感勒索会摧毁任何关系中的安全感。我所说的安全感指的是善意和信任——正是这些要素让我们能够向他人敞开心扉，而不必担心自己最深层的想法和感受会遭到冷遇。一旦这些要素消失，剩下的就只是一段肤浅的关系，缺乏情感上的坦诚，也就无法让我们在另一个人面前展现真实的自我。

As the safety level of a relationship drops, we become guarded, hiding more and more from our blackmailers. We stop trusting them to care about how we feel or what’s best for us or even to tell us the truth, knowing that when they’re out to get their way they can be at best insensitive and at worst ruthless. The victim is intimacy.

随着一段关系的安全感下降，我们会变得戒备森严，对勒索者越来越隐瞒。我们不再相信他们会关心我们的感受，不再相信他们会为我们着想，甚至不再相信他们会对我们说实话，因为我们知道，当他们一心想要达到目的时，轻则冷漠无情，重则残忍无情。亲密关系成了受害者。

Shutting Down

关闭

Eve talked about the erosion of intimacy in her relationship with Elliot in an especially poignant way:

伊芙以一种特别感人的方式谈到了她与艾略特之间亲密关系的消逝：

I know he sounds very bizarre and crazy, but it wasn’t always like this. The first year we were together it was a totally different relationship—simple and romantic. He’s bright and incredibly talented and we really loved each other. It was only when I moved in with him that he showed his crazy side.

我知道他听起来很古怪，甚至有点疯狂，但并非一直如此。我们在一起的第一年，关系完全不同——简单而浪漫。他聪明又才华横溢，我们真心相爱。直到我搬去和他同住，他才展现出疯狂的一面。

Now it’s like a pressure chamber. I can’t even describe it. It’s the way you feel for someone you’d been angry at and maybe they get some awful disease, but you love them and deep down care about them. But there’s no intimacy, genuine intimacy. I’m not talking about sexually. I’m talking about emotionally. I can’t tell him my real feelings, because he’s so vulnerable . . . fragile. I can’t tell him my dreams or plans, because he’s so threatened by them. They’re not safe subjects. There’s no real intimacy when you have to watch everything you say.

现在感觉就像身处一个高压舱，我根本无法形容。就像你曾经对某人生气，也许他得了什么重病，但你依然爱他，内心深处依然关心他。然而，我们之间却没有亲密感，真正的亲密感。我说的不是性方面的亲密，而是情感上的亲密。我无法告诉他我的真实感受，因为他太脆弱了……太敏感了。我无法告诉他我的梦想和计划，因为他觉得这些会威胁到他。这些都是不安全的话题。当你说话都要小心翼翼的时候，就谈不上真正的亲密。

Targets of emotional blackmail become so accustomed to negative judgments, disapproval, pressure and overreactions that, like Eve, they are reluctant to share major parts of their lives. We stop talking about:

情感勒索的受害者会逐渐习惯负面评价、不赞同、压力和过度反应，就像夏娃一样，他们不愿分享自己生活中的重要部分。我们不再谈论：

  • Dumb or embarrassing things we did. Our blackmailers might ridicule us.
    我们做过的愚蠢或尴尬的事情。勒索者可能会嘲笑我们。
  • Sad, frightened or insecure feelings. Our blackmailers might use them against us to prove we’re wrong to resist what they want.
    悲伤、恐惧或缺乏安全感。勒索者可能会利用这些情绪来对付我们，证明我们拒绝他们的要求是错误的。
  • Hopes, dreams, plans, goals, fantasies. The blackmailer might shoot them down or use them as proof of how selfish we are.
    希望、梦想、计划、目标、幻想。勒索者可能会粉碎这些幻想，或者用它们来证明我们有多自私。
  • Unhappy life experiences or difficult childhoods. The blackmailer might use them as evidence of our instability or inadequacy.
    不幸的人生经历或艰难的童年。勒索者可能会利用这些经历作为我们精神不稳定或能力不足的证据。
  • Anything that will show we’re changing and evolving. Blackmailers don’t like it when we rock the boat.
    任何能表明我们正在改变和发展的举措。勒索者不喜欢我们打破现状。

What’s left when we must consistently walk on eggs with someone? Superficial small talk, strained silences, lots of tension. Just below the artificial calm that surrounds a placated blackmailer and a target who’s given in is the widening chasm that’s opening between them.

当我们不得不时刻如履薄冰地与人相处时，还剩下什么？肤浅的闲聊、令人窒息的沉默、以及无尽的紧张。在被安抚的勒索者和屈服的受害者之间虚假的平静之下，是一道正在不断扩大的鸿沟。

Karen’s mother resorts to arm-twisting to get Karen to spend more time with her, yet for all the closeness that’s left between them, she’d do just as well to talk to a cardboard cutout of her daughter. The rigid interaction between them has no room for the real Karen or what matters to her. It’s as though there are coils of barbed wire separating these two women, one strand consisting of the mother’s criticism and the other of Karen’s efforts to protect herself by withdrawing.

凯伦的母亲为了让凯伦多陪陪她，不惜使出浑身解数，但即便母女间仅存的些许亲近，她对着女儿的纸板人像说话也无济于事。她们之间僵硬的互动容不下真实的凯伦，也容不下她真正关心的一切。仿佛有两道带刺的铁丝网将这两个女人隔开，一道是母亲的批评，另一道是凯伦为了保护自己而选择退缩。

It’s amazing how much of ourselves we hold back when we’re trying to stave off another blackmail episode. We keep crossing the street conversationally to avoid a serious topic, or worse, a demand. Zoe put it well:

令人惊讶的是，为了避免再次遭遇勒索，我们往往会隐藏自己很多真实的一面。我们总是用言语回避严肃的话题，或者更糟糕的是，回避对方的要求。佐伊说得好：

I don’t even ask Tess how she’s doing anymore because I know she’ll tell me, and then she’ll want me to make it all better for her. I figure we can talk about, oh, the weather, the Dodgers, Mel Gibson, movies—but only comedies. I just keep it light.

我现在都不敢问泰丝过得怎么样了，因为我知道她会告诉我，然后她就会想让我帮她把一切都安排好。我想我们可以聊聊天气、道奇队、梅尔·吉布森、电影——但只能聊喜剧。我尽量让气氛轻松一些。

In a blackmail-tainted situation, relationships with friends, lovers and family members that once had real depth begin to get thinner as the roster of safe topics shrinks.

在充斥着勒索的情况下，与朋友、爱人和家人之间曾经很深厚的关系会随着安全话题的减少而变得疏远。

Allen, the businessman, believed that he had to be careful about what he shared with Jo because of her extreme dependency and overreactiveness.

商人艾伦认为，由于乔极度依赖他人且反应过度，他必须谨慎对待与乔分享的事情。

I can’t tell Jo I’m feeling scared or insecure, because I’m supposed to be the rock of Gibraltar here. But she’s my wife, and I wish I could just share even a little of what I’ve been going through lately. I’m having trouble with my business — sales are way off—and I’ve had to dig into some investments to cover the bills. There’s a small factory in San Jose I want to go take a look at. They’re talking about some new contracts that could be a lifesaver. But I don’t even want to mention making a trip and being gone for a few days. She’ll freak out. And I can’t tell her the truth, because she panics. Hell, this isn’t a real partnership — it’s a one-man band.

我不能告诉乔我感到害怕或缺乏安全感，因为在这里我应该像磐石一样坚强。但她是我妻子，我多么希望能够和她分享哪怕一点点我最近的经历。我的生意遇到了麻烦——销售额大幅下滑——我不得不动用一些投资来支付账单。我想去圣何塞看看一家小工厂。他们正在洽谈一些新合同，这些合同或许能救我一命。但我甚至不想提起要出差几天的事。她会吓坏的。而且我不能告诉她真相，因为她会惊慌失措。唉，这根本就不是真正的合伙关系——完全是我一个人在打拼。

Allen censored himself from talking about the topics he thought Jo “couldn’t handle,” and as a result, even though they lived together, he felt very alone, without the intimacy that comes from being able to share the dark times as well as the bright ones. Their marriage was in an emotional straitjacket.

艾伦刻意回避那些他认为乔“无法承受”的话题，结果，尽管他们住在一起，他却感到非常孤独，无法与乔分享人生中的阴暗时刻和美好时光，从而获得亲密感。他们的婚姻如同被情感的枷锁束缚。

Constricting Emotional Generosity

限制情感慷慨

In one of the great paradoxes of emotional blackmail, the more we feel the blackmailer demanding our time, our attention or our affection, the less we feel free to give. We frequently hold ourselves back from expressing even casual affection because we’re afraid it may be misinterpreted as a sign we’ve given in to their pressure. We turn ourselves into emotional misers, not wanting to feed the blackmailer’s hopes or fantasies.

情感勒索的一大悖论在于：勒索者越是索取我们的时间、关注或情感，我们就越不愿意付出。我们常常克制自己，甚至连最基本的亲昵都不愿表达，因为我们害怕这会被误解为我们屈服于对方压力。我们变得吝啬，不愿助长勒索者的希望或幻想。

Roger, the screenwriter, talked about this paradox early in my work with him, before he and Alice had gotten their relationship onto more solid ground.

编剧罗杰在我与他合作初期就谈到了这个悖论，当时他和爱丽丝的关系还没有稳定下来。

Alice and I have a lot of terrific times together, and I’d really like to be able to tell her that and let her know how much I appreciate her and what a wonderful woman she is in many ways. But I can’t say anything that sounds too loving, because I know she’s going to hear it as a marriage proposal. Or she’ll start on the baby thing again. I’m a very affectionate person, but I find myself holding back a lot—I don’t want to mislead her—and then I feel lousy because I don’t feel free to express myself, and I know that she feels rejected.

我和爱丽丝有很多美好的时光，我真的很想告诉她这些，让她知道我有多感激她，她各方面都是个多么优秀的女人。但我不能说任何听起来太甜言蜜语的话，因为我知道她会听成求婚。或者她又会开始念叨生孩子的事。我其实是个很热情的人，但我发现自己总是忍不住要表达——我不想误导她——然后我又会感觉很糟糕，因为我感觉自己无法自由地表达自己，我知道她会觉得被拒绝。

Roger, at that time in their relationship, didn’t feel free to express his real feelings—even though they were positive—because he knew that whatever he said would wind through the loops and convolutions of Alice’s unrealistic expectations and turn into ammunition for future emotional blackmail.

在他们关系的那个阶段，罗杰不敢自由地表达自己的真实感受——即使是积极的感受——因为他知道，无论他说什么，都会在爱丽丝不切实际的期望中兜兜转转，变成将来情感勒索的把柄。

Often we have to guard our happy feelings as well as our loving ones because there’s no reason for celebration unless you can arrange to be happy on the blackmailer’s terms. Josh obviously can’t share any of his joy with either parent, because his father’s powerful disapproval of Beth has made it unsafe to do so.

我们常常不得不守护自己的快乐和爱人，因为除非你能按照勒索者的条件去享受快乐，否则就没有理由庆祝。显然，乔什无法与父母分享任何喜悦，因为他父亲对贝丝的强烈反对使得这样做变得危险。

“He doesn’t want to hear about it. I’m not supposed to lead my own life. He says he loves me, but how can he?” Josh asked. “He doesn’t even know who I am.”

“他根本不想听这些。我不应该过自己的生活。他说他爱我，但他怎么可能爱我呢？”乔什问道，“他甚至都不知道我是谁。”

The relationship Josh’s father thinks he has with his son doesn’t exist. Obedient Josh doesn’t exist. And what is real—the contentment that Josh has found with Beth—is only allowed to exist outside his father’s knowledge. The relationship between father and son is a sham, and so are many, if not most, of our long-term dealings with emotional blackmailers.

乔什的父亲以为他和儿子之间有那种关系，但这种关系并不存在。听话的乔什也并不存在。而真正存在的——乔什和贝丝在一起的幸福——却只能瞒着他的父亲。父子关系是虚假的，我们与情感勒索者之间许多（如果不是大多数）的长期交往也都是虚假的。

When safety and intimacy are gone from a relationship, we get used to acting. We pretend that we’re happy when we’re not and say that everything is fine when it isn’t. We act as though we’re not really excited about something when we are, and we pantomime loving the people who are pressuring us, even though we hardly know them anymore. What used to be a graceful dance of caring and closeness becomes a masked ball in which the people involved are hiding more and more of their true selves.

当一段关系中失去了安全感和亲密感，我们便习惯了伪装。我们明明不快乐，却假装快乐；明明一切都不好，却说一切都好。我们明明对某件事充满热情，却装作漠不关心；我们甚至会假装爱那些给我们施加压力的人，尽管我们早已对他们知之甚少。曾经充满关爱与亲密的优雅舞蹈，如今却变成了一场假面舞会，参与者们在舞会上不断隐藏着越来越真实的自我。

It is now time to take all this understanding and turn it into action so that you can start to deal effectively with emotional blackmail and the people who are using it against you. You will be amazed at how quickly you can reclaim your integrity—and dramatically improve your relationship with the blackmailer.

现在是时候将这些理解付诸行动了，这样你才能有效地应对情感勒索以及那些利用情感勒索对你的人。你会惊讶地发现，重拾尊严的速度如此之快，而且与勒索者的关系也会得到显著改善。

# ↩

Part II

第二部分

Turning Understanding into Action

将理解转化为行动

Introduction: A Time for Change

引言：变革的时刻

One of my favorite stories is about a man who’s driving down a road when he sees a woman crawling around on her hands and knees under a street lamp. Thinking she must be in trouble, he pulls over.

我最喜欢的故事之一是关于一个男人开车行驶在路上，看到一个女人在路灯下手脚并用地爬行。他以为她一定遇到了麻烦，于是把车停在了路边。

“What’s going on?” he asks. “You look like you could use some help.”

“怎么了？”他问。“你看上去需要帮助。”

“Thanks,” she replies. “I’m looking for my keys.”

“谢谢，”她回答说，“我正在找钥匙。”

After they search for awhile he asks, “Do you have any idea where you dropped them?”

他们找了一会儿后，他问道：“你们知道你们把它们丢在哪里了吗？”

“Oh, yes,” she replies. “I lost them about a mile down the road.”

“哦，是的，”她回答说。“我在大约一英里外的路上把他们跟丢了。”

Understandably baffled, he asks, “Then why are we looking here?”

他显然感到困惑，问道：“那我们为什么要在这里寻找呢？”

And she answers, “Because it’s familiar territory and the light’s better.”

她回答说：“因为这里是熟悉的地方，而且光线更好。”

A lot of us think we can solve our problems with emotional blackmail by sorting through a repertoire of familiar behavior to find an escape. We accept the blackmailers’ accusations, buy their blame, apologize and ultimately comply. There’s a certain logic to this—we know how to do it, and compliance brings immediate relief. But if we stick to our accustomed ways of responding, we’ll never lay hands on the real keys to ending emotional blackmail. They’re a mile down the road, in the self-affirming, nondefensive behaviors I will teach you in this part of the book.

我们很多人都以为，只要套用一套熟悉的应对方式，就能摆脱情感勒索的困扰。我们接受勒索者的指责，相信他们的所作所为，道歉，最终屈服。这似乎合情合理——我们知道该怎么做，而且屈服能带来立竿见影的解脱。但如果我们固守成规的应对方式，就永远无法真正掌握终结情感勒索的秘诀。其实，秘诀就在不远处，就在我将在本书这一部分教你的那些自我肯定、不设防的行为之中。

It’s vital to move from the comfortable, well-lighted arena of habitual responses into the far more uncomfortable sphere of behavioral change. By now you have a good understanding of how and why you’re being blackmailed, but knowledge is utterly useless if it doesn’t become a catalyst that moves you to do what it takes to end the blackmail. Change requires using information, not just collecting it. To change, we have to know what we need to do and then we have to act. Yet for many reasons, most of us resist this step with every fiber of our being. We’re afraid we’ll try and fail. We’re afraid we’ll lose the good parts of our relationships when we try to get rid of the bad. We, who are good at so many things in our lives, often resist changing self-defeating behavior patterns with exquisitely wrought reasons why we can’t do anything different.

从舒适安逸、习以为常的应对方式，迈入截然不同、令人不适的行为改变领域，至关重要。如今，你或许已经对被勒索的方式和原因有了清晰的认识，但如果这些知识不能成为促使你采取行动、终结勒索的催化剂，那么它们就毫无用处。改变需要运用信息，而不仅仅是收集信息。要改变，我们必须知道自己需要做什么，然后付诸行动。然而，出于种种原因，我们大多数人都在竭力抗拒这一步。我们害怕尝试后失败。我们害怕在试图摆脱不良习惯的同时，也会失去人际关系中美好的部分。我们这些在生活中擅长诸多事情的人，常常会用精心编造的理由来逃避改变那些自我挫败的行为模式，声称自己无能为力。

So we wait to learn new behavior until we feel a little less anxious, a bit less afraid or insecure. And the blackmail gets worse. The good news is that if you’re willing to take action now and let your feelings of confidence and competence catch up with you, you can end emotional blackmail. The bad news is that you have to begin the change process while you are still afraid.

所以，我们总是等到焦虑、恐惧或不安全感减轻一些才去学习新的行为模式。而这种情感勒索只会愈演愈烈。好消息是，如果你现在就愿意采取行动，让自己的自信和能力感逐渐增强，你就能摆脱这种情感勒索。坏消息是，你必须在仍然感到恐惧的时候就开始改变。

STEP BY STEP

步步

If you want to deal effectively with a blackmailer, you have to learn some very different responses and communication skills. The words that come out of your mouth have to change, be replaced by a new style of response and expression. The emotional tone surrounding your responses has to be different. You have to interrupt the ritualistic pattern of resistance, pressure and capitulation by changing the reactions that have kept you on automatic pilot.

如果你想有效应对勒索者，就必须学习一些截然不同的应对方式和沟通技巧。你脱口而出的话语必须改变，取而代之的是全新的回应和表达方式。你回应时的情绪基调也必须有所不同。你必须打破那种机械式的抵抗、施压和屈服的模式，改变那些让你一直处于自动反应状态的惯性思维。

In this portion of the book, I’ll walk you through a process I’ve designed to take you step by step from where you are now to the point where you can respond in a new way the next time someone tries to blackmail you. I’ll teach you powerful nondefensive communications skills and guide you through visualizations, checklists and writing exercises that can quickly bring change on many levels.

在本书的这一部分，我将引导你逐步完成我设计的一套流程，帮助你从目前的状况过渡到下次有人试图勒索你时，能够以全新的方式应对。我将教你强有力的非防御性沟通技巧，并通过可视化练习、清单和写作练习指导你，这些练习能够迅速在多个层面带来改变。

We’ll be proceeding along two tracks. The first, which you can start to use almost immediately, is the behavioral track. At first you may feel as though you haven’t changed at all inside—it’s quite likely that you’ll still feel guilty or obligated or afraid when a blackmailer turns up the pressure. But you will learn to act more effectively, and once you change your behavior, the relationship must change as well. The results you’ll see will embolden and encourage you.

我们将从两个方面着手。第一方面是行为层面，你可以几乎立即开始运用。起初，你可能会感觉内心没有任何改变——当勒索者加大压力时，你很可能仍然会感到内疚、愧疚或害怕。但你会学会更有效地应对，一旦你改变了自己的行为，双方的关系也必然随之改变。你所看到的成果会激励你，让你更加勇敢。

At the same time, we’ll work together on the emotional track, which will take you through the somewhat longer process of changing your inner world, disconnecting old hot buttons as well as doing some work on the wounds and erroneous belief systems that have made you vulnerable to emotional blackmail.

与此同时，我们将共同努力，从情感层面入手，这将带你经历一个稍长的过程，改变你的内心世界，消除旧的敏感点，并处理那些使你容易受到情感勒索的创伤和错误的信念体系。

It may sound odd for someone who’s been a therapist for 25 years to tell you this, but you can do a lot of this work successfully on your own. Obviously, if there is abuse in the relationship or if you are suffering from deep depression, unmanageable anxiety, extreme degrees of self-hatred or a dramatic lack of confidence, there are wonderful resources for you to take advantage of, and this book can serve as an important adjunct to one-on-one or group therapy, 12-Step programs or personal growth seminars. In most cases, though, all you’ll need is courage and determination.

或许你会觉得，一个从业25年的心理治疗师说出这样的话有些奇怪，但很多事情你完全可以靠自己成功完成。当然，如果你的感情关系中存在虐待，或者你正遭受严重的抑郁、难以控制的焦虑、极度的自我厌恶或极度缺乏自信的困扰，那么有很多优秀的资源可以帮助你。本书可以作为一对一或团体治疗、十二步互助小组或个人成长研讨会的重要辅助材料。但在大多数情况下，你需要的仅仅是勇气和决心。

In the past, you have behaved in automatic, predictable ways when faced with emotional blackmail. You’ve argued, tried to explain your position, offered up some active or passive resistance and ultimately given in. Now it’s time to replace that way of behaving with a far more self-respectful, efficient and empowering set of techniques. With practice—the willingness to keep using these techniques until they become comfortable for you—you will put an end to blackmail.

过去，面对情感勒索，你的反应总是机械而可预测。你会争辩，试图解释自己的立场，进行一些主动或被动的抵抗，最终还是屈服了。现在，是时候用一套更尊重自己、更高效、更能增强自身力量的技巧来取代这种行为模式了。通过练习——坚持不懈地运用这些技巧，直到你能够自如运用——你就能彻底摆脱勒索的困扰。

As you’re exploring the chapters that follow, you’re likely to face blackmail situations that will give you an immediate opportunity to apply what you’re learning as you learn it. Jump in and take your new skills off the page and into your life. I promise you that when you see yourself begin to deal in a more conscious way with blackmailers’ pressure, you’ll notice a dramatic improvement in the way you feel about yourself.

在接下来的章节中，你很可能会遇到勒索情境，这将为你提供立即运用所学知识的机会。大胆尝试，将新技能从书本运用到生活中。我保证，当你开始更有意识地应对勒索者的压力时，你会明显感受到自我价值的提升。

Once you are less afraid and feel less manipulated by fear, obligation and guilt, you’ll notice how many choices open up to you. You’ll be able to decide who you want to be close to, how much you are responsible for other people, how you really want to use your time and love and energy.

一旦你不再那么害怕，不再受恐惧、责任和内疚的摆布，你就会发现有多少选择摆在你面前。你将能够决定你想和谁亲近，你对他人负有多少责任，以及你真正想如何支配你的时间、爱和精力。

Please be patient with yourself, and be persistent. Some of you may start this work feeling that your self-respect and integrity have been so profoundly violated that they are lost to you forever, but I urge you to use the word misplaced instead of lost —and then look to new behavior to help you find them. Together, we’ll do the work of rediscovering and rebuilding what emotional blackmail has worn away inside you and in your relationships with blackmailers. I applaud you for taking concrete steps to eliminate emotional blackmail from your life.

请对自己保持耐心，并坚持不懈。你们中的一些人或许会觉得，自己的自尊和正直受到了如此严重的践踏，以至于永远失去了它们。但我恳请你们用“错位”而非“失去”来形容——然后尝试用新的行为方式来找回它们。我们将共同努力，重新发现并重建那些被情感勒索侵蚀的自我，以及它们在你与勒索者的关系中所造成的伤害。我赞赏你们采取切实行动，将情感勒索从生活中彻底清除。

# ↩

8

Before You Get Started

开始之前

You’ve probably heard the joke about the tourist in New York who stops a man with a violin under his arm and asks for directions to Carnegie Hall. “You want to know how to get Carnegie Hall?” replies the violinist. “Practice, practice, practice.”

你可能听过这样一个笑话：一个游客在纽约拦住一个胳膊下夹着小提琴的男人，问他卡内基音乐厅怎么走。“你想知道怎么去卡内基音乐厅？”小提琴手回答说，“练习，练习，再练习。”

We all know those familiar directions, and most of us are able to recognize the relationship between practice and mastery in many aspects of life. You probably remember wobbling toward steadiness on a bicycle or awkwardly moving your fingers on a keyboard while learning to type.

我们都熟悉这些道理，而且大多数人都能认识到练习与精通在生活诸多方面的重要性。你可能还记得骑自行车时摇摇晃晃地摸索着前进，或者学习打字时笨拙地在键盘上移动手指。

But when it comes to making important changes in our lives, we often expect results overnight. The unavoidable truth is that learning new skills takes practice, and it may be awhile before you’re comfortable using them. Just as we have to walk around in a new pair of shoes before they really fit, we have to break in new behavior. You probably won’t see immediate changes in your life the first day you make the commitment to free yourself from emotional blackmail—but you will see them soon. Remember, commitment is a promise to yourself, and it’s one well worth keeping.

但当我们想要在生活中做出重大改变时，往往期望一夜之间就能见效。然而，事实是，学习新技能需要练习，而且可能需要一段时间才能熟练运用。就像新鞋需要一段时间才能真正合脚一样，新的行为也需要磨合。你或许不会在下定决心摆脱情感勒索的第一天就看到立竿见影的变化，但你很快就会看到改变。记住，承诺是对自己许下的诺言，而且绝对值得信守。

THE FIRST STEP

第一步

Before you think about dealing with the blackmailer, there are some things you need to do yourself. Every day for the next week, I’d like you to set aside some private time to work with three very simple tools: a contract, a power statement and a set of self-affirming phrases. You’ll need as little as 15 minutes a day. I’d like you to take the phone off the hook, remove yourself from interruptions and focus on you. Some people have found that the only private time they have is in the bathtub, in the car or at their desk during lunch. That’s fine. You can do this work anywhere.

在你考虑如何应对勒索者之前，你需要先做一些事情。接下来的一周，我希望你每天都能抽出一些独处的时间，使用三个非常简单的工具：一份合同、一份强有力的宣言和一套自我肯定的短语。你每天只需要15分钟。我希望你把电话线拔掉，避免任何干扰，专注于自己。有些人发现他们唯一能拥有的独处时间是在浴缸里、车里或者午休时间。没关系。你可以在任何地方完成这项工作。

The first thing I’d like you to do is sign a contract that lists a number of promises I’d like you to make to yourself—ground rules for this process. You may have serious doubts at this point about your ability to keep promises like these, especially if you’ve tried unsuccessfully in the past to stop giving in to emotional blackmail. I’d like you to put the past aside right now and begin to take a new set of steps based on new understanding and new skills.

首先，我希望你签署一份合同，其中列出了我希望你对自己做出的几项承诺——这是整个过程的基本规则。此时此刻，你或许会对自己能否信守这些承诺深感怀疑，尤其如果你过去曾尝试摆脱情感勒索却以失败告终。我希望你现在就放下过去，基于新的认知和技能，开始采取一系列新的行动。

This contract is a powerful symbol that puts your willingness to change into tangible form and helps clarify your goals.

这份合同是一个强有力的象征，它将你改变的意愿转化为切实可见的形式，并有助于明确你的目标。

Some people find that they get the best results from handwriting this contract on a sheet of paper. You may also want to write it on the first page of a notebook you devote specifically to the exercises I’ll be teaching you. If you want to record your observations and feelings as we go, please do.

有些人发现，用手写的方式把这份合同写在纸上效果最好。你也可以把它写在你专门用来记录我接下来要教你的练习的笔记本的第一页上。如果你想在练习过程中记录你的观察和感受，请随意。

Whether you recopy the contract or simply sign it in the book, please read it aloud to yourself every day this week.

无论你是重新抄写合同还是直接在合同本上签字，请在本周每天大声朗读一遍。

Second, I’d like you to learn and practice saying a power statement, one short sentence that you can use to keep yourself grounded when blackmailers turn up the pressure.

其次，我希望你们学习并练习说一句强有力的宣言，一句简短的句子，当勒索者加大压力时，你可以用它来让自己保持冷静。

Power statement: I CAN STAND IT.

力量宣言：我能忍受。

Those four words may look insignificant, but used correctly, they can become one of your most potent weapons for resisting emotional blackmail. They’re effective because they counter a belief that ushers us straight in to saying yes to our blackmailers: the idea that we can’t stand the pressure.

这四个字看似微不足道，但如果运用得当，却能成为你抵御情感勒索的最有力武器之一。它们之所以有效，是因为它们能反驳一种让我们轻易答应勒索者的信念：我们无法承受压力。

CONTRACT WITH MYSELF

与自己签订的合同

I,______________, recognize myself as an adult with options and choices, and I commit myself to the process of actively getting emotional blackmail out of my relationships and out of my life. In order to reach that goal, I make the following promises:

我，____，认识到自己是一个拥有选择权和权力的成年人，并承诺积极主动地从我的人际关系和生活中消除情感勒索。为了实现这一目标，我做出以下承诺：

  • I promise myself that I am no longer willing to let fear, obligation and guilt control my decisions.
    我向自己承诺，我不再让恐惧、责任和内疚控制我的决定。
  • I promise myself that I will learn the strategies in this book and that I will put them into practice in my life.
    我向自己承诺，我会学习这本书中的策略，并将它们运用到我的生活中。
  • I promise myself that if I regress, fail or fall into old patterns, I will not use slips as an excuse to stop trying. I recognize that failure is not failure if you use it as a way to learn.
    我向自己承诺，即使我退步、失败或重蹈覆辙，我也不会以此为借口放弃尝试。我明白，如果能把失败当作学习的机会，那么失败就不是真正的失败。
  • I promise to take good care of myself during this process.
    我保证在此过程中会好好照顾自己。
  • I promise that I will acknowledge myself for taking positive steps, no matter how small they are.
    我承诺，无论采取的积极措施多么微小，我都会认可自己的努力。

_____________ Signature

____ 签名

_____________ Date

____ 日期

  • “I can’t stand to hurt his feelings.”
    “我舍不得伤害他的感情。”
  • “I can’t stand it when she says things like that to me.”
    “我最受不了她跟我说那种话。”
  • “I can’t stand my guilt!”
    “我无法忍受我的罪恶感！”
  • “I can’t stand my anxiety.”
    “我无法忍受我的焦虑。”
  • “I can’t stand it when she cries.”
    “我受不了她哭。”
  • “I can’t stand his anger.”
    “我受不了他的怒气。”

We are constantly making statements like these to ourselves, and if you truly believe you can’t stand it—whether you’re referring to a blackmailer’s tears, a red-faced shout or a “gentle” reminder of how much you owe someone—you’ll only be able to see one course of action. You’ll have to back down, give in, go along, keep the peace. This belief is the fundamental trap that undermines blackmail targets. We’ve made “I can’t stand it” our mantra, and in effect, we’ve brainwashed ourselves. Though you may not believe me now, you are a lot stronger than you think. You can stand the pressure, and your first step is to replace any belief that tells you otherwise.

我们常常这样对自己说，如果你真的无法忍受——无论是勒索者的眼泪、涨红的叫喊，还是“温和地”提醒你欠了多少钱——你只会想到一种应对方式：退让、妥协、顺从，维持表面的和平。这种想法正是勒索受害者最根本的陷阱。我们把“我无法忍受”奉为口头禅，实际上，我们已经给自己洗脑了。虽然你现在可能不相信，但你比你想象的要坚强得多。你能承受压力，而你的第一步就是摒弃任何让你产生相反想法的观念。

Repeating “I CAN stand it” will begin putting a new message into your conscious and unconscious mind. For this week, every time you think about taking steps to eliminate blackmail and start to get frightened, upset or discouraged, stop and repeat this statement to yourself. Breathe deeply, exhale completely and say, “I can stand it.” Do this at least 10 times.

反复默念“我能忍受”，就能将新的信息植入你的意识和潜意识。本周，每当你想要采取措施消除勒索，并开始感到害怕、沮丧或气馁时，停下来，对自己重复这句话。深呼吸，完全呼气，然后说：“我能忍受。”至少重复10次。

I suggest practicing by imagining yourself face-to-face with a blackmailer who’s in the midst of pressuring you. Have you seen the clear acrylic shields that riot police sometimes use? Let “I can stand it” be a shield that comes between you and the blackmailer’s words and nonverbal expressions. Say the power statement aloud as you practice. You may be timid with it at first, and not very convincing, but stay with it. You’ll start to believe yourself. Is this process mechanical? Yes. Does it feel foreign? Yes, it might. But remember that your old responses have not worked. I assure you that repeating “I can stand it” to yourself does work.

我建议你练习时想象自己正与一个勒索者面对面，他正在向你施压。你见过防暴警察有时使用的透明亚克力盾牌吗？让“我能承受”这句话成为你与勒索者的言语和非语言表达之间的屏障。练习时，大声说出这句话。一开始你可能会有些怯懦，也不太有说服力，但请坚持下去。你会开始相信自己。这个过程很机械吗？是的。感觉很陌生吗？是的，也许会。但请记住，你过去的应对方式并没有奏效。我向你保证，反复对自己说“我能承受”是有效的。

REVERSING THE BEHAVIORS OF COMPLIANCE

扭转顺从行为

Now, using the same basic concept of replacing old beliefs with new ones, I’d like to help you develop a set of self-affirming phrases that will calm you, make you feel stronger and embolden you to act. First, let’s take a look at a set of statements that describe the typical feelings and behavior of emotional blackmail targets toward their blackmailers. Most, or even all, of the statements may be true for you—not in all your relationships, certainly, but when you face blackmail. Check all that apply.

现在，运用用新信念取代旧信念的基本概念，我想帮助你建立一套自我肯定的语句，这些语句可以让你平静下来，增强你的力量，并鼓励你采取行动。首先，我们来看一些描述情感勒索受害者对勒索者典型感受和行为的陈述。其中大部分甚至全部陈述可能都适用于你——当然，并非适用于你所有的人际关系，但当你面临勒索时，这些陈述就适用。请勾选所有适用的选项。

When dealing with emotional blackmailers:

应对情感勒索者时：

__I tell myself that giving in is no big deal.

我告诉自己，妥协没什么大不了的。

__I tell myself that giving in is worth it if it gets the other person to shut up.

我告诉自己，如果让步能让对方闭嘴，那也是值得的。

__I tell myself that what I want is wrong.

我告诉自己，我想要的东西是错的。

__I tell myself it’s not worth the battle.

我告诉自己，这场仗不值得打。

__I give in now because I’ll take a stand later.

我现在妥协，因为我以后会表明立场。

__I tell myself it’s better to give in than to hurt their feelings.

我告诉自己，与其伤害他们的感情，不如妥协。

__I don’t stand up for myself.

我不会为自己挺身而出。

__I give away my power.

我放弃我的权力。

__I do things to please other people and get confused about what I want.

我总是为了取悦别人而做事，却搞不清楚自己真正想要的是什么。

__I acquiesce.

我同意。

__I give up people and activities that I care about to please the blackmailer.

为了取悦勒索者，我放弃了我在乎的人和事。

These statements sound pretty feeble, don’t they? But don’t be embarrassed. Until a few years ago, most of the statements would have been true for me, too, in certain relationships—and they’re true for many people. Emotional blackmail is very prevalent, and we’re all in this together. Pay attention to how the statements you’ve checked make you feel, and use the following list to help you pinpoint the full range of feelings that go along with this behavior. Circle the words that apply to you, and add any other feelings you’re aware of that I haven’t listed.

这些说法听起来很苍白无力，对吧？但别觉得难为情。几年前，在某些关系中，这些说法对我来说也同样适用——而且对很多人来说也是如此。情感勒索非常普遍，我们都身处其中。注意一下你勾选的这些说法会让你有什么感受，并参考下面的列表来帮助你准确地找出伴随这种行为而来的各种感受。圈出符合你情况的词语，并添加任何你意识到的、我没有列出的其他感受。

How do I feel when I act this way?

当我这样做的时候，我感觉如何？

Embarrassed

尴尬的

Hurt

伤害

Ashamed

羞愧

Angry

生气的

Weak

虚弱的

Depressed

郁闷

Frustrated

沮丧的

Emotionally numb

情感麻木

Sad

伤心

Powerless

无力

Self-pitying

自怜

Helpless

无助

殉道者

Agitated

激动

不满

Victimized

受害人

If you circled angry, I wouldn’t be surprised if you were angry at yourself, and even angry at me for reminding you of certain aspects of your behavior that you’d rather forget. Use this discomfort—it’s letting you know what aspects of your behavior need attention.

如果你圈出了“生气”这个词，我不会惊讶于你是在生自己的气，甚至会生我的气，因为我提醒了你一些你宁愿忘记的行为。利用这种不适感——它让你意识到你的哪些行为需要改进。

Now take your original list of statements, and change each item you’ve checked to its opposite. For example:

现在，请将你最初的陈述列表，把每一项你勾选的内容都替换成它的相反项。例如：

Old: “I tell myself that what I want is wrong.”

老者：“我告诉自己，我想要的东西是错的。”

New: “I ask for what I want, even when it upsets the blackmailer.”

新内容：“我会提出我的要求，即使这会让勒索者不高兴。”

Old: “I give in now because I’ll take a stand later.”

老先生：“我现在妥协，因为我以后会表明立场。”

New: “I hold my ground and take a stand now.”

新：“我坚持立场，表明我的立场。”

Old: “I do things to please other people and get confused about what I want.”

老先生：“我总是为了取悦别人而做事，却搞不清楚自己想要什么。”

New: “I do things to please myself as well as others, and I am clear about what I want.”

新：“我做事既是为了取悦自己，也是为了取悦他人，而且我很清楚自己想要什么。”

You can also put your original behavior statements in the past tense by saying, “I used to [statement], but I don’t do that anymore.” For example: “I used to tell myself that what I want is wrong, but I don’t do that anymore.”

你也可以用过去时态来描述你之前的行为，比如：“我以前会[陈述]，但我现在不会了。” 例如：“我以前会告诉自己，我想要的东西是错的，但我现在不会了。”
