Try both approaches and see which feels best to you. Then repeat these new positive statements aloud as if they described you. I know they’re not true right now, but they’ll give you a sense of what it will feel like to be free of behavior that’s driven by fear, obligation and guilt. Putting these statements in the past tense or restating them in a positive way helps drain power from them and return it to you. Some of my clients have found this exercise to be especially effective when they repeat the positive statements to themselves while looking themselves in the eye in a mirror. It will give you a chance to literally see yourself describing your actions in an affirmative way.

两种方法都试试，看看哪种感觉更适合你。然后大声重复这些新的积极陈述，就好像它们在描述你自己一样。我知道它们现在可能并不真实，但它们能让你体会到摆脱恐惧、责任和内疚驱使的行为会是什么感觉。用过去式或积极的方式重述这些陈述，有助于削弱它们的力量，并将力量还给你。我的一些客户发现，当他们对着镜子看着自己的眼睛重复这些积极陈述时，这个练习尤其有效。这能让你有机会真切地看到自己用肯定的方式描述自己的行为。

Think about how you would feel if you were to act in this new way. Use the following list to help you describe those feelings.

想想如果你以这种新的方式行事，你会有什么感受。请参考以下列表来描述这些感受。

Strong

强的

Elated

欣喜若狂

Self-affirming

自我肯定

Proud

自豪的

Triumphant

凯

Powerful

强大的

Confident

自信的

Excited

兴奋的

Capable

有能力的

Courageous

勇敢

Hopeful

充满希望

These adjectives will help you visualize yourself dealing confidently with blackmail. Change starts with a vision, and it’s important to give yourself a clear mental picture of what you are trying to achieve. Then, as we work, you can energize your vision with action and move steadily toward your goal. You may want to write or repeat a statement that expresses this vision—“I stand up to emotional blackmail and feel strong, confident, proud and elated.”

这些形容词能帮助你想象自己自信地应对勒索的场景。改变始于愿景，因此，清晰地描绘出你想要达成的目标至关重要。然后，在我们共同努力的过程中，你可以将愿景转化为行动，并稳步朝着目标迈进。你可以写下或重复一句表达这种愿景的话——“我勇敢地对抗情感勒索，我感到强大、自信、自豪和振奋。”

Please go through these lists every day for a week as you mentally review your recent and past interactions with emotional blackmailers, and each time you do, jot down five or six feelings that come up for you. You’ll probably notice that your feelings change over time, and you may find that it becomes harder for you to repeat the negative statements and easier to imagine yourself resisting blackmail.

请在接下来的一周里，每天回顾这些清单，反思你最近和过去与情感勒索者的互动，每次回顾时，记下五六种涌上心头的感受。你可能会注意到，随着时间的推移，你的感受会发生变化，你会发现自己越来越难以重复那些负面的话语，也更容易想象自己能够抵制勒索。

After a week of working by yourself with these three exercises, you should be feeling more centered and ready to start dealing directly with your current situation. Let yourself take the time to do the preparatory exercises, no matter how eager you are to get going. You have plenty of time—neither your blackmailer nor the blackmail is going anywhere.

独自完成这三项练习一周后，你应该会感到更加平静，并准备好直接应对目前的困境。无论你多么渴望立即行动，都请给自己时间完成这些准备练习。你时间充裕——勒索者和勒索行为都不会消失。

SENDING UP AN SOS

发出求救信号

I’d like to give you a game plan, starting with the first steps to take before responding to a blackmailer’s demands. It’s easy to remember, and stripped down to the essentials it’s When you feel as though you’re sinking under the pressure of emotional blackmail, send up an SOS.

我想给你制定一个应对方案，首先从回应勒索者的要求之前应该采取的第一步开始。这个方案简单易记，而且直击要点。当你感觉自己快要被情感勒索压垮时，发出求救信号。

You don’t need know Morse code or wave flags around. Just remember this convenient shorthand for the first three steps in the change process. SOS: Stop. Observe. Strategize. We’ll cover the first two steps in this chapter and explore tools and strategies in the following chapter. Don’t skip any steps—building your strategies on a strong foundation is essential.

你不需要懂摩尔斯电码，也不需要挥舞旗帜。只需记住变革流程前三个步骤的便捷缩写：SOS：停止（Stop）、观察（Observe）、制定策略（Strategize）。本章将介绍前两个步骤，下一章将探讨相关工具和策略。切勿跳过任何步骤——建立在坚实基础上的策略至关重要。

STEP ONE: STOP

第一步：停止

Patty was a little bewildered when I told her that the first thing any target of emotional blackmail has to do is nothing. That means you don’t make a decision about how to respond the moment a demand is made. This sounds easy, but it can be challenging—especially when the pressure to give an answer feels intense—so it’s important to brace yourself and prepare.

当我告诉帕蒂，任何情感勒索的受害者首先要做的就是什么都不做时，她有点困惑。这意味着你不能在对方提出要求的那一刻就决定如何回应。这听起来容易，但做起来却很难——尤其是在你感到必须给出答复的压力很大的时候——所以做好心理准备非常重要。

You’ll feel awkward at first. That’s OK. Feel awkward—and keep going.

一开始你会觉得尴尬。没关系。尴尬就好——然后继续。

How do you do nothing? Well, the first thing you need to do is give yourself time to think—away from the pressure. To do this, you’ll need to learn some time-buying phrases that will slow things down. Below, I’ve listed some suggestions for your first response to whatever the demand happens to be:

如何做到什么都不做？首先，你需要给自己一些时间思考——远离压力。为此，你需要学习一些能拖延时间的短语，让事情慢下来。下面，我列出了一些建议，供你应对各种需求时的第一反应：

  • I don’t have an answer for you right now. I need some time to think.
    我现在没法给你答案，我需要时间考虑一下。
  • This is too important to decide quickly. Let me think about it.
    这件事太重要了，不能仓促决定。让我考虑一下。
  • I’m not willing to make a decision right now.
    我现在不打算做决定。
  • I’m not sure how I feel about what you’re asking. Let’s discuss this a little later.
    我不太确定该如何看待你提出的问题。我们稍后再讨论吧。

Use time-buying statements as soon as a demand is made, and continue to repeat them if the blackmailer pressures you to make an immediate decision. How much time should you ask for? Obviously, the higher the stakes and the more the profound the issue, the more time you need. You can make a quick decision about where to spend a vacation or whether to buy a computer, and even if your choice isn’t great, not that much is lost. But when it comes to such major life issues as the fate of a marriage, children or changing jobs, you should be prepared to take as much time as you need to think things through.

一旦对方提出要求，就立即使用争取时间的说辞，如果对方施压要求你立即做决定，就反复使用这些说辞。你应该争取多少时间？显然，事关重大，风险越高，你需要的时间就越多。你可以很快决定去哪里度假，或者是否购买电脑，即使你的选择并不理想，也不会造成太大损失。但是，当涉及到婚姻、子女或换工作等重大人生抉择时，你应该做好准备，花足够的时间仔细考虑。

As part of our learning process with this book, when a blackmailer pressures you about something that falls outside the “major issue” category, let him or her know you want at least 24 hours to make a decision. You’ll be using the time you’ve bought for yourself to make a decision and prepare to stand behind it.

作为本书学习过程的一部分，当勒索者就一些并非“重大问题”的事情向你施压时，请告知对方你需要至少24小时的时间来做决定。你要利用这段时间做出决定，并做好承担后果的准备。

Your Timetable or Theirs

你的时间表还是他们的时间表

What makes emotional blackmail unique is the sense of a clock constantly ticking in the background. There’s a request on the table, and at some point you need to respond. A lot of the blackmailer’s pressure comes from the idea that there’s no time to lose. It’s the same illusion that makes thrillers and suspense films so effective—the story is set up as a race against time. We get caught up in that drama and don’t bother to question whether it’s real. If you do step back, you’ll see that in the vast majority of cases there is no urgency, except in the mind of the blackmailer.

情感勒索的独特之处在于，它营造了一种时间紧迫感。对方提出了要求，你必须在某个时刻做出回应。勒索者施加的压力很大程度上来自于“时间紧迫”的观念。这种错觉正是惊悚片和悬疑片如此引人入胜的原因——故事被设定为一场与时间赛跑的较量。我们沉浸于这种戏剧化的氛围中，却懒得去质疑它的真实性。如果你冷静下来仔细想想，就会发现，绝大多数情况下，除了勒索者自己臆想的之外，根本不存在什么紧迫感。

When you step uncritically into the “act now, last chance” universe, which is where almost all blackmail is set, the pressure is on. Time-buying statements allow you to turn off the sound of the ticking clock and view this drama from the outside. Maybe the sale on cars or computers only lasts until Sunday—but there will be another sale. Maybe the blackmailer does have an important deadline—but it’s not your deadline.

当你不加批判地踏入“立即行动，最后机会”的世界——几乎所有的勒索都发生在这个世界里——压力就随之而来。拖延时间的言论让你暂时忘却时间的紧迫，以旁观者的身份审视这场闹剧。也许汽车或电脑的促销活动只持续到周日——但肯定还会有下一次。也许勒索者确实有一个重要的截止日期——但那不是你的截止日期。

You have something the blackmailer wants. Time is on your side. When you use a time-buying statement, all you want is time to think—something almost any reasonable person would be willing to give you. But some blackmailers will even use blackmail to get you to back down from your time-buying. That was one of Patty’s concerns.

你拥有勒索者想要的东西。时间站在你这边。当你提出争取时间的策略时，你想要的仅仅是思考的时间——几乎所有通情达理的人都愿意给你时间。但有些勒索者甚至会用勒索来让你放弃争取时间的策略。这正是帕蒂的担忧之一。

“This is all fine,” she told me as we practiced the time-buying statements. “But you just don’t know Joe. As soon as I tell him I want time to think, he’ll start pouting, and then he’ll say, ‘You know the sale ends this week. It’s not like we have all the time in the world. What’s the problem?”’

“这都没问题，”我们练习争取时间的说辞时，她对我说。“但你根本不了解乔。我一跟他说我想考虑一下，他就开始撅嘴，然后说，‘你知道促销活动这周就结束了。我们又不是有的是时间。有什么问题吗？’”

“And what will you say?” I asked.

“那你又会说什么呢？”我问道。

“I’ll try something like, ‘I’m not willing to make a decision right now,’ but I know that’s going to go in one ear and out the other. He’s going to be like a kid—‘How long will it take? How long will it take?”’

“我会试着说，‘我现在不想做决定’，但我知道他肯定左耳进右耳出。他会像个孩子一样问——‘还要多久？还要多久？’”

“And you’ll keep repeating, ‘It’ll take as long as it takes,”’ I told her. The blackmailer may resent you for wanting time, pout or use other forms of pressure, but the power of repetition is generally enough to deliver the message that you’re serious.

“你要一直重复‘需要多久就多久’，”我告诉她。勒索者可能会因为你想要时间而心生不满，或者耍脾气，或者用其他方式施压，但重复的力量通常足以传达你是认真的。

A New Dance

一种新的舞蹈

These time-buying statements may confuse or upset the blackmailer. After all, you’re changing the usual and expected scenario by not automatically giving in. It’s almost as though the two of you had been doing a tango when all of a sudden you began to waltz. The blackmailer may experience your slowdown as resistance or a negative answer, and as a result may start pressuring you immediately. The result can be, and often is, chaos. Just by saying “I need time,” you’ve shifted the balance of power in the relationship and put the blackmailer in the position of waiting to see what you’re going to do—a reactive, and for them a much less powerful, role.

这些争取时间的言论可能会让勒索者感到困惑或恼火。毕竟，你没有立即妥协，改变了以往的惯例和预期。这就像你们原本在跳探戈，突然间你转而跳起了华尔兹。勒索者可能会将你的放慢节奏视为抵抗或否定的回应，并因此立即开始向你施压。结果往往是混乱，而且通常确实如此。仅仅一句“我需要时间”，你就改变了你们关系中的权力平衡，让勒索者处于被动等待你下一步行动的位置——对他们来说，这是一个远不如主动权强大的角色。

Be prepared for even more pressure as blackmailers try to regain their position. As they stick to their by now familiar script, stick to your new set of responses and mentally repeat “I can stand it.”

勒索者会试图重新夺回控制权，所以要做好承受更大压力的准备。当他们继续使用他们早已熟悉的套路时，你也坚持使用新的应对策略，并在心里默念“我能承受”。

The force of old habits and the blackmailer’s skillfulness at creating FOG can make using the new responses an unnerving experience. With punishers, who dislike giving up any measure of control in a relationship—and with any blackmailer who’s strongly resistant to your time-buying statements—it’s important to clarify your motives. You might want to say something like:

旧习惯的根深蒂固，加上勒索者擅长制造心理迷雾，会让使用新的应对方式变成一件令人不安的事情。对于那些不愿在关系中放弃任何控制权的惩罚型勒索者，以及任何强烈抵制你拖延时间的勒索者，明确你的动机至关重要。你可以这样说：

  • This is not a power struggle.
    这不是一场权力斗争。
  • This is not about my trying to control you.
    这并非是我试图控制你。
  • This is about my needing more time to give thought to what you want.
    这是因为我需要更多时间来仔细考虑你的想法。

If you are dealing with a rational person, these are thoughtful, reassuring statements that can help defuse tension.

如果你面对的是一个理性的人，这些深思熟虑、令人安心的话语可以帮助缓解紧张气氛。

Doing It Right but Feeling Bad

做得对但感觉不好

Because asking for time and stating your motives takes you out of your accustomed role, it’s not unusual to do everything right and still feel as though you’ve bungled your end of the transaction. That’s what Zoe found:

因为请求时间并说明你的动机会让你脱离惯常的角色，所以即使你做的一切都正确无误，仍然会觉得自己在交易中搞砸了，这种情况并不罕见。佐伊就遇到了这种情况：

You want to know what happened? It was terrible. Tess was pushing me to put her on our big new shoe account because the partners who own the firm will be in from New York in a week and she wanted to impress them, especially Dale, who she’s convinced has his eye on getting rid of her position. The visit was a week away, and she wanted to have the assignment NOW. So she tried everything. She’d say, “I know I’m going to get fired if you don’t let me do this job, and I don’t know what I’ll do if you don’t help me. I hate to pressure you, but I really need help right now.” Her eyes started to tear up a little.

你想知道发生了什么吗？糟透了。苔丝一直缠着我让她负责我们新开的大鞋业客户，因为公司合伙人一周后要从纽约过来，她想给他们留下好印象，尤其是戴尔，她认定戴尔一心想把她赶走。合伙人一周后就要来，她恨不得马上就拿到这份工作。所以她使尽浑身解数。她说：“我知道如果你不让我做这份工作，我肯定会被炒鱿鱼，如果你不帮我，我真不知道该怎么办。我不想给你压力，但我现在真的需要帮助。”说着说着，她的眼眶就开始泛红。

I did what you said. I said, “I’m sorry, but I can’t make an important decision like that right now.” And she came right back with, “But you know how much this means to me. I really need your help. Aren’t we friends? Don’t you trust me? You know I’ll do a good job, and you know I’d do this for you.”

我照你说的做了。我说：“对不起，我现在没法做这么重要的决定。”她立刻反驳道：“可是你知道这对我有多重要。我真的需要你的帮助。我们不是朋友吗？你不信任我吗？你知道我会做好，你也知道我会为你做这件事。”

By this time, I’m getting caught in this “Oh my god, oh my god. I have to help her. This is urgent. She’s right. If I don’t help her now, she’ll be in big trouble. I have to do something.” I could feel my heart starting to beat faster and I felt like I was breathing faster, too. I tried to slow it down, and I did say a couple of quick I-can-stand-it’s. And then I said, “I know you want me to do something right now, but I need time to think about this. We can talk tomorrow.”

这时，我陷入了“天哪，天哪。我必须帮她。情况紧急。她说得对。如果我现在不帮她，她会有大麻烦。我必须做点什么。”的思维模式。我感觉自己的心跳开始加速，呼吸也变得急促起来。我努力让自己平静下来，还快速地说了几句“我能忍住”。然后我说：“我知道你想让我现在就做点什么，但我需要时间考虑一下。我们明天再谈。”

She gave me an angry glare and said, “I thought you were my friend as well as my boss. I thought friendship meant something to you.” And then she walked out and I totally felt like shit. And I still feel like I let her down. I thought this was supposed to make me feel better. I feel awful.

她狠狠地瞪了我一眼，说：“我以为你既是我的老板，也是我的朋友。我以为友情对你来说很重要。”说完她就走了，我感觉糟透了。直到现在，我仍然觉得自己让她失望了。我以为这样能让我感觉好一些。我感觉糟透了。

“Congratulations,” I told her. “That means you’re breaking old patterns.” Bad habits are comfortable, seductively so—until you feel their consequences. Buying time may not be easy, but it gets easier as you go along. And as I reminded Zoe, all you are doing at this point is delaying a decision. You haven’t done anything but put the blackmailer on your timetable—hardly the drastic step the blackmailer will probably say it is.

“恭喜你，”我告诉她，“这意味着你正在打破旧习。”坏习惯很舒服，甚至有种诱惑力——直到你感受到它们的后果。争取时间或许并不容易，但随着时间的推移，你会越来越得心应手。正如我提醒佐伊的那样，你现在所做的只是拖延一个决定。你只不过是把勒索者拉进了你的日程表——这远不像勒索者所说的那么极端。

As you continue to use your stalling scripts, the blackmailer may respond with increasing desperation. The operative words are “Gimme—NOW.”

当你继续使用拖延战术时，勒索者可能会越来越绝望。关键在于“现在就给我”。

Learning to tolerate discomfort in the service of healthy change is one of the most difficult things any of us has to do. In the past, discomfort has always been the prelude to compliance, but now you’re changing all that, and you’re going to feel unsteady. It’s OK to feel uncertain and anxious as you regain your integrity. Things are starting to shift internally as well as externally, and I want to reassure you that it’s perfectly natural to feel shaky when that’s happening.

学会忍受不适，从而实现健康的改变，是我们每个人都必须面对的最艰难的挑战之一。过去，不适往往是顺从的前奏，但现在你正在改变这一切，你会感到不安。在重拾自我的过程中，感到迷茫和焦虑是正常的。你的内在和外在都在发生变化，我想向你保证，在这种情况下感到不安是完全正常的。

Don’t let discomfort throw you off course.

不要让不适感扰乱你的计划。

A Dialogue with Discomfort

与不适的对话

Zoe felt increasingly uncomfortable about clinging to her request for time. Tess was insistent, and she became the picture of suffering whenever Zoe saw her. The more she thought about Tess’s request, the more she realized that she couldn’t give in to it—yet the guilt she felt seemed to get ever larger.

佐伊越来越觉得坚持要求多给点时间让她很不自在。苔丝坚持要她多给点时间，而且每次佐伊看到她，苔丝都一副痛苦不堪的样子。佐伊越想苔丝的要求，就越意识到自己不能答应——然而，她内心的愧疚感却似乎越来越强烈。

I can’t get over this feeling that I’m a heartless criminal. I feel worse and worse about this. I’m doing nothing, and it’s tearing me apart. Are you sure this is working?

我无法摆脱这种感觉，觉得自己像个冷血罪犯。这种感觉越来越强烈。我什么都没做，这让我痛苦不堪。你确定这样做有用吗？

Internal discomfort is one of the major impediments to change, and we’re so used to responding to it as though it were a fire to be put out that many of us haven’t learned to live with it in the natural amounts that accompany change. We push it away, extinguish it, treat it as though it has no place in our lives—and by doing so, we eliminate some of our most effective options. Most of us are so reluctant to examine our discomfort that we often misinterpret what it’s trying to tell us by reacting to its presence blindly instead of asking what it means.

内心的不适感是改变的主要障碍之一，我们习惯于把它当作一场必须扑灭的火灾来应对，以至于许多人都没有学会如何与它共存，而这种不适感本就伴随着改变而来。我们把它推开，扑灭它，仿佛它在我们的生活中毫无立足之地——这样做，我们反而错失了一些最有效的应对方式。我们大多数人都不愿正视自己的不适感，因此常常误解它想要告诉我们的信息，只是盲目地对它做出反应，而不是探究它的意义。

I told Zoe that one of the ways to reach wholeness is to reclaim even the parts of ourselves we’re struggling with and learn to recognize them as normal. One means of doing this involves entering into a dialogue with those parts—pulling them outside ourselves and getting to know them. For our next session, I asked Zoe to pick an object in her house that represented discomfort to her—an itchy sweater, an unflattering picture of herself, a tight pair of shoes—and we’d use it to get to know more about the feelings that seemed so formidable to her.

我告诉佐伊，达到身心完整的方法之一，就是重新接纳那些我们正在与之抗争的自我部分，并学会将它们视为正常状态。实现这一目标的方法之一是与这些部分展开对话——将它们从我们自身中抽离出来，去了解它们。在下次咨询中，我请佐伊挑选一件她家里让她感到不适的物品——一件让她发痒的毛衣、一张不太好看的自拍照、一双紧绷的鞋子——我们将以此为契机，更深入地了解那些对她来说似乎难以承受的感受。

When she came in, I asked her to take the object—she’d picked an unattractive pair of high heels that had never fit her—and put it on the empty chair in front of her. She was then to start talking to this symbol of her discomfort as though she were talking to a person. Later, she’d play the part of the discomfort itself and let it talk to her.

她进来后，我让她拿起那个东西——她选了一双不合脚、也不好看的高跟鞋——放在她面前的空椅子上。然后，她要对着这个象征着她不适感的物件说话，就像在跟人说话一样。之后，她要扮演这种不适感本身，让它跟她对话。

Zoe had never done anything like this before, and she felt understandably self-conscious and somewhat reluctant. But I explained to her that she could learn a lot about this state of being that seemed to have so much power over her. I encourage you to try this yourself, and feel free to vent. Tell the discomfort just how you feel about it and ask it questions.

佐伊以前从未做过这样的事，所以她感到不自在，甚至有些犹豫，这是可以理解的。但我向她解释说，她可以从中了解很多关于这种似乎对她有着强大控制力的状态的信息。我鼓励你也尝试一下，并尽情倾诉。把你对这种不适的感受如实告诉它，并向它提出问题。

Zoe warmed up to the process once she got going. Here are some of the things she said.

佐伊一旦进入状态，就逐渐投入到工作中。以下是她的一些发言。

Discomfort, you think you’re really hot stuff, don’t you. You’ve been running the show for a long time and I’m sick of it. I’ve given you a lot of power, but I’m putting you on notice that those days are over. I thought you were bigger than I am—and maybe you knew more—but when I look at you, I can see that you’re small, you’re ugly and you get me into trouble. In fact, whenever you take over, I’m such a wimp and a coward I don’t even know who I am anymore. I’m really tired of you. Is there any good reason why I shouldn’t just show you the door?

不舒服，你以为自己很了不起，是吧？你掌权太久了，我受够了。我给了你很大的权力，但我警告你，好日子到头了。我原以为你比我强大——或许你也比我懂得多——但现在我看着你，发现你渺小、丑陋，还给我惹麻烦。事实上，每次你掌权，我都变得如此懦弱胆小，甚至不知道自己是谁。我真的厌倦你了。我有什么理由不把你赶出去？

I asked Zoe what the experience had felt like for her.

我问佐伊，她当时的感受如何。

I felt kind of silly at first, but as I got into it, I realized that this part of me really takes over a lot of the time. It’s just one part, and I act as though it’s a 500-pound gorilla. It’s a lot more like these shoes—it just doesn’t fit in my life as much as I thought it did.

一开始我觉得有点傻，但后来我意识到，我内心的这一部分经常占据主导地位。它只是我的一部分，但我却把它当成一只500磅重的大猩猩。其实它更像是这双鞋——它并不像我想象中那样适合我的生活。

For the next part of the exercise, Zoe sat opposite me in the chair and held the shoes as she played the part of her discomfort, responding to what Zoe had just said.

在练习的下一部分，佐伊坐在我对面的椅子上，手里拿着鞋子，一边扮演着不自在的角色，一边对佐伊刚才说的话做出回应。

You show me the door? That’s a laugh. I’m not going anyplace. I like it here and I’m not leaving without a fight. It’s pretty cushy here—all I have to do is make one tiny squeak and you jump to let me do whatever I want.

你想把我赶出去？真是笑话。我哪儿也不去。我喜欢这里，不抗争一下我是不会走的。这里挺舒服的——我只要稍微动一下，你们就立马让我为所欲为。

Zoe came away from the exercise with a new way to look at a sensation she’d always thought she had no control over and had branded intolerable. But I told her that this awareness was not going to change things for her overnight. Though she’d begun to find some of the keys to her regular patterns of care-taking and capitulation, her discomfort wasn’t going to go away without a fight. Her job would still be to change behavior while she was feeling uncomfortable. Meanwhile, she could continue to get to know more about what brought discomfort up for her when she faced a blackmailer—and keep exploring ways to see discomfort as just one element of a situation, rather than the unbearable totality.

佐伊通过这次练习，对一种她一直认为自己无法控制、甚至觉得难以忍受的感觉有了新的认识。但我告诉她，这种觉察不会在一夜之间改变她的一切。虽然她已经开始找到一些应对日常照顾和屈服模式的关键，但她的不适感不会轻易消失。她仍然需要在感到不适时改变自己的行为。与此同时，她可以继续深入了解在面对勒索者时，是什么让她感到不适——并不断探索如何将不适感视为情境中的一个因素，而不是难以承受的整体。

I hope you’ll use this exercise yourself. You can speak to an object or, if you’d prefer, write a letter to your discomfort and a letter from your discomfort to you. Some people like to type a dialogue, first speaking to the discomfort, then asking questions of it and letting discomfort answer.

我希望你能亲自尝试一下这个练习。你可以对着一个物体说话，或者，如果你愿意，可以给你的不适感写一封信，再从你的不适感中写一封信给你。有些人喜欢用对话的形式，先对着不适感说话，然后向它提问，让它来回答。

Your words and discoveries may be very different from Zoe’s, but I’m sure you’ll gain valuable information. The point of the exercise is to externalize the discomfort, look at it and begin to develop ways of handling it that go beyond running the other way. When you face discomfort, you’ll find that it’s smaller, less menacing and far less threatening than it felt when you tried so hard to avoid it.

你的感受和发现或许与佐伊截然不同，但我相信你也能从中获得宝贵的信息。这项练习的目的是将不适感外化，正视它，并开始探索应对之道，而不是一味地逃避。当你直面不适时，你会发现它远没有你之前费尽心思逃避时那么可怕、那么令人不安。

Turning a Triangle into a Straight Line

将三角形变成直线

There’s another version of the do-nothing technique that’s useful when you find yourself in the middle of a conflict between two other people, or when a third party is using emotional blackmail on you to benefit someone else. The action you need to take: Get out of the way.

还有一种“不作为”策略，当你身处两人冲突之中，或者第三方利用情感勒索你以谋取他人利益时，这种策略就非常有用。你需要采取的行动是：置身事外。

For Karen, in the midst of her mini-crisis with her mother and her daughter, doing nothing actually proved to be the beginning of some real healing for all three women. Karen said:

对凯伦来说，在她与母亲和女儿之间出现小危机之际，什么都不做反而成了三人真正疗愈的开始。凯伦说：

Let’s say I’m able to stall the way you say when my mom says, “If Melanie comes to the party, I want to call the whole thing off.” And let’s say I’m able to tell her that I can’t make a decision about this right away and I’ll call her back. Then what?

假设我能像你说的拖延时间，当我妈说“如果梅兰妮来参加派对，我就取消整个派对”的时候，我告诉她我暂时无法做决定，我会稍后再给她回电话。然后呢？

“Then you call your mother and tell her your decision is that you’re not going to make a decision. Look, Karen, this is between your mother and Melanie. You know what happens to the referee when he tries to get between two fighters—he gets clobbered! You need to get out of the middle. Tell your mother that she’s the one who’s going to tell Melanie that she doesn’t want her at the party and you’re not going to do it for her. You’ve got plenty of time to cancel the party if you need to. Let’s see what happens.”

“然后你就打电话给你妈，告诉她你决定不做决定。听着，凯伦，这是你妈和梅兰妮之间的事。你知道裁判插手两个打手会怎么样吗？——他会被揍得鼻青脸肿！你得置身事外。告诉你妈，她会告诉梅兰妮她不想让她来参加派对，你不会替她这么做。如果需要的话，你有足够的时间取消派对。咱们走着瞧吧。”

As expected, Frances howled and complained and pressured Karen to do her dirty work for her, which was to be expected. But when she saw that Karen wouldn’t budge, she did indeed call her granddaughter and told her that she was upset with her. To everyone’s amazement, this opened the door to some honest dialogue between Melanie and her grandmother, which resulted in some major air-clearing between them—and the beginning of a more honest relationship. This, in turn, had a positive effect on Karen’s relationship with Frances because Frances saw her daughter refuse to yield to pressure. As a result, Frances gained a new respect for Karen and began to realize the old manipulations weren’t going to work anymore. All this because Karen did “nothing.”

不出所料，弗朗西丝又吼又闹，逼迫凯伦替她做些见不得光的事。但当她见凯伦不肯让步时，她真的给孙女打了电话，表达了对她的不满。出乎所有人意料的是，这竟促成了梅兰妮和祖母之间坦诚的对话，消除了彼此间的隔阂，也开启了更加真诚的关系。反过来，这也对凯伦和弗朗西丝的关系产生了积极的影响，因为弗朗西丝看到女儿拒绝屈服于压力。结果，弗朗西丝对凯伦刮目相看，也开始意识到过去的那些伎俩已经行不通了。而这一切，仅仅是因为凯伦“什么都没做”。

It’s essential when you get triangled into a conflict between two people in your life that you gracefully remove yourself from the ring by refusing to carry messages or become an arbitrator. If you don’t remove yourself, it’s almost a given that the bad feelings between the other people will end up being dumped on you, and nothing will get resolved.

当你的生活陷入两个人之间的冲突时，至关重要的是要优雅地抽身而出，拒绝传递信息或充当调解人。如果你不置身事外，几乎可以肯定的是，其他人的负面情绪最终会转移到你身上，而问题也得不到解决。

In Maria’s case, her in-laws put themselves in the middle between Maria and Jay and were pushing hard on her obligation hot buttons to keep her from leaving their son. Maria had already told Jay that she needed time to make such an important decision, and despite his fervent pleas for an answer, she didn’t waver. However, with her in-laws she was having a tough time being resolute.

玛丽亚的公婆介入了她和杰伊的感情，并不断利用她对儿子的责任感，试图阻止她离开儿子。玛丽亚已经告诉杰伊，她需要时间来做这个重要的决定，尽管杰伊苦苦哀求，她依然坚定不移。然而，面对公婆，她很难再下定决心。

I know how much I’m hurting them, and they don’t deserve it. They’re dear, sweet people and they haven’t done anything wrong, but I know how much they’ll suffer if I divorce Jay. His mom calls me almost daily and reminds me how much it would mean to them if Jay and I could work things out.

我知道我给他们带来了多大的伤害，他们不应该承受这些。他们都是善良可爱的人，他们没有做错任何事，但我知道如果我和杰离婚，他们会多么痛苦。杰的妈妈几乎每天都给我打电话，提醒我如果我和杰能重归于好，对他们来说意义有多么重大。

I told Maria that she, too, needed to learn how to do nothing. In her case, that involved not having repetitive coercive phone conversations with her mother-in-law or dwelling on this subject with anyone else who had their own agenda. A sample set of responses I gave Maria can help you disengage yourself from the pressure of third parties.

我告诉玛丽亚，她也需要学会什么都不做。对她来说，这意味着不要再和婆婆进行反复的、带有胁迫性的电话交谈，也不要和任何有其他目的的人纠缠于这个话题。我给玛丽亚的一些应对方法可以帮助你摆脱第三方的压力。

Mother-in-law: “Fred and I can’t stand this. We don’t know what’s happening or what’s going to happen. We’re so worried about you and Jay and our grandkids. How long are you going to take to decide about a divorce?”

婆婆：“弗雷德和我受够了。我们不知道现在发生了什么，也不知道将来会发生什么。我们非常担心你、杰伊还有我们的孙子孙女们。你们到底还要多久才能决定离婚？”

Maria: “Mom, I haven’t made a decision.”

玛丽亚：“妈妈，我还没做决定。”

Mother-in-law: “Then how long is it going to take?”

婆婆：“那还要多久？”

Maria: “Mom, it’ll take as long as it takes. Let’s talk about something else.”

玛丽亚：“妈，需要多久就多久。我们聊点别的吧。”

Just keep answering that you haven’t made a decision, repeat that it’ll take as long as it takes to decide—and then change the subject. People ask us lots of questions, and often we feel we have to answer definitively right away. Of course, we don’t. It’s fine to answer with “I don’t know.” It’s equally fine to say “I’ll let you know when I’ve made a decision.” And if pressure continues, it’s fine to steer the conversation to other topics. Even when the person pressuring you is not the blackmailer, but rather a person you like and respect, it’s vital to maintain your own timetable and not feel rushed to make a decision, especially an important one.

就一直回答说你还没做决定，反复强调需要时间考虑——然后转移话题。人们总是问我们很多问题，我们常常觉得必须马上给出明确的答案。当然，我们不必如此。回答“我不知道”完全没问题。同样，说“等我决定了会告诉你”也完全可以。如果对方继续施压，那就把话题引到其他方面。即使施压的人不是勒索者，而是你喜欢和尊重的人，也务必保持自己的节奏，不要急于做决定，尤其是在重要的事情上。

Take Some Space

留出一些空间

Buying time gives you a chance to experience your own thoughts, your own priorities and your own feelings. Remember that you have a lifeline to hold on to—your time-buying statements. You may feel like a broken record by the time you’re through repeating them, but keep going and give them a chance to work.

争取时间能让你有机会体验自己的想法、自己的优先事项和自己的感受。记住，你还有一根救命稻草——那就是你争取时间的那些话。重复一遍之后，你可能会觉得自己像个复读机，但请坚持下去，给它们一个发挥作用的机会。

However, if after using these statements you still feel so anxious and pressured that you’re tempted to do something to alleviate your discomfort, walk away. I’m not talking about turning on your heel and leaving the other person without explanation. I’m talking about excusing yourself and going to another room where you can be quiet for a few minutes. You can say “I need a drink of water” or “I need to use the bathroom—I’ll be right back.” Or if you feel really anxious, how about “I need a drink of water and I need to use the bathroom.”

但是，如果你用了这些话之后仍然感到焦虑和压力，想要做点什么来缓解这种不适，那就走开。我说的不是转身就走，不给对方任何解释。我的意思是找个借口离开，去另一个房间安静地待一会儿。你可以说“我想喝杯水”或者“我想去趟洗手间，马上回来”。如果你真的感到很焦虑，那就说“我想喝杯水，也想去趟洗手间”。

By the way, you can do this at home, in a restaurant, at the office, on an airplane, in fact, just about anywhere. Putting some physical distance, even a room or two, between you and the blackmailer can take a lot of urgency out of the transaction and give you some all-important emotional distance as well.

顺便说一句，你可以在家、餐厅、办公室、飞机上，实际上几乎任何地方这样做。在你和勒索者之间保持一定的物理距离，哪怕只是一两个房间，也能大大降低交易的紧迫性，同时也能给你带来至关重要的情感距离。

When I talk about emotional distance, I mean turning down the flame and allowing your feelings to cool. When confronted with emotional blackmail, your feelings may be so intense that you can’t think, reason, judge or look at what your choices are. Emotional blackmail is in your face: intense, pressured, demanding—full of frantic energy. This cacophony of feelings often seems overwhelming. You’re in a state of pure emotional reactiveness, and you need to move into a more cognitive, detached mode. Taking a few minutes to quiet yourself will do that for you. Calm yourself, repeat “I can stand it,” and resolve to buy yourself time.

当我谈到情感上的疏离时，我的意思是缓和情绪，让你的感受冷却下来。当面对情感勒索时，你的感受可能非常强烈，以至于你无法思考、推理、判断，也无法审视自己的选择。情感勒索就摆在你面前：强烈、充满压力、咄咄逼人——充满了疯狂的能量。这种纷乱的情绪常常让人难以承受。你正处于一种纯粹的情绪反应状态，你需要进入一种更具理性、更超脱的状态。花几分钟时间让自己安静下来就能做到这一点。让自己平静下来，反复告诉自己“我可以承受”，并下定决心为自己争取时间。

STEP TWO: BECOME AN OBSERVER

第二步：成为一名观察者

Once you’ve detached yourself from the blackmail drama, you’re in a position to gather the information that will help you decide how to respond to the blackmailer. During the time you have bought to make your decision, you’ll need to become an observer of both yourself and the other person.

一旦你从勒索事件中抽身出来，你就能收集信息，从而决定如何应对勒索者。在你做出决定的这段时间里，你需要冷静地观察自己和对方。

Use Visualization

使用可视化

To help you do this, I’d like you to use this visualization exercise: Envision a glass elevator on the ground floor of a 50-story observation tower. I’d like you to picture yourself inside the elevator as the car slowly starts to move up. As you look out on the lower floors, it’s difficult to see anything because of a swirling ground fog. Occasionally the fog breaks and you can make out the outlines of objects and people, but they’re vague and fuzzy, appearing and disappearing. This is the realm of pure emotions, the gut feelings that blackmailers churn up in us.

为了帮助你做到这一点，我希望你做以下想象练习：想象你身处一座50层观景塔的底层，乘坐着一部玻璃电梯。想象自己坐在电梯里，电梯缓缓上升。当你向低层望去时，由于地面雾气弥漫，你几乎什么都看不清。偶尔雾气散开，你能看到物体和人的轮廓，但它们模糊不清，时隐时现。这就是纯粹情感的领域，是勒索者在我们心中激起的那种本能感受。

The elevator car keeps moving up, and as it does, you leave the fog behind and begin to see a wider landscape. By the time you reach the top, you have a panoramic view, and you can see that the fog that you thought covered everything is confined to the valley at the base of the tower. What seemed all-encompassing was just a tiny patch, a small part of the picture. The elevator has reached a different plane, a place of reason, perception and objectivity. Step out of the car onto the observation platform. Enjoy the quiet and the clarity. Remember that you always have access to this place.

电梯轿厢继续向上移动，随着电梯的上升，你逐渐摆脱了迷雾，开始看到更广阔的景色。到达顶端时，你拥有了全景视野，你会发现，你以为笼罩一切的迷雾其实只局限于塔底的山谷。之前看似无所不在的迷雾，其实只是其中一小块，是整个画面的一小部分。电梯已经到达了另一个层面，一个理性、感知和客观的境界。走出轿厢，来到观景台上。尽情享受这份宁静与澄澈。记住，你随时都可以来到这里。

Traveling up from the gut level to the head is useful when you’re under the pressure of blackmail because it’s easy for us to get so caught up in the feelings of fear, obligation and guilt that our perceptions are fragmentary or distorted. I’m not asking you to detach from your feelings—I’d just like you to add perception and reason to the mix so that you’re not driven solely by feeling. Both the intellect and the emotions contain a great deal of information, and we need to create an exchange between the two. The goal is to be able to think and feel at the same time, rather than just thrashing around in the emotions alone. When blackmail heats up, you need the perspective of the observation tower.

在遭受勒索的压力时，从本能层面提升到理性层面会很有帮助，因为我们很容易被恐惧、责任和内疚等情绪所困扰，导致认知碎片化或扭曲。我并不是要你完全摆脱情感——我只是希望你能将感知和理性融入其中，这样你就不会完全被感觉所左右。理智和情感都包含大量信息，我们需要在两者之间建立联系。目标是能够同时思考和感受，而不是仅仅被情绪所左右。当勒索愈演愈烈时，你需要站在高台上，保持清醒的头脑。

What’s Really Happening?

究竟发生了什么？

Take time alone to think about the blackmailer’s request, stepping into the role of observer. Your feelings will still be there, but turn your attention away from them and let your mind review the situation. Ask yourself: What just happened? It’s a good idea to write down the answers to the questions that follow. Taking the information out of your head and putting it on paper will also help you gain emotional distance. If not, you can do this entirely in your head. Either way, answering these questions will provide a lot of clarity for you.

独自一人静下心来思考勒索者的要求，把自己当作一个旁观者。你的情绪依然会存在，但要将注意力从它们身上转移开，让你的思绪重新审视整个情况。问问自己：刚才发生了什么？最好把接下来问题的答案写下来。把信息从脑海中转移到纸上，也能帮助你拉开情感上的距离。如果不想写，你也可以完全在脑海中思考。无论哪种方式，回答这些问题都会让你思路清晰很多。

First, step back and look at the demand.

首先，退后一步，看看市场需求。

  1. What did the other person want?
    对方想要什么？
  2. How was the request made? For example, was it posed lovingly, threateningly, impatiently? Use any description that applies to your situation.
    这个请求是如何提出的？例如，是充满爱意的、带有威胁性的还是不耐烦的？请使用任何适用于您情况的描述。
  3. What did the blackmailer do when you didn’t agree immediately? Here, you’ll want to take into account facial expressions, tone of voice, body language. Be as specific as you can. What were the blackmailer’s eyes doing? Where were their arms and hands? Where did they stand while speaking to you? What gestures did they use? What tone of voice? What was the overall emotional tone? Put into words the picture you’ve taken in.

    Here are notes that Patty took after a recent scene with Joe:


    当你没有立即答应时，勒索者做了什么？你需要注意他们的面部表情、语气和肢体语言。尽可能具体地描述。勒索者的眼神如何？他们的手臂和手放在哪里？他们和你说话时站在哪里？他们使用了哪些手势？语气如何？整体情绪基调是什么？用文字描述你观察到的画面。以下是帕蒂在最近一次与乔的谈话后所做的笔记：

He was withdrawing, sulking, acting very upset. His whole posture and body language was communicating how sad and disappointed he was. His arms were crossed on his chest and he wouldn’t look me in the eye. He was sighing a lot and pulling at the lint on his sweater, and when he talked he whined. Then he got up, slammed the door and turned up the radio in the bedroom.

他变得孤僻，闷闷不乐，非常沮丧。他的姿态和肢体语言都在诉说着他的悲伤和失望。他双臂抱在胸前，不敢直视我的眼睛。他不停地叹气，揪着毛衣上的绒毛，说话时也总是带着抱怨的语气。然后他起身，砰地一声关上门，把卧室里的收音机音量调大。

Next, look at your own reactions to the demand.

接下来，看看你对这种需求的反应。

1. WHAT ARE YOU THINKING?

1. 你在想什么？

Write down what’s going through your mind, paying special attention to thoughts that repeat or keep intruding. They’ll give you valuable insights into the beliefs that you have formed over the years. Among the common beliefs I see in blackmail targets are:

把你脑子里想的事情写下来，特别注意那些反复出现或不断闯入的念头。它们会让你更深入地了解自己多年来形成的信念。我在勒索受害者身上发现的一些常见信念包括：

  • It’s OK to give a lot more than I get.
    付出远多于所得是可以的。
  • If I love someone, I’m responsible for their happiness.
    如果我爱一个人，我就有责任让他人幸福。
  • Good, loving people are supposed to make the other person happy.
    善良有爱心的人应该让对方感到快乐。
  • If I do what I really want to do, the other person will see me as selfish.
    如果我做自己真正想做的事，对方会觉得我自私。
  • Getting rejected is the worst thing that could happen to me.
    被拒绝是我最不愿遇到的事。
  • If no one else will fix the problem, it’s up to me.
    如果没人愿意解决这个问题，那就只能靠我了。
  • I never win with this person.
    我跟这个人打永远赢不了。
  • The other person is smarter or stronger than I am.
    对方比我聪明或强壮。
  • It won’t kill me to do this, because they really need me.
    这样做不会要了我的命，因为他们真的需要我。
  • Their needs and feelings are more important than mine.
    他们的需求和感受比我的需求和感受更重要。

Which of these statements seem true to you? Which do you identify with the most? Ask yourself: Where did I learn this, and how long have I believed it?

你觉得这些说法哪些是正确的？你最认同哪一种？问问自己：我是在哪里学到这些的，我信奉这些说法有多久了？

None of these beliefs is true, yet we cling to them because they’re what we’ve absorbed over the years. Often, as I’ve mentioned, we think we chose such beliefs, but they’ve been imparted by powerful people at every stage of our lives—parents, teachers, mentors, close friends. It’s important to identify our beliefs about ourselves as they come up in the face of emotional blackmail because beliefs are the precursor to feelings.

这些信念没有一个是正确的，但我们却执迷不悟，因为它们是我们多年来耳濡目染形成的。正如我之前提到的，我们常常以为自己选择了这些信念，但实际上，它们是我们人生各个阶段那些有影响力的人——父母、老师、导师、挚友——灌输给我们的。面对情感勒索，认清我们关于自身的信念至关重要，因为信念是情感的先决条件。

Feelings aren’t the ephemeral, independent forces we often think they are. They’re a response to what we think. Almost every anxious, sad, fearful or guilty feeling we have in response to emotional blackmail is preceded by a negative or erroneous belief about our own adequacy, lovability and responsibility to others. And these beliefs are fountainheads of our feelings. Our behavior, then, is often an attempt to quiet the uncomfortable feelings that spring from these beliefs. The bottom line: to change self-defeating behavior patterns, we must start with the root element—our beliefs.

情感并非我们通常认为的那样转瞬即逝、独立存在。它们是对我们想法的一种回应。几乎每一种因情感勒索而产生的焦虑、悲伤、恐惧或内疚感，都源于我们对自身能力、可爱程度以及对他人的责任感的负面或错误信念。而这些信念正是我们情感的源泉。因此，我们的行为往往是为了平息这些信念所引发的不适感。归根结底：要改变自我挫败的行为模式，我们必须从根源入手——我们的信念。

When Eve guiltily drops out of school because Elliot is upset, she’s acting on a belief that his feelings have more value than hers do. First comes the belief: the other person is more important than I am, and what I want isn’t important. From the belief flow the feelings: guilt, obligation, pity. And finally, the behavior: dropping out of school.

当伊芙因为埃利奥特难过而内疚地辍学时，她其实是出于一种信念：埃利奥特的感受比她的更重要。首先是这种信念：对方比我更重要，我的想法并不重要。这种信念衍生出各种感受：内疚、责任感和自怜。最终，导致了辍学的行为。

We know now that our moods are influenced as much by our brain chemistry as by the events in our lives, but even many of the people who have repetitive depressions and anxiety disorders as a result of biochemical imbalances can exacerbate these conditions with self-denigrating beliefs. Uncovering your deep beliefs can help you learn why you feel the way you do. And once you’ve done that, you’ll begin to see how these beliefs and feelings become the catalyst for self-defeating behavior patterns of compliance and capitulation.

我们现在知道，情绪不仅受生活事件的影响，也受大脑化学物质的影响。但即使是那些因生化失衡而反复出现抑郁和焦虑症状的人，也会因为自我贬低的信念而加剧病情。揭开你深层的信念可以帮助你了解自己感受的根源。一旦你做到了这一点，你就会开始明白，这些信念和感受是如何成为自我挫败行为模式（例如顺从和屈服）的催化剂。

2. HOW ARE YOU FEELING?

2. 你感觉怎么样？

What do you feel as you replay your transaction with the blackmailer? Write down as many feelings as you are aware of, using the following list as a starting point:

当你回想与勒索者的交易过程时，你有什么感受？请把你意识到的所有感受都写下来，可以参考以下列表：

Angry

生气的

Irritated

烦躁

Wrong

错误的

Anxious

焦虑的

Trapped

被困

Threatened

受到威胁

Insecure

缺乏安全感

Inadequate

不足

Unlovable

不讨人喜欢

Overwhelmed

不知所措

Hurt

伤害

Frustrated

沮丧的

Doomed

注定失败

Resentful

不满

Guilty

有罪的

Disappointed

失望的

Scared

害怕的

Stuck

卡住

This check-in is the equivalent of taking your emotional pulse, and though it’s simple, it’s an important diagnostic tool. Keep in mind that a feeling is an emotional state that can be expressed in one, or at most two, words. The moment you say “I feel like . . .” or “I feel that . . . ,” you’re describing what you think or believe. Because we’re trying to differentiate between thoughts and feelings, and find the relationships between them, it’s important to be clear.

这种自我评估相当于测量你的情绪脉搏，虽然简单，却是一个重要的诊断工具。记住，感觉是一种情绪状态，可以用一到两个词来表达。当你表达“我感觉……”或“我觉得……”时，你描述的是你的想法或信念。因为我们试图区分想法和感觉，并找到它们之间的联系，所以表达清晰至关重要。

Example: “I feel that my husband always wins” is a thought. To get to the feeling, you can say, “I believe that my husband always wins, and I feel discouraged.”

例如：“我觉得我丈夫总是赢”是一种想法。要表达这种感觉，你可以说：“我相信我丈夫总是赢，这让我感到沮丧。”

Now check in with your body.

现在，倾听你身体的声音。

As you look at your list, identify where you feel these feelings physically. Are they churning in your stomach? Knotting in your neck? Gripping in your back? Burning in your cheeks? Notice how your body reacts to your feelings.

当你查看清单时，请感受一下这些感受在你身体的哪个部位有所体现。它们是否让你胃部翻腾？脖子发紧？背部紧绷？脸颊灼热？注意你的身体对这些感受的反应。

Sometimes our bodies will tell us a truth that our minds don’t. We may say we’re really not anxious—then notice that we’re drenched with perspiration. No, no, nothing’s wrong—so why is my stomach in knots? The body’s responses cut through denial and rationalization, and the body won’t lie to you. Keep in mind that any time you identify feelings of anger or resentment, you’re being alerted to watch out for aspects of the demand that are not in your best interests.

有时候，我们的身体会告诉我们一些我们头脑无法理解的真相。我们可能说自己一点也不焦虑——然后却发现自己汗流浃背。不，不，什么事都没有——那为什么我的胃会像打了个结一样难受呢？身体的反应会戳穿你的否认和合理化，而且身体不会骗你。记住，每当你察觉到愤怒或怨恨的情绪时，它都在提醒你注意那些对你不利的需求。

3. WHAT ARE YOUR FLASHPOINTS?

3. 你们的冲突导火索是什么？

The blackmailer’s words and nonverbal language resonate within us in very particular ways, and it’s important to know what our personal triggers are. Facial expressions, tone of voice, gestures, postures, words and even smells can activate belief systems and feelings that lead us toward giving in to a demand. They’re the wires that lead straight to our hot buttons, and the more we know what gets to them, the closer we can come to disconnecting them.

勒索者的言语和非语言表达会以非常特殊的方式在我们心中产生共鸣，因此了解我们自身的触发点至关重要。面部表情、语气、手势、姿势、言辞，甚至气味，都可能激活我们的信念系统和情感，最终导致我们屈服于勒索的要求。它们就像电线一样，直通我们的敏感点。我们越了解哪些因素会触动这些敏感点，就越能避免被它们牵着鼻子走。

Observe yourself, and think over past instances of blackmail. Then list the behaviors that get to you the most. Among the triggers I’ve seen are:

观察自己，回想过去遭遇勒索的经历。然后列出最让你感到不适的行为。我观察到的一些触发因素包括：

  • Yelling
    大声喊叫
  • Door-slamming
    摔门
  • Particular words (like “big shot,” “selfish”) that make us feel bad about ourselves
    某些特定的词语（例如“大人物”、“自私的人”）会让我们感到自卑。
  • Crying
    哭泣
  • Sighing
    叹息
  • An angry face—red face, eyebrows drawing together, angry scowl
    愤怒的表情——脸涨得通红，眉头紧锁，怒目而视
  • The silent treatment
    冷战

Then connect the behavior to your feelings: When the blackmailer does __________, I feel __________________.

然后将这种行为与你的感受联系起来：当勒索者做出____时，我感到____。

When I asked Josh to begin to connect his father’s appearance and behavior to specific responses in himself, he noticed that it was his father’s appearance even more than his words that turned up the anxiety levels he felt.

当我让乔希开始将他父亲的外貌和行为与他自身的特定反应联系起来时，他注意到，是他父亲的外貌，甚至比他的言语，更能加剧他的焦虑感。

“Susan, I made my lists, and I noticed that whenever my father’s face gets red—before he even opens his mouth—I get scared. I looked through all the adjectives, and I tried to find something more dignified than scared, but that’s the one that fit the best. Scared for me is fight or flight—I start going on pure animal instinct.”

“苏珊，我列了清单，我注意到，每当我父亲脸涨红——甚至在他开口说话之前——我就会感到害怕。我翻遍了所有的形容词，想找一个比‘害怕’更体面的词，但‘害怕’是最合适的。对我来说，害怕就意味着战斗或逃跑——我会完全按照动物的本能行事。”

It’s important to be as honest as you can while you’re observing. Don’t judge the feelings, don’t evaluate them, and don’t try to decide whether they’re valid or not valid or whether you have a right to be feeling them. Turn off the running commentary and observe. I’ve found that it helps many people to preface their observations with phrases such as:

观察时，尽可能保持诚实非常重要。不要评判感受，不要评估感受，也不要试图判断感受是否合理，或者你是否有权感受这些感受。停止胡思乱想，静下心来观察。我发现，在开始观察之前，用以下语句开头对很多人很有帮助：

  • Isn’t it interesting that . . .
    这不是很奇怪吗……
  • I’m beginning to notice that . . .
    我开始注意到……
  • I never realized that . . .
    我从未意识到……
  • I’m becoming aware that . . .
    我逐渐意识到……

Josh noticed that his defensiveness and anxiety lessened when he phrased his observation this way: “Isn’t it interesting that whenever I see my father’s face get red, I feel scared.” It’s a far more thoughtful and objective statement than “I get really scared when my father’s face gets red.” This objectivity helps put you in a more cognitive mode and helps insulate you from self-criticism. “When I said to myself, ‘Isn’t it interesting,’ I felt a lot less like a baby and a wimp,” Josh said.

乔什注意到，当他这样表达自己的感受时，他的防御心理和焦虑感有所减轻：“是不是很奇怪，每次看到爸爸脸红，我都会感到害怕。” 这比“爸爸脸红的时候我真的会很害怕”要理性得多，也客观得多。这种客观性有助于你进入一种更理性的思考模式，并帮助你避免自我批评。“当我对自己说‘是不是很奇怪’时，我感觉自己不再像个孩子，也不再那么胆小了，”乔什说道。

The “Isn’t it interesting” let Josh know that what followed were observer’s comments, and it gave him more distance from the judge inside that tends to critique and label so many of our reactions.

“这不是很有趣吗？”这句话让乔希意识到接下来是旁观者的评论，也让他与内心那个喜欢批评和评判我们许多反应的评判者拉开了距离。

Keep observing until you begin to make connections between your beliefs, feelings and behavior. Our blackmailers have made these connections both instinctively and intellectually, and they’ve used them to keep their advantage over us. But now you’ve begun to level the playing field, and what was once “insider information” is available to you. Now I’ll give you the tools to turn this preparation and knowledge into effective behavioral strategies that will dramatically alter the existing patterns between you and the blackmailer.

持续观察，直到你开始将你的信念、感受和行为联系起来。勒索者凭借本能和理性，早已将这些联系融会贯通，并利用它们来维持对我们的优势。但现在，你已经开始扭转局面，曾经的“内幕消息”也为你所用。接下来，我将为你提供工具，帮助你将这些准备和知识转化为有效的行为策略，从而彻底改变你与勒索者之间现有的互动模式。

# ↩

9

A Time for Decision

抉择的时刻

In the past, you’ve generally responded to the urgency of the other person’s needs and desires with automatic compliance—an almost reflexive response to pressure. But now that you’ve bought some time, you have the luxury of being able to consider what you want as well. Although I can’t make your decision for you, I can help you ask some penetrating questions that will enable you to take an objective look at what’s being asked of you and thoughtfully decide whether you want to comply or resist. Once you’ve done that, I’ll show you powerful and effective ways to present your decision to the blackmailer and deal with his or her reaction to the choice you’ve made.

过去，面对对方迫切的需求和愿望，你通常会下意识地顺从——几乎是出于本能地应对压力。但现在你争取到了一些时间，可以好好考虑一下自己的想法。虽然我不能替你做决定，但我可以帮助你提出一些深刻的问题，让你能够客观地审视对方的要求，并认真思考是顺从还是反抗。做出决定后，我会教你一些有效且有力的方法，向勒索者表明你的决定，并应对对方对你选择的反应。

THE THREE CATEGORIES OF DEMANDS

三种需求类别

To begin, I’d like you to go back to the other person’s demand and answer some questions about it. Write the answers down, and as you do, don’t censor yourself, and don’t feel that you’re permanently bound to what you put on the page. If you change your mind or have new insights, go back and add, erase or enlarge upon your original response.

首先，请你回顾一下对方的要求，并回答一些相关问题。把答案写下来，在回答的过程中，不要自我审查，也不要觉得你写下的内容就一定不能更改。如果你改变了想法或有了新的见解，可以返回去补充、删除或扩展你最初的回答。

  • Is something in this demand making me uncomfortable? What is it?
    这个要求中有什么地方让我感到不舒服吗？是什么呢？
  • What part of the demand is OK for me, and what part is not?
    哪些需求部分我可以接受，哪些部分我不能接受？
  • Is what the other person wants going to hurt me?
    对方想要的东西会伤害我吗？
  • Is what the other person wants going to hurt anyone else?
    对方想要的东西会伤害到其他人吗？
  • Does the other person’s request take into consideration my wants and feelings?
    对方的要求是否考虑到了我的意愿和感受？
  • Is something in the demand or the way it was presented to me making me feel afraid, obligated or guilty? What is it?
    需求本身或者呈现方式是否让我感到害怕、有义务或内疚？究竟是什么？
  • What’s in it for me?
    我能从中得到什么好处？

You’ll notice that if you look at the component parts of a demand, you may very well be able to accept all but one or two of them. For example, your husband is pressuring you to travel across the country to visit his folks, which you’re happy to do, but this is your busy time of year at work, and that’s making you uncomfortable. This is important information to have as you shape your response.

你会发现，如果你仔细分析一项要求的组成部分，你很可能可以接受其中除一两项以外的所有要求。例如，你丈夫一直催促你横跨整个国家去看望他的父母，你很乐意去，但这段时间是你一年中最忙的时候，这让你感到不自在。在你制定应对方案时，了解这些信息至关重要。

You may begin to feel alarmed if you answer yes to the red-flag questions that ask if you or anyone else will be hurt by complying with the demand. That’s your integrity barometer warning you of an impending storm.

如果你对那些“遵从要求是否会伤害到你或其他人”的警示性问题回答“是”，你可能会开始感到不安。这是你诚信的晴雨表，它预示着一场风暴即将到来。

As you look over your answers, you’ll find that most demands fall into one of three categories:

当你查看你的答案时，你会发现大多数要求都属于以下三类之一：

  1. The demand is no big deal.
    需求量并不大。
  2. The demand involves important issues, and your integrity is on the line.
    这项要求涉及重要问题，你的正直正直将受到考验。
  3. The demand involves a major life issue, and/or giving in would be harmful to you or others.
    该要求涉及重大的人生问题，而且/或者满足该要求会对您或他人造成伤害。

Different decisions and responses, naturally, are appropriate for each category, and in the sections that follow, I’ll help you assess your answers and consider options suited to each one.

当然，不同的决定和应对方式对不同的类别都是合适的，在接下来的章节中，我将帮助你评估你的答案，并考虑适合每个类别的选项。

NO BIG DEAL

没什么大不了的

Small decisions come up daily in most of our relationships. We go back and forth about the timing and cost of purchases, where to spend our vacations, how much time to spend with someone, how to balance career, family and friends. These are not matters of life and death, and it’s common not to have strong feelings about disagreements in one of these arenas. No matter what happens, no one will suffer great harm, and the primary cause of friction is probably the blackmailer’s pressure tactics rather than the content of the demand. Some of us tend to cede this category automatically to the blackmailer, thinking there’s no harm in doing so. It’s small potatoes. No big deal.

在大多数人的人际关系中，每天都会遇到一些小决定。我们会反复讨论购物的时间和价格、去哪里度假、花多少时间陪伴某人、如何平衡事业、家庭和朋友等等。这些都不是生死攸关的大事，所以对于这些领域的分歧，我们通常也不会太在意。无论发生什么，都不会有人受到太大的伤害，摩擦的主要原因很可能是勒索者的施压手段，而不是勒索内容本身。有些人往往会不假思索地在这类事情上向勒索者妥协，认为这样做没什么大不了的。这只是小事一桩，没什么大不了的。

But please proceed with caution here. The word automatic is one I’d like you to try to erase in any dealings with an emotional blackmailer. No matter how small the issue, examine the demand, especially the style in which it was presented to you. Get a clear understanding of the parts of it that bother you, if any, and look at the transaction in the context of the relationship as a whole.

但请务必谨慎行事。在与情感勒索者打交道时，我希望你尽量避免使用“自动”这个词。无论问题多么微不足道，都要仔细审视对方的要求，尤其是他们提出要求的方式。弄清楚其中哪些部分让你感到不安（如果有的话），并将整个交易放在你们关系的整体背景下进行分析。

Going Through the Process

经历这个过程

When Leigh, the stockbroker whose mother, Ellen, constantly used negative comparisons, mentioned that she was having a tough time at work and was dreading the prospect of going out to dinner with her mother later in the week, which Ellen was pressuring her to do, I asked her to go through this process.

股票经纪人莉（Leigh）的母亲艾伦（Ellen）总是喜欢拿别人做负面比较。莉提到自己工作很不顺心，而且很害怕这周晚些时候要和母亲一起出去吃饭，因为艾伦一直催促她去。于是我请她尝试一下这个过程。

“Oh come on, Susan,” she said. “This is ridiculous. So I’m tired. It’s just one dinner, and it’s not going to kill me.”

“哎呀，苏珊，”她说。“这太荒谬了。我的确很累。不就是吃顿晚饭吗，又不会要了我的命。”

“Just walk through the list,” I told her. “You never know what you’ll find out.”

“你就按清单过一遍吧，”我告诉她。“你永远不知道会发现什么。”

“OK,” she said reluctantly. “This will be fast. The only thing about Mom’s wanting to go out that bothered me was that when I said I was tired, she said something about how Caroline always had time for her. I don’t mind taking Mom out, and it’s crazy to ask if it’s going to hurt anyone—of course it won’t. Does she care how I feel—well, not entirely, but this is just dinner, for god’s sake. Why should I fight about that? Is she making me feel afraid? No. Obligated? Kind of. Guilty? A little. But so what? I’ll probably go and be glad I did—believe it or not, we like spending time together. And what’s in it for me . . . I’ll make her happy and I’ll feel good about that.”

“好吧，”她不情愿地说，“很快就好。妈妈想出去吃饭，唯一让我有点在意的是，我说我累了的时候，她说卡罗琳总是有时间陪她。我不介意带妈妈出去，问会不会伤害到别人也太傻了——当然不会。她会在意我的感受吗？嗯，倒也不是完全在意，但这只是顿饭而已，我的天。我为什么要为此争辩？她让我害怕吗？不。有义务吗？有点。有愧疚感吗？有一点。但那又怎样？我可能去了之后还会很高兴——信不信由你，我们喜欢待在一起。对我来说又有什么好处呢……我会让她开心，我会为此感到高兴。”

I asked Leigh how answering the questions had made her feel.

我问莉，回答这些问题让她感觉如何。

“I guess my neck and jaw are a little tight,” she said. She knew from the observation work she’d done that those were anger’s tension spots for her, a cue to pay attention.

“我感觉脖子和下巴有点紧，”她说。她从之前的观察工作中得知，这些部位是她生气时容易紧张的地方，需要特别注意。

In contrast to the overreactiveness of many blackmailers, which we saw in Chapter 5 , many targets of emotional blackmail tend, like Leigh, to underr eact. That means they often minimize their uncomfortable feelings, denying that anything is bothering them and using rationalizations to persuade themselves that their objections to other people’s requests are groundless.

与第五章中我们看到的许多勒索者反应过度的情况相反，许多情感勒索的受害者，比如莉，往往反应不足。这意味着他们常常会淡化自己的不适感，否认自己有任何困扰，并用各种理由来说服自己，他们对别人要求的反对毫无根据。

I suggested to Leigh that in the process of looking at what her mother wanted from her she could ask some additional questions to help make her more aware of her habitual ways of responding. I certainly don’t suggest that you put every transaction under a microscope—there’s no need to overanalyze everything and remove all spontaneity from your dealings with other people. But if you’ve experienced discomfort and emotional bullying in a relationship, it’s important to use a more critical eye than you would in other circumstances. If you think that you may be an underreactor, I suggest that you ask yourself:

我建议莉在思考母亲对她的期望时，可以多问一些问题，帮助她更好地了解自己习惯性的回应方式。我当然不是建议你把每件事都放在显微镜下仔细审视——没必要过度分析，也不需要完全扼杀与人交往中的自发性。但是，如果你在一段关系中感到不适或遭受情感霸凌，那么比起其他情况，更需要用批判的眼光去看待问题。如果你觉得自己可能反应过度，我建议你问问自己：

  • Is a pattern developing here?
    这其中是否正在形成某种模式？
  • Do I seem to be in the habit of saying “It’s no big deal,” “No problem,” “I don’t have a preference” or “I don’t care”?
    我是否经常说“没什么大不了的”、“没问题”、“我没有偏好”或“我不在乎”？
  • If it were entirely up to me, what would I do?
    如果完全由我决定，我会怎么做？
  • Is my body telling me something different from what my mind is telling me? (For example, you’re thinking: It’s only a movie, so even though I don’t feel like it, I’ll go—but you notice that your stomach is pumping more acid than usual.)
    我的身体发出的信号和我的大脑发出的信号不一致吗？（例如，你心想：这只是一部电影，所以即使我不想去，我也会去——但你注意到你的胃酸分泌比平时多。）

If you answer yes to these questions, it’s time to take a stand and express your own desires. You may decide to say yes, but you need to identify the elements of the demand that are troublesome to you and make a decision to tell the other person about them. Give yourself permission to say “I don’t want to” or “I don’t feel like it” without feeling that you have to give elaborate explanations. Don’t question your right to say no to something that seems relatively unimportant. Standing up for yourself on the small issues will give you an opportunity to develop the skills you need to hold fast if or when the stakes are higher.

如果你对这些问题的回答是肯定的，那么是时候表明立场，表达自己的意愿了。你或许会选择答应，但你需要找出哪些要求让你感到困扰，并决定是否要告诉对方。允许自己说“我不想”或“我没心情”，而不必给出冗长的解释。不要质疑自己对看似无关紧要的事情说“不”的权利。在小事上坚持己见，能让你有机会培养在更重要的事情上也能坚定立场的能力。

Keep in mind that sometimes what’s most objectionable about a demand is the way it is presented. Sometimes style is substance, and we can’t ignore it. Leigh said:

请记住，有时最令人反感的要求恰恰是它的表达方式。有时形式即实质，我们不能忽视这一点。莉说：

I don’t care — really!—about taking Mom out. What pisses me off is the way she got me to say yes. I hate being compared to Caroline, and I’d like her to stop it.

我真的不在乎带妈妈出去。让我生气的是她哄骗我答应的方式。我讨厌别人拿我和卡罗琳比较，我希望她别再这样了。

The pressure blackmailers use can feel insulting, grating or demeaning, and it’s vital not to minimize it or let it pass just because the issue on the table seems insignificant and you’re not planning to object to it. In Leigh’s case, it was most important to call her mother’s attention to how resentful the negative comparisons made her feel. Yes, she could take Ellen to dinner because the action itself wasn’t a problem, but she needed to explain to her mother how to ask for time with her without using emotional blackmail.

勒索者施加的压力会让人感到侮辱、刺耳或有损尊严，因此，切勿轻视或置之不理，即便问题看似无关紧要，或者你并不打算反对。就莉而言，最重要的是让她母亲意识到，那些负面的比较让她感到多么愤恨。没错，她可以带艾伦去吃饭，因为这件事本身并没有错，但她需要向母亲解释，如何才能在不使用情感勒索的情况下，请求与母亲共度时光。

Conscious Compliance

有意识的服从

Conscious compliance is the yes you choose after thinking about what another person wants and after you have disabled the mechanisms of automatic compliance by observing and becoming aware of your thoughts, feelings and preferences. Used appropriately, conscious compliance can be the best way to achieve the results that are most important to you. But remember that this form of compliance is the result of a careful reflective process. It follows from the Stop, Observe, Explore steps I’ve described.

有意识的顺从是指在思考他人需求，并通过观察和觉察自己的想法、感受和偏好，抑制自动顺从机制之后，才选择“是”。如果运用得当，有意识的顺从可以成为达成对你而言最重要的结果的最佳途径。但请记住，这种顺从是经过深思熟虑的反思过程的结果，也是我之前提到的“停止、观察、探索”步骤的必然结果。

Conscious compliance is a good choice when:

在以下情况下，自觉遵守规则是一个不错的选择：

• You examine the demand and find that it has no negative impacts. Perhaps it was delivered with whining or mild sulking, but none of the behaviors that accompany it are habitual, and you and the other person are not frozen in a blackmail pattern. The other person may want you to do something you regard as boring or tedious, but it’s not harmful to anyone. You can look at your decision to say yes as part of the natural give and take of a good relationship, an expression of generosity that is likely to be returned.

• 你仔细审视了对方的要求，发现它并无负面影响。或许对方在提出要求时带着些许抱怨或轻微的闷闷不乐，但这些行为都不是习惯性的，你和对方之间也没有陷入勒索的模式。对方可能想让你做一些你觉得无聊或乏味的事情，但这并不会伤害任何人。你可以把答应这件事看作是良好关系中自然而然的互惠互利，一种慷慨的表达，而这种慷慨很可能会得到回报。

• You examine the demand and find that it will have no negative impact as long as it involves an even trade with the blackmailer. You will comply this time, but the blackmailer agrees to let you make an equivalent decision next time. For example, I pick this year’s vacation spot, you pick next year’s. I’m not suggesting that you keep score or reduce your exchanges with a friend, colleague or loved one to “I gave you your way twice and you only did what I wanted once, so you owe me.” But if you look back over your recent dealings with another person and realize that you are doing most of the compromising, you are witnessing the beginnings of a power imbalance. It’s important to address it before it becomes entrenched.

• 你仔细审视了对方的要求，发现只要双方能进行公平的交换，就不会产生任何负面影响。这次你会答应，但勒索者同意下次让你做出同等的选择。例如，今年我选度假地点，明年你选。我并不是建议你斤斤计较，或者把与朋友、同事或爱人的交往简化成“我两次都顺从了你，你只按我说的做了一次，所以你欠我的”。但如果你回顾最近与他人的交往，发现自己一直在做出妥协，那么你就看到了权力失衡的苗头。在它根深蒂固之前，及时解决至关重要。

• You examine the demand and find that you can say yes willingly, and without harm to yourself or others, but only to parts of it. When this is the case, conscious compliance involves striking a deal—saying yes to what you can. In exchange, you ask the blackmailer to drop the elements that you find disturbing.

• 你仔细审视对方的要求，发现自己可以心甘情愿地答应，而且不会伤害自己或他人，但只能答应其中的一部分。在这种情况下，有意识的顺从意味着达成某种协议——答应你能接受的部分。作为交换，你要求勒索者放弃那些让你感到不安的内容。

• You examine the demand and decide to say yes for a time—and you label your compliance as strategy. You know why you are saying yes, and you develop a plan for changing the parts of the situation that are not acceptable to you.

• 你审视了这一要求，决定暂时答应——并将这种顺从称为策略。你知道自己为什么答应，并制定了计划来改变那些你无法接受的情况。

The first two categories are fairly self-explanatory: You look at the situation and decide that saying yes is OK, something you can live with. No bad or stuffed feelings, no hidden agendas, no power imbalance, no confrontation. If you come to a compromise—your way this time, my way next time—you trust that the other person will honor it.

前两类情况很容易理解：你审视情况后认为答应是可以接受的，是可以接受的。没有负面情绪或压抑感，没有隐藏的动机，没有权力失衡，也没有冲突。如果你们达成妥协——这次按你的方式，下次按我的方式——你相信对方会遵守约定。

The other two categories are more complex, so let’s look at them in depth.

另外两类比较复杂，所以我们来深入探讨一下。

YES—WITH CONDITIONS

是的——但有条件

When Leigh considered what would make her dinner with Ellen feel less burdensome, she realized that she hadn’t given herself any options besides having dinner and spending the rest of the evening with her mother.

当莉莉思考怎样才能让她和艾伦的晚餐不那么成为负担时，她意识到除了和母亲一起吃晚饭并度过余下的夜晚之外，她没有给自己任何其他选择。

I asked Leigh if the world would come to an end if she told her mother that she could have dinner with her but that she’d be going home early.

我问莉，如果她告诉她妈妈她可以和她一起吃晚饭，但她会早点回家，世界会不会因此毁灭。

“Can I really do that?” she asked.

“我真的可以这样做吗？”她问道。

“Of course,” I told her. “What you need to tell her is that you’ve had a rough week and you can go out to dinner but you’re not coming over afterwards. And then—and this is really important—you need to say, ‘Mom, I really want you to stop comparing me to Caroline every time I say no to you about anything. It really hurts me, and it makes me feel resentful and less likely to do things with you. And I’m warning you right now that I’m going to bust you every time you do it. Deal?”’

“当然，”我告诉她。“你需要告诉她，你这周过得很艰难，你可以出去吃晚饭，但吃完饭后你不会回来。然后——这一点非常重要——你需要说，‘妈，我真的希望你不要每次我拒绝你的时候都拿我和卡罗琳比较。这真的让我很受伤，让我感到怨恨，也让我更不愿意和你一起做事。我现在就警告你，你每次再这样我都会揭穿你。明白吗？’”

Even though this solution was fairly obvious, Leigh hadn’t been able to see it. Typically, in our FOG-filled interactions with blackmailers, the obvious eludes us. That’s what makes it so important to slow down and observe. Doing so allows you to explore the vast territory that exists right outside the immediate yes that you’ve become accustomed to giving to your blackmailers. When you become clear about your decision before you respond to the blackmailer, you can find compromises that quite frequently satisfy you both.

尽管这个解决办法显而易见，但莉却一直没能看清。通常情况下，在我们与勒索者周旋时，那些显而易见的答案往往会被我们忽略。正因如此，放慢脚步、仔细观察才显得尤为重要。这样做能让你探索出在你习惯性地对勒索者说“是”之外的广阔领域。当你能在回应勒索者之前明确自己的决定时，你就能找到双方都能接受的折中方案。

WHEN THE STAKES ARE HIGHER

当风险更高时

When we look carefully at what’s being asked of us, we may see that saying yes is indeed a big deal. Although it may not be a major crisis, acceding would violate our standards, our sense of what’s right and our self-respect. Even before we know this intellectually, our discomfort level starts to rise and we feel uneasy. Something about the demand goes against our grain. And on some level, we know we can’t be complacent.

当我们仔细审视对方的要求时，或许会发现答应其实意义重大。虽然这可能算不上什么大危机，但答应却会违背我们的原则、是非观和自尊。即便我们尚未从理智上意识到这一点，不适感便会开始上升，让我们感到不安。这种要求似乎与我们自身的本能相悖。某种程度上，我们知道自己不能逆来顺受。

Like many of us, Zoe was quite good at rationalizing her objections and uneasiness. But when she took the time to look closely at what Tess was asking of her, she realized that the arguments she was using just weren’t holding up.

和我们许多人一样，佐伊很擅长为自己的反对意见和不安情绪找到合理的解释。但当她仔细思考苔丝的要求时，她意识到自己之前的理由根本站不住脚。

She says she can do it, but I know she wants more responsibility than she can handle. Yet as a friend, and as a boss, I want to give her a chance. That’s what’s pulling me apart. I don’t want to let her down or be uncaring, but I’m worried about putting her on a big account because it’s so important to the company. I thought I was just being a perfectionist, but the bottom line is that this is just no place for beginners. I guess that’s the thing—these questions about if this is going to hurt anyone. It could hurt me a lot if we can’t do good work for this new client, and it could make a lot of other people look bad.

她说她能做到，但我知道她想承担的责任超出了她的能力范围。然而，作为朋友，也作为老板，我都想给她一个机会。这让我很纠结。我不想让她失望，也不想显得冷漠无情，但我又担心把这么重要的客户交给她，因为这对公司来说至关重要。我原以为自己只是个完美主义者，但说到底，这里真的不适合新手。我想，问题就在这里——我一直在想，这样做会不会伤害到别人。如果我们不能为这个新客户做好工作，我会受到很大的打击，而且也会让很多人蒙羞。

When you evaluate a blackmailer’s demand, even a simple question like “Will saying yes hurt me or anyone else?” can help you look beyond the blackmailer’s myopic interpretation of a situation. When Zoe did this, she knew she couldn’t say yes to Tess without compromising her professional and personal integrity. She’d have to take a stand.

当你评估勒索者的要求时，即使是像“答应她会伤害我或其他人吗？”这样简单的问题，也能帮助你超越勒索者对情况的短视解读。佐伊这样做时，她知道如果答应苔丝，就会损害她的职业操守和个人诚信。她必须表明立场。

What Money Can’t Buy

金钱买不到的东西

Jan was mightily tempted by what seemed to be the great bargain her sister offered. She could give Carol a thousand dollars, and in return, she’d be part of the family she wanted so much.

简被姐姐提出的看似诱人的交易深深吸引。她可以给卡罗尔一千美元，作为交换，她就能成为她梦寐以求的家庭的一份子。

You know, if there was the smallest chance that this loan could bring us closer together, I think it would be worth it. I know it’s a long shot given my history with Carol, but maybe she’s changed—maybe it’ll be OK this time. And I’d be helping her kids. The most I could lose is a thousand dollars — that’s not so much.

你知道，如果这笔贷款哪怕只有一丝可能让我们关系更亲近，我觉得也值得。我知道鉴于我和卡罗尔的过往，这希望渺茫，但也许她已经改变了——也许这次会没事的。而且我还能帮帮她的孩子们。我最多也就损失一千美元——那不算什么。

For Jan, a thousand dollars was a lot of money, but it wouldn’t break her to lend it, even if she never saw it again. What she couldn’t afford to lose was her integrity. “I have to make up my mind right now, so don’t talk to me about integrity,” she wailed. “Carol’s telling me they’re going to be out on the street. No offense, but this touchy-feely stuff is totally irrelevant.”

对简来说，一千美元是一笔巨款，但即使再也拿不回来，借出去也不会让她破产。她最不能失去的是她的正直。“我现在必须做决定，所以别跟我谈什么正直，”她哭喊道。“卡罗尔告诉我她们要流落街头了。别介意，但这些感性的话语根本无关紧要。”

“I’m sure it seems that way when you’re under this kind of pressure,” I told her, “but indulge me. Just go through this list and see if you still think it’s irrelevant.”

“我知道在这种压力下你会这么想，”我告诉她，“但请允许我这么说。你仔细看看这份清单，再决定是否还觉得它无关紧要。”

To help Jan see what a nebulous concept like integrity had to do with her decision about helping Carol, I asked her to answer the following questions. Many people find them helpful when they feel a worrisome buzz around a request but can’t pinpoint what’s bothering them, or when they want to assess the real cost of a decision.

为了帮助简理解像诚信这样模糊的概念与她是否帮助卡罗尔的决定有何关联，我请她回答以下问题。许多人发现，当他们对某个请求感到不安却又说不清究竟是什么困扰着自己，或者想要评估某个决定的真正代价时，这些问题会很有帮助。

If I say yes to the request:

如果我同意这个请求：

  • Am I taking a stand for what I believe in?
    我是否在坚持自己的信念？
  • Am I letting fear run my life?
    我是否让恐惧主宰了我的生活？
  • Am I confronting people who have injured me?
    我是否在与伤害过我的人对峙？
  • Am I defining who I am rather then being defined by other people?
    我是在定义自己，而不是被别人定义吗？
  • Am I keeping the promises I’ve made to myself?
    我是否信守了对自己许下的承诺？
  • Am I protecting my physical and emotional health?
    我是否在保护我的身心健康？
  • Am I betraying anyone?
    我背叛了谁吗？
  • Am I telling the truth?
    我说的都是真话吗？

You may notice that these questions are based on the components of integrity. They’re an effective way to reveal how and where we are not being true to ourselves. Jan found several of the questions sobering.

你可能会注意到，这些问题都基于诚信的构成要素。它们能有效地揭示我们在哪些方面、哪些行为违背了自我。简发现其中几个问题令人深思。

Am I confronting someone who’s injured me? . . . That was like cold water in my face. Because I think of Carol as someone who’s really hurt me in the past. She’s hurt a lot of people, but no one ever tells her. Then I got to the one about keeping promises to myself. The fact is, after our last big blowout about money, I swore that I wouldn’t let her keep pushing me around. She’s just not trustworthy when it comes to money. And the most awful question was about telling the truth. Carol hasn’t changed, and neither has our family. It’s just not real to think that I can wave a magic wand, write Carol a big check and we’ll be all warm and fuzzy and happy. Am I betraying anyone if I do it? Yes. Myself.

我这是在质问一个伤害过我的人吗？……这话就像一盆冷水浇在我脸上。因为我觉得卡罗尔过去真的伤透了我的心。她伤害过很多人，但没人告诉过她。然后我问到了关于信守对自己的承诺的问题。事实上，上次我们因为钱大吵一架之后，我发誓不会再让她摆布我。在钱的问题上，她根本不可信。而最可怕的问题是关于说实话。卡罗尔没变，我们家也没变。我根本无法想象自己能挥动魔法棒，给卡罗尔开一张大支票，然后我们就能从此过上幸福美满的生活。如果我这么做了，是不是背叛了谁？是的，背叛了我自己。

Jan was silent for a few moments. Then she asked,

简沉默了一会儿，然后问道：

How could it be so easy to put all that aside and pretend it never happened? That’s more depressing than the fact that I was ready to throw a thousand dollars down the toilet.

怎么能这么容易就把这一切都抛到脑后，假装它从未发生过呢？这比我差点把一千美元扔进马桶更令人沮丧。

When someone asks to borrow money, it usually appears to be a question of whether you can afford to lend it and whether the other person is trustworthy. But money is never just money among intimates. It’s a powerful symbol of love, trust, competence, who wins and who loses. Friends and relatives at different levels of achievement or monetary success frequently have seething envies and resentments toward one another that severely contaminate their relationships. It’s also very common for people, especially family members, to get set in rigidly defined roles around money: the rescuer, the family hero, the irresponsible and reckless child.

当有人向你借钱时，你通常会考虑自己是否有能力借出去，以及对方是否值得信任。但在亲密关系中，金钱绝不仅仅是金钱。它象征着爱、信任、能力，以及输赢。朋友和亲戚之间，如果成就或经济状况不同，往往会产生强烈的嫉妒和怨恨，严重损害彼此的关系。此外，人们，尤其是家庭成员，常常会围绕金钱设定一些固定的角色：救世主、家庭英雄、不负责任的鲁莽之徒等等。

Jan realized that this had happened in her family. Now she was able to make her decision based on new knowledge and awareness. She decided to say no to Carol because she saw that if she gave in to Carol’s emotional blackmail, she would be using money to try to buy something that didn’t exist. Further, she would be enabling her sister to continue to be reckless with money, which her family had done for years. (I reminded her that this kind of blackmail isn’t usually an isolated incident. One request for money usually leads to another.) And most important, she’d have to deny hard-learned truths and break important promises to herself, compromising her self-respect. The cost to her integrity would be much higher than a thousand dollars.

简意识到这种事也发生在她家。现在，她能够根据新的认知和意识做出决定。她决定拒绝卡罗尔，因为她明白，如果屈服于卡罗尔的情感勒索，她就等于用钱去买根本不存在的东西。而且，她还会助长妹妹挥霍无度的风气，而她的家人多年来一直如此。（我提醒她，这种勒索通常不是孤立事件。一次要钱往往会引发另一次。）最重要的是，她将不得不否认自己苦苦领悟的真理，违背自己对自己的重要承诺，损害自己的自尊。她为此付出的代价远不止一千美元。

Intimacy with Integrity

亲密而正直

The sexual arena is one in which people frequently founder when they run into differing expectations or pressure. There’s no place where we’re more vulnerable or emotionally naked, and no place where we so want to be accepted—and accepting. If we don’t let the other person know what pleases us and what doesn’t, what arouses us and what makes us uncomfortable, we can’t have genuine intimacy. Yet we don’t want to offend or be rigid or closed to playing and experimenting. We know that different people have different levels of comfort and desire, and we want to honor those. We also know the power of sex to attract someone we want, and we know how easy it is to manipulate another person by withholding it. If we’re not careful, we wind up making decisions about sex based on all the wrong reasons: To prove we’re desirable. To show how free, liberated or spontaneous we are. To assert our claim on the other person. To punish. To escape from FOG.

在性领域，人们常常因为彼此期望不同或面临压力而感到困惑和不知所措。没有哪个地方比这里更让我们脆弱、更袒露心扉，也没有哪个地方比这里更让我们渴望被接纳——同时也渴望接纳他人。如果我们不让对方知道什么让我们愉悦、什么让我们不适，什么能唤起我们的欲望、什么会让我们感到不舒服，我们就无法建立真正的亲密关系。然而，我们又不想冒犯对方，也不想显得僵化、固执，更不想拒绝尝试和探索。我们知道，不同的人有不同的舒适度和欲望，我们也想尊重这些差异。我们也知道，性能够吸引我们心仪的人，我们也知道，通过拒绝性来操控他人是多么容易。如果我们不小心，最终会基于各种错误的理由来做出关于性的决定：为了证明自己有魅力；为了展现自己的自由、解放或随性；为了宣示对对方的所有权；为了惩罚；为了逃避迷雾。

How do you make decisions in such a sensitive—and murky—area? After all, there are no hard-and-fast rules, just the ones that you and your partner agree to. You need to be clear about what you want and need and to look carefully at what’s being asked of you. Then, as in every other part of your life, you need to evaluate the impact of troublesome requests or demands on your integrity and decide what you want to do. It may seem as though questions of a sexual nature are too delicate and nuanced to be analyzed with the same kind of thoroughness we’ve used so far, but as you’ll see, they’ll easily survive the scrutiny—and so will you.

在如此敏感且模糊的领域，你该如何做决定？毕竟，没有一成不变的规则，只有你和伴侣共同认可的。你需要清楚自己想要什么、需要什么，并仔细审视对方的要求。然后，就像生活中的其他方面一样，你需要评估那些棘手的要求或规定对你自身原则的影响，并决定你的应对之策。或许你会觉得，性方面的问题过于微妙复杂，无法像我们之前讨论的那样进行全面细致的分析，但你会发现，它们经得起推敲——而你也一样。

Is This about Love?

这是关于爱吗？

Sex is all about give and take, and it’s fine to do some giving just to please the other person. For example, a man wakes up in the morning ready to make love, and his wife is sleepy and not particularly in the mood but is happy to please him. Nothing’s lost, and her integrity isn’t at stake, unless this is part of a consistent pattern of man takes, woman complies unexcitedly and without pleasure. In a good relationship between two people who are sexually compatible, going along from time to time won’t harm your integrity if it doesn’t become obligation or drudgery. Similarly, say a woman asks her lover to indulge a fantasy—“Wear your cowboy boots.” It may not be the other person’s fantasy, but in a healthy relationship, we ask for pleasure, and we offer it.

性爱讲究的是付出与接受，偶尔付出取悦对方也无可厚非。例如，一个男人早上醒来准备亲热，而他的妻子虽然睡意朦胧，兴致不高，但仍然乐意让他开心。这并无损失，她的自尊心也不会受到损害，除非这种情况是长期存在的“男人索取，女人冷漠顺从，毫无愉悦感”的模式。在一段性生活和谐的良好关系中，偶尔的顺从并不会损害你的自尊心，只要它不变成义务或苦差事。同样地，假设一个女人要求她的伴侣满足一个幻想——“穿上你的牛仔靴”。这可能并非对方的幻想，但在一段健康的关系中，我们既要寻求愉悦，也要给予愉悦。

But we need to feel free to protect ourselves when what’s asked crosses the line and feels harmful to us. Helen talked about how uncomfortable she felt about having sex with Jim one night because she felt she had to regain his affection—even though she was totally exhausted and stressed out. “It was a real low point for me,” she said. “I was just so out of it, but he was making me feel so guilty I just went along. I like sex, but this was not fun. I felt used—invisible.”

但当对方的要求越界，让我们感到受伤时，我们也要有权利保护自己。海伦谈到，有天晚上她和吉姆发生性关系时，她感到非常不自在，因为她觉得自己必须重新获得他的爱——尽管她当时已经筋疲力尽，压力巨大。“那是我人生中的低谷，”她说，“我当时完全神志不清，但他让我感到内疚，所以我只好顺从。我喜欢性爱，但这感觉一点也不好。我觉得自己被利用了——被忽视了。”

I reminded Helen that there’s a big difference between being a good sport, wanting to please the other person even though you’d rather be reading, and being pressured to have sex when you’re not feeling well or if you’re under a lot of stress. She quickly caught on to that difference. “I love Jim, but I’ve made my decision,” she said. “I’m not going to let this happen again.” Helen asked for help in holding her ground, and in the next chapter I’ll show you some responses she could give the next time she was faced with this situation.

我提醒海伦，做一个有风度的人，即使更想看书也想取悦对方，和在身体不舒服或压力很大的情况下被迫发生性关系，这两者之间有很大的区别。她很快就明白了其中的区别。“我爱吉姆，但我已经决定了，”她说，“我不会让这种事再次发生。”海伦请求我帮助她坚持自己的立场，在下一章中，我会向你展示一些她下次遇到类似情况时可以采取的应对方式。

Bullying someone into having sex when they really don’t want to, or don’t feel good, is a very unloving thing to do, and a person who’s tempted to give in under those circumstances needs to ask: Is this about love, or is it about power, control, winning and domination? If it’s about love, the other person will have some compassion for how you’re feeling. And if it’s not, it’s vital to protect your self-respect and your integrity.

强迫他人发生性关系，尤其是在对方并不情愿或感到不适的情况下，是一种极其缺乏爱意的行为。在这种情况下，如果有人想要屈服，就应该扪心自问：这是出于爱，还是为了权力、控制、胜利和支配？如果是出于爱，对方会体谅你的感受。如果不是，那么维护你的自尊和人格就至关重要。

MAJOR LIFE DECISIONS: HANDLE WITH CARE

重大人生决定：谨慎处理

When the stakes involved in a blackmailer’s demand are very high, I urge you to stretch out your decision-making process, carefully considering how each option will affect your life and your integrity. I’m talking here about major life decisions such as:

当勒索者的要求非常高昂时，我强烈建议您延长决策时间，仔细考虑每种选择会对您的生活和人格造成怎样的影响。我这里指的是一些重大的人生抉择，例如：

  • Deciding the future of a marriage or love relationship
    决定婚姻或恋爱关系的未来
  • Breaking off a close relationship with a parent, relative or friend
    与父母、亲戚或朋友断绝亲密关系
  • Deciding whether to stay in or leave an unhappy job situation
    决定是继续留在不满意的工作岗位还是离开。
  • Spending or investing a significant amount of money
    花费或投资大量资金

A compromise that preserves the relationship but removes the elements that are unacceptable to you may be perfectly appropriate if the blackmailer is willing to participate. After all, the goal here is not to replace the other person’s “My way or the highway” with your own. If you can, you’ll want to try to restore the give-and-take flow that emotional blackmail has eliminated.

如果勒索者愿意配合，那么达成一个既能维系关系又能剔除你无法接受的因素的妥协方案或许完全合适。毕竟，我们的目标并非用自己的方式取代对方的“要么听我的，要么滚蛋”。如果可以，你应该努力恢复被情感勒索破坏的互惠互利的关系。

Give yourself time to explore the blackmailer’s demands and the range of responses open to you—except when:

给自己一些时间去了解勒索者的要求以及你可以采取的各种应对措施——除非：

  • The other person is physically abusive or threatens to become so
    对方有肢体虐待行为或威胁要进行肢体虐待。
  • The other person is compulsive with alcohol, drugs, gambling or debting and refuses to acknowledge the problem or get treatment
    另一个人有酗酒、吸毒、赌博或负债成瘾的问题，并且拒绝承认问题或接受治疗。
  • The other person is involved in illegal activities
    另一方则参与了非法活动。

In these cases, you don’t have the luxury of time, and you will have to make your decision and take action quickly.

在这种情况下，你没有时间可以浪费，你必须迅速做出决定并采取行动。

Holding Patterns: Deciding Not to Decide

犹豫不决：决定不做决定

Sarah, the court reporter you met in the introduction, had wanted to marry her boyfriend, Frank, but his constant testing of her was making her feel ambivalent. When I took her through the decision-making process, she realized that certain changes needed to occur before she could feel more comfortable about marrying him.

你在引言中认识的法庭记录员莎拉一直想嫁给男友弗兰克，但弗兰克不断试探她，让她感到犹豫不决。当我引导她完成决策过程后，她意识到，在她能够更安心地嫁给他之前，需要做出一些改变。

I gave Sarah the assignment of listing what she needed from Frank and what kind of behavior she would and wouldn’t accept from him. “Is it OK if I do two lists, the ‘You moron, who do you think you are?’ list and then the real list?” Sarah asked. “I think I need to blow off some steam.”

我给莎拉布置了一项任务，让她列出她希望弗兰克为她做什么，以及她能接受和不能接受弗兰克的哪些行为。“我可以列两份清单吗？一份是‘你这个白痴，你以为你是谁？’的清单，另一份是她真正需要的清单？”莎拉问，“我觉得我需要发泄一下。”

If you’ve been stuffing feelings and talking yourself out of your anger, you’ll probably want to do the same—or find other safe ways to begin expressing your frustrations—before you focus on your list. Considering what you want and need certainly sounds like a calm, rational process, but the fact is that many emotional blackmail targets have been holding in their resentments for so long that they’re close to blowing.

如果你一直压抑自己的情绪，试图通过说服自己来平息怒火，那么在认真对待你的清单之前，你可能需要再次这样做——或者找到其他安全的方式来表达你的不满。思考自己想要什么、需要什么，听起来当然是一个冷静理性的过程，但事实上，许多情感勒索的目标人物已经积压怨恨太久，濒临爆发的边缘。

One particularly effective way to vent volatile emotions is to put an empty chair in front of you and picture the other person sitting in it. (A photograph of the person can help you do this.) Say aloud what you’ve been thinking and feeling for so long. Verbalizing your anger outside the presence of the blackmailer will release bottled-up energy and build your connection to clarity. Yelling or venting with the blackmailer most likely won’t clear the air and may instead exacerbate the hard feelings between you.

一个特别有效的宣泄情绪的方法是，在你面前放一把空椅子，想象对方坐在上面。（一张对方的照片可以帮助你做到这一点。）把你长期以来的想法和感受大声说出来。在勒索者不在场的情况下表达你的愤怒，可以释放积压的能量，让你更加清晰地了解对方。当面吼叫或发泄情绪很可能不会化解矛盾，反而会加剧你们之间的不快。

Sarah began:

莎拉开始说道：

I don’t know what’s happened to us, Frank. You treated me so well at the beginning. I thought I meant a lot to you. But love is not a test. I’m your friend, I’m your lover, maybe I’ll be your wife, and I’m outraged that there are so many strings attached to your love. What? We can’t get married because I won’t baby-sit for your sister? How dare you be that petty? How dare you value me on that basis. You can’t buy love, Frank, and I refuse to be forced into trying to buy yours. What do you think I am? How can you be such a jerk? Stop it! Just stop it!

弗兰克，我不知道我们之间到底发生了什么。一开始你对我那么好，我以为我在你心中很重要。但爱情不是考验。我是你的朋友，我是你的爱人，也许我会成为你的妻子，但我却对你的爱附加了这么多条件，这让我非常愤怒。什么？就因为我不肯帮你妹妹带孩子，我们就不能结婚？你怎么敢这么斤斤计较？你怎么敢用这种理由来衡量我？弗兰克，爱情是买不到的，我拒绝被迫去用金钱去换取你的爱。你把我当成什么了？你怎么能这么混蛋？够了！别再这样了！

Sarah was breathing hard when she finished. She smiled, turned to me and said, “OK. Now I’m ready to do my list.”

莎拉说完后气喘吁吁。她笑了笑，转过身对我说：“好了，现在我可以开始列清单了。”

I told Sarah that in laying out what we want in a relationship, we’re not trying to control the situation. We’re really saying “This is what would make the relationship more fulfilling to me.”

我告诉莎拉，当我们阐明对一段感情的期望时，我们并不是想控制局面。我们真正想表达的是“对我来说，怎样才能让这段感情更加充实”。

Sarah developed the following list for herself and Frank:

莎拉为自己和弗兰克列出了以下清单：
