1: No more testing to prove my feelings for you. You either want to marry me or you don’t. I love you, and I want to marry you, but I’m no longer going to jump through hoops to prove it to you. If you’re that unsure of me, talk to me and we’ll work it out.

1：我不会再用各种方式来证明我对你的感情了。你要么想娶我，要么不想。我爱你，也想娶你，但我不会再费尽心思去证明这一点。如果你真的对我没把握，那就跟我谈谈，我们一起解决。

2: I love you, and I want to expand my business. One does not preclude the other, and the two things can coexist. If they can’t in your mind, then there is something fundamentally wrong between us, and we’d better find it out now rather than later.

2：我爱你，我也想拓展我的事业。这两件事并不冲突，它们可以并存。如果你认为它们不能并存，那么我们之间就存在根本性的问题，我们最好现在就找出问题所在，而不是以后。

3: I need you to stop using my resistance to giving you your way about everything as evidence that I’m not committed to you. One has nothing to do with the other.

3：我希望你不要再把我不愿事事顺从你当作我对你不忠的证据。这两件事根本没有关系。

4: If you want something from me, ask for it, and I’ll do everything I can to please you if what you want is OK with me. But I need to be able to say no about some things without you making me feel like a serial killer.

4：如果你想从我这里得到什么，就直接说，只要你同意，我会尽我所能让你满意。但我需要有拒绝某些事情的权利，而你又不能让我觉得自己像个连环杀手。

“I feel really good about having done this,” Sarah said, “but now I’m worried. What if he just laughs at me? What if he just says no, I can’t do that?”

“我感觉自己做这件事真的很好，”莎拉说，“但我现在很担心。万一他嘲笑我怎么办？万一他说不行，我不能那样做怎么办？”

“You won’t know until you do it,” I told her. “You can rehearse telling him by yourself until you’re comfortable, and then you can do it and watch how he reacts. Remember that you’re still collecting information. Don’t assume anything, but pay close attention. You’re making two decisions here. The first is to tell Frank what you need. And the second is to delay making a decision about the relationship until you’ve seen how Frank responds.”

“你不做怎么知道呢？”我告诉她，“你可以自己练习一下怎么跟他说，直到你觉得自在为止，然后再去跟他说，观察他的反应。记住，你还在收集信息。不要妄下结论，但要仔细观察。你现在要做两个决定。第一个决定是告诉弗兰克你的需求。第二个决定是，在看到弗兰克的反应之前，不要急于对这段关系做出决定。”

Defusing a Marriage Crisis

化解婚姻危机

Liz had been stuffing her anger for years, and overreacted dramatically when Michael got upset at her desire to go back to work. Both of them had resorted to threats—Liz’s to leave the marriage and Michael’s to take the twins away from her and leave her penniless. As she looked at what Michael wanted her to do—“Stay home with the kids”—she knew she couldn’t do it without giving up something vital to her sense of herself.

莉兹多年来一直压抑着自己的愤怒，当迈克尔对她想重返职场的想法感到不满时，她反应过度了。两人都动用了威胁——莉兹威胁要离开婚姻，而迈克尔则威胁要夺走双胞胎，让她身无分文。当她看到迈克尔想要她做的事——“待在家里带孩子”——她知道，如果她不放弃对她而言至关重要的东西，她根本做不到。

I suggested to Liz that she write a letter to Michael, telling him how she felt and once again describing what she needed. If she felt apologies were due, she could make them, and I urged her to use the same kind of nonattacking approach that Sarah used in describing what she wanted from Frank.

我建议莉兹给迈克尔写封信，告诉他自己的感受，并再次说明她的需求。如果她觉得应该道歉，可以自己道歉。我还敦促她像莎拉描述她对弗兰克的期望时那样，采用不带攻击性的方式。

Writing a letter to a blackmailer, especially when the situation between you has markedly deteriorated, is a safe way to express yourself. It’s a way of keeping yourself from getting so anxious that you forget what you want to say, and it helps you focus on what the key issues are for you. Think of it as a way to find grace under pressure.

给勒索者写信，尤其是在你们之间的关系明显恶化的情况下，是一种安全的表达方式。它可以避免你焦虑到忘记自己想说什么，并帮助你专注于对你而言最重要的问题。把它看作是在压力下找到平静的一种方式吧。

Here’s what Liz wrote to Michael:

以下是莉兹写给迈克尔的信：

Dear Michael,

亲爱的迈克尔：

I have decided to write my thoughts and feelings instead of trying to express them directly to you for several reasons. The most important one is that I have become very afraid of your anger whenever I try to discuss our situation with you. Now that you have started threatening me with terrible consequences if I decide to divorce you, I am even more afraid. I get all jumbled up in my mind at those times, and I can’t think clearly, and I know I don’t express myself adequately. For one thing, you constantly interrupt and cut me off when I say something you don’t want to hear. By putting what I want to say on paper, I have the chance to organize my thoughts and to state them clearly.

我决定把我的想法和感受写下来，而不是直接跟你表达，原因有很多。最主要的是，每次跟你谈起我们之间的问题，我都会非常害怕你的愤怒。现在你开始威胁我说，如果我决定离婚，后果不堪设想，我更加害怕了。每当这时，我的思绪都会变得混乱，无法清晰地思考，我知道自己无法很好地表达自己。一方面，每当我说到你不想听的话时，你总是打断我，让我无法继续说下去。把我想说的话写下来，我才有机会整理思路，清晰地表达出来。

My hope is that you will read this letter through and then we can sit calmly and talk about things rationally and without a win-lose atmosphere.

我希望你能仔细阅读这封信，然后我们就可以冷静地坐下来，理性地、不带输赢观念地谈论这些事情。

Michael, I don’t want to leave you if there is any chance that we can rebuild our relationship and get it onto a healthier, more loving and equal plane. I still have a lot of love for you despite how much you have hurt me in the last few years, and I know you do for me as well. You can be the most terrific guy in the world (as well as the sexiest), but if I’m going to stay, I need you to take 50 percent of the responsibility for what’s gone wrong and do 50 percent of the work to get us back on track.

迈克尔，如果还有一丝机会重建我们的关系，让它回到更健康、更充满爱意、更平等的状态，我不想离开你。尽管过去几年你伤我很多，但我依然深爱着你，我知道你也一样。你可以是世界上最棒的男人（也是最性感的男人），但如果我要留下，你需要承担一半的责任，付出一半的努力让我们重回正轨。

I promise to do the same. In fact, I’ll start right now. I know that I overreacted when you had a cow about my going back to school, and I know that my talking about divorce and seeing a lawyer had a lot to do with you getting so angry and threatening with me. So we both added fuel to the fire and neither one of us talked about how we really felt. I was determined to show you that you couldn’t control my life and I take full responsibility for handling it so badly. I’m really sorry.

我保证以后也会这样做。事实上，我现在就开始。我知道你因为我重返校园而大发雷霆时，我的反应过度了；我也知道我谈论离婚和咨询律师让你如此生气，甚至威胁我，都是我反应过激的原因。我们都火上浇油，谁也没有坦诚地表达自己的真实感受。我当时一心想让你明白你无法掌控我的人生，我愿为自己处理得如此糟糕承担全部责任。我真的很抱歉。

Until I started seeing Susan I didn’t have a term for what was going on between us, but I do now. It is called “emotional blackmail” and it started with us a long time ago. I knew that your “little punishments” like unhooking the garage door opener were insulting and childish, but they seemed minor in comparison to all the good things we had together. I realize now that part of my 50 percent of the responsibility is my failure to let you know how demeaning that behavior was or to let you know that it was not acceptable. Now that the blackmail has escalated to the point of dire threats to try and keep me in line, there must be some major changes or I cannot continue in this marriage.

在认识苏珊之前，我一直不知道该如何形容我们之间发生的一切，但现在我知道了。这叫做“情感勒索”，而且它在我们之间由来已久。我知道你那些“小惩罚”，比如拔掉车库门遥控器，既侮辱人又幼稚，但和我们共同拥有的美好时光相比，这些似乎微不足道。现在我意识到，我也有50%的责任，那就是我没有让你知道这种行为有多么侮辱人，也没有让你知道这是不可接受的。如今，这种勒索已经升级到你用可怕的威胁来控制我的地步，我必须做出重大改变，否则我无法继续这段婚姻。

I am working hard in therapy to rebuild my self-respect, and I am learning a lot about what it was in me that allowed me to accept emotional blackmail for so long. But I can’t do it all by myself. I know how much you like getting to the point and problem-solving, so let me tell you what needs to happen from my point of view if we are to have any chance of salvaging what was once a good relationship.

我正在努力接受心理治疗，重建自尊。我也在努力了解自己内心深处究竟是什么让我长期以来一直忍受情感勒索。但我无法独自完成这一切。我知道你喜欢直奔主题、解决问题，所以，让我从我的角度告诉你，如果我们想要挽救这段曾经美好的关系，需要做些什么。

1: The bullying and threats must stop immediately. That is not negotiable. I know that you can’t take all the money and the kids, so save your breath! If you are angry with me or frightened about the possibility of my leaving you, you can tell me that, but I will not permit you to treat me like a naughty child, and I will leave the room and the house if necessary if you continue to do so. (Michael, I don’t know if you can do that on your own, and I would be ecstatic if you would get some professional help to deal with whatever is causing you to act this way and to learn how to manage your anger.)

1：欺凌和威胁必须立即停止。这一点没有商量的余地。我知道你不可能既要钱又要孩子，所以省省力气吧！如果你生我的气，或者害怕我离开你，你可以告诉我，但我绝不允许你把我当成淘气的孩子对待。如果你继续这样，必要时我会离开房间，离开家。（迈克尔，我不知道你能不能自己做到这一点，如果你能寻求专业人士的帮助，解决导致你这种行为的原因，并学习如何控制你的愤怒，我会非常高兴。）

2: I want to set aside some private time each evening after the kids are asleep for us to talk to each other respectfully and with kindness. We both have grievances, and I certainly don’t expect things to change overnight, but we need to talk them out and find some compromises and solutions.

2：我希望每天晚上孩子们睡着后，我们能抽出一些私人时间，好好地、尊重地、友善地谈谈。我们俩都有不满，我当然不指望事情一夜之间就能改变，但我们需要开诚布公地谈谈，找到一些妥协和解决办法。

3: I know that you are much more of a neat freak than I am, and that I do leave things lying around a lot. I will try to pick up after myself, but you need to relax your impossible standards a little, too, and cut me and the kids some slack. Maybe instead of punishing me you could help me.

3：我知道你比我更有洁癖，也知道我经常乱放东西。我会尽量收拾，但你也需要稍微降低一下你那不切实际的标准，对我和孩子们宽容一些。或许你可以帮帮我，而不是惩罚我。

4: No more yelling. Yelling is an insult to the soul, and besides, it reminds me of my father and scares the hell out of me.

4：别再大喊大叫了。大喊大叫是对灵魂的侮辱，而且，它让我想起我父亲，把我吓得魂飞魄散。

I hope with all my heart that these conditions are acceptable to you. I am more than willing to work with you. Susan has suggested 60 days as a trial period, and that sounds fine to me. Then we can reevaluate things and see how we both feel. Right now I’m feeling very scared but also very hopeful. I think we have a real chance to use this crisis as a wonderful springboard to a better marriage.

我衷心希望这些条件您能接受。我非常愿意与您合作。苏珊建议先试行60天，我觉得可以。之后我们可以重新评估情况，看看彼此的感受。我现在既感到害怕，又充满希望。我认为我们有机会将这场危机转化为一个契机，让我们的婚姻更加美满。

—Liz

——莉兹

Michael had been punitive and emotionally abusive, and there was no way of predicting how he’d react to Liz’s clear statement of her needs and hopes, but the letter was a positive step for Liz, regardless of the outcome.

迈克尔一直对莉兹进行惩罚和情感虐待，无法预测他会对莉兹明确表达的需求和希望作何反应，但无论结果如何，这封信对莉兹来说都是一个积极的进展。

Coping on the Job

应对工作中的挑战

When emotional blackmail comes up on the job, especially when it involves a superior, it can feel like an insurmountable problem. “Boss from hell” stories are legion, and all the worse because they involve such a great power imbalance. At the back of our minds is the knowledge that our livelihood is in the hands of our blackmailer, and we cede our power to the keeper of the paycheck. Just as in romantic relationships, we may let instances of workplace blackmail pass unremarked on, allowing them to escalate until the only option we feel we have is to leave.

当职场中出现情感勒索，尤其当勒索者是上级时，往往会让人感到束手无策。“恶老板”的故事不胜枚举，而更糟糕的是，这往往意味着巨大的权力失衡。我们内心深处明白，自己的生计掌握在勒索者手中，我们不得不将权力拱手让给掌管薪水的人。就像恋爱关系一样，我们可能会对职场勒索视而不见，任其升级，直到我们觉得唯一的选择就是离开。

EXPANDING YOUR OPTIONS

拓展您的选择

Kim, the magazine editor, felt that she was under siege.

杂志编辑金感觉自己被围困了。

I’ve had it. I spend my life at my desk with my hands surgically attached to my computer and phone. I’m so exhausted I can hardly think straight, and Ken just won’t stop with the negative comparisons. I feel like he’s holding me up to impossible standards. I’m not a workaholic like some of my coworkers, and if I don’t keep cranking at top speed, I’ll be working my way off his good list and onto the marginal list—in danger the next time this crazy company decides to downsize again.

我受够了。我整天坐在办公桌前，双手仿佛被手术钉在电脑和手机上。我累得精疲力竭，几乎无法集中精力思考，而肯却不停地拿我和别人做比较。我觉得他给我设定的标准根本不可能达到。我不像某些同事那样是工作狂，如果我不继续拼命工作，就会被他从“好员工”名单里除名，进入“边缘员工”名单——等着这家疯狂的公司下次裁员的时候，我就危险了。

There’s nothing I can do except look for another job. But I’m worn down physically and emotionally, and all I can do when I get home is try not to burst into tears or yell at somebody who doesn’t deserve it. I can’t quit, because we need the money. I never used to believe in hell, but I do now.

除了另找工作，我别无选择。但我身心俱疲，回到家后只能努力克制自己，不让自己崩溃大哭，也不让自己对不该受气的人发火。我不能辞职，因为我们需要钱。我以前从不相信有地狱，但现在我相信了。

Clearly, something had to change for Kim. The demands of her job were endangering her physical and mental health, yet she’d made a decision—“There’s nothing I can do”—that had cut her options to zero. To get unstuck, she had to make a decision to define for herself what she needed and wanted and then work, even in small, incremental ways, to make changes in her situation.

显然，金必须做出改变。工作的压力正在损害她的身心健康，但她却做出了一个决定——“我无能为力”——这让她彻底失去了选择余地。为了摆脱困境，她必须先明确自己的需求和愿望，然后努力改变现状，哪怕是从微小的、循序渐进的方式开始。

We began by looking at Ken’s demand.

我们首先研究了肯的需求。

“I don’t know how we can do this,” she said. “It’s not just one demand. It’s the whole unending series of them. He thinks I can work all the time, and I can’t.”

“我不知道我们该怎么办，”她说。“这不仅仅是一个要求，而是一连串没完没了的要求。他以为我可以一直工作，但我做不到。”

“So what would you say the demand really is?” I asked.

“那么你认为实际需求是多少呢？”我问道。

“It’s like—Do whatever I say or else.”

“就好像——要么听我的，要么就等着瞧。”

“Or else what?”

“不然呢？”

“Or else I’ll get rid of you, or at the very least I’ll say that you’re not as good as Miranda, the greatest editor who ever lived. And once I’m not essential anymore, I’m expendable. Pink slip city.”

“否则我就炒了你鱿鱼，或者至少我会说你不如米兰达，她是有史以来最伟大的编辑。一旦我不再重要，我就成了可有可无的。到时候就等着被解雇吧。”

“We’ve talked about the negative comparisons with Miranda, but what makes you think that if you don’t take on every job that Ken pressures you to take, your job will be in jeopardy?” I asked. “Has he said anything specific like that?”

“我们讨论过你和米兰达的负面比较，但你为什么认为如果你不接受肯逼你接受的每一份工作，你的工作就会有危险呢？”我问。“他有没有说过什么具体的话？”

“Not in so many words,” she said, “but it’s in the air. Everyone knows that you don’t want to fall from grace around there.”

“她虽然没明说，”她说，“但大家都心知肚明。在那儿，谁都不想失宠。”

“Have you talked to him about the problems you’re having with your arms and neck from doing all this work?” I asked.

“你有没有跟他谈过你因为工作太多而导致的胳膊和脖子疼痛的问题？”我问道。

“Are you kidding?” she said. “We’re all just cogs there.”

“你在开玩笑吗？”她说道，“我们都只是那里的齿轮而已。”

I pointed out to Kim that she seemed to be basing her responses to her boss on some fairly untested assumptions. Then I asked her to describe for herself what it was reasonable for Ken to ask of her.

我指出金似乎在用一些未经检验的假设来回应她的老板。然后我请她自己描述一下，肯对她提出的要求哪些是合理的。

Once she had a firm idea of what was reasonable, she could turn her attention to what was unreasonable, and look at what the unreasonable elements cost her and other people.

一旦她对什么是合理的有了清晰的认识，她就可以把注意力转向什么是不合理的，并看看不合理的因素给她和其他人带来了什么损失。

“For people in my job, overtime comes with the territory—this is about a 50-hour-a-week job, plus weekend reading time,” Kim said. “I know and accept that—but it’s been way more than that. I’m at about 60 or 65 hours, plus going in on weekends. At a really basic level, I hate the pressure. I hate being compared to someone else. It’s not motivating me, it’s making me feel afraid and resentful.”

“对于我这样的工作来说，加班是家常便饭——这份工作每周大约50个小时，再加上周末的阅读时间，”金说道。“我知道也接受这一点——但实际情况远不止如此。我现在每周工作大约60到65个小时，周末还要加班。说到底，我讨厌这种压力。我讨厌被拿来和别人比较。这非但没有激励我，反而让我感到害怕和怨恨。”

Finally, I asked Kim to describe what she needed and wanted. “I need to let other people do some of the work I’m doing, and I want Ken to start asking them as well as me,” she said. “He’s leaning on me too much. I feel so pressured by his negative comparisons that I need them to stop, and I want Ken to just ask me for what he wants instead of twisting my arm that way.”

最后，我请金描述一下她需要什么、想要什么。“我需要让其他人分担一些我正在做的工作，我希望肯也能开始征求他们的意见，”她说。“他太依赖我了。他总是拿我跟别人做负面比较，让我压力很大，我希望他能停止这种做法，我希望肯能直接问我他想要什么，而不是用这种方式强迫我。”

At that point I said to Kim, “You’re talking a lot about Ken. What’s your role in all of this?”

当时我对金说：“你一直在谈论肯。你在这一切中扮演什么角色？”

Kim began to think about what she needed to do. “I feel upset that I’ve let things get this bad. I know I need to learn to say no when I’m tired or hurting or when I need to have a life. It might help if I stop assuming the worst all the time, too.”

金开始思考自己需要做什么。“我很沮丧，事情竟然发展到这种地步。我知道我需要学会说‘不’，尤其是在我疲惫、受伤或者需要自己的生活时。如果我不再总是往最坏的方面想，也许会有帮助。”

When Kim thought about the reality of her situation, she could see that much of the pressure she’d felt was coming from inside rather than outside. Was Ken going to fire her if she said she needed to cut back her pace to protect her health? In all likelihood, he wouldn’t think of it. She hadn’t even mentioned the toll her work was taking on her health—all she’d been able to say to Ken was yes. But she couldn’t afford to do that now. The consequences of allowing herself to work past her limits were far too dire. She decided that what she’d thought was her only choice—to maintain the status quo—was really not an option.

金仔细思考了自己的处境后，意识到自己感受到的压力大多来自内心而非外界。如果她说需要放慢工作节奏以保护健康，肯会解雇她吗？他很可能根本不会考虑这么做。她甚至都没提过工作对健康的影响——她对肯说的只是“是”。但她现在承担不起这样的后果。如果让她超负荷工作，后果不堪设想。她意识到，之前以为的唯一选择——维持现状——其实根本行不通。

Kim was petrified of approaching Ken, but we practiced what she would say until she felt comfortable. In the next chapter I’ll show you how she presented her decision to Ken in a way that enabled them to work far more smoothly together.

金一开始很害怕和肯说话，但我们反复练习她要说的话，直到她感觉自在为止。下一章我会向你展示她是如何向肯表达自己的决定，从而使他们能够更顺利地合作。

CALL IT STRATEGY

称之为战略

If your experience has shown you that you’ll probably face unacceptable consequences if you try to approach or resist your boss, then, as long as your physical and mental health are not in jeopardy, you can still choose to go along for the time being.

如果你的经验表明，如果你试图接近或反抗你的老板，你可能会面临无法接受的后果，那么，只要你的身心健康没有受到威胁，你仍然可以选择暂时顺从。

How do you find a way to work with an employer who is an emotional blackmailer and may be irrational, have a hair-trigger temper or treat you with disdain? Most of us can’t and won’t change our personalities in order to get by, yet that may seem to be what’s asked of us. We know we need to get out of a poisonous situation, but the reality is that without money in the bank or another job offer, many people don’t have the luxury of an immediate grand exit.

如何与一位情感勒索者共事？他可能不讲道理，脾气暴躁，动不动就发火，甚至对你充满蔑视。我们大多数人既不能也不愿意为了生存而改变自己的性格，然而，这似乎正是雇主要求我们做的。我们知道自己需要摆脱这种糟糕的处境，但现实是，如果没有存款或下家，很多人根本无法立刻轰轰烈烈地离开。

The answer is to relabel your behavior strategy instead of compliance or capitulation. Doing this will dramatically diminish your feelings of victimization and hopelessness. Strategy implies that you’ve made a choice that’s part of a plan that will benefit you, and that’s exactly what it should be. Is it devious to look as if you’re complying while looking for an escape hatch? No—it’s self-preservation.

答案在于重新定义你的行为策略，而不是顺从或屈服。这样做会显著减轻你的受害者心态和绝望感。策略意味着你做出了一个对你有利的选择，而这正是它应有的样子。表面上顺从，实则寻找脱身之计，这算狡猾吗？不——这是自我保护。

Guidelines for a strategic holding pattern:

战略性按兵不动的指导原则：

1: Don’t tolerate anything that’s harmful to your health.

1：不要容忍任何对健康有害的事情。

This is one place where it’s imperative to protect yourself. You cannot choose to tolerate abuse or imperil your physical or emotional well-being.

在这里，保护自己至关重要。你不能选择容忍虐待，也不能危害自己的身心健康。

2: Decide to define your job to yourself in a different way.

2：决定以不同的方式定义自己的工作。

Instead of thinking of your workplace as “the salt mines,” focus on it as a means to an end that you choose. Tell yourself, for example, “I choose to stay in this situation until I have the financial base I need to make a change.” If you’re in a position close to the entry level, put your energy into learning all you can, and take advantage of opportunities for formal training or chances to learn from experienced colleagues. Channel the energy of your dislike for the situation into a plan to get out of it.

不要把工作场所看作是“苦不堪言的苦差事”，而是把它看作是你实现目标的途径。例如，告诉自己：“我选择继续待在这里，直到我积累了足够的经济基础来做出改变。” 如果你处于接近入门级的职位，那就把精力投入到学习中，尽可能多地学习，并抓住机会参加正规培训或向经验丰富的同事学习。把你对现状的不满转化为摆脱困境的计划。

3: Make a timetable and a plan.

3：制定时间表和计划。

I’m not suggesting that you put up with a difficult job situation indefinitely. What actions will you take to change your situation? Will you look for a new job? Take classes? Get on a promotion track? Change shifts? Save money? How much and how often? Be as specific as you can about what you need from yourself, and make a commitment to your plan.

我并不是建议你无限期地忍受糟糕的工作状况。你会采取哪些行动来改变现状？你会寻找新工作吗？参加培训课程？争取晋升？换班？存钱？存多少钱？多久存一次？尽可能具体地说明你需要做些什么，并坚持你的计划。

4: Decide to take small actions to improve your situation.

4：决定采取一些小行动来改善你的处境。

There’s no need to force a dramatic confrontation with an irrational or tyrannical boss, particularly if you’re convinced that your job is at stake. But you can take small steps to test the waters and clarify your position. Kim, for example, could interrupt her pattern of always saying yes to Ken by letting him know that she’d made important plans and wouldn’t be available at a particular time. She might be surprised to find that he was willing to work with her instead of against her. Some of the biggest bullies will collapse if you hold your ground and begin to stand up for yourself. Paradoxically, they’ll also respect you more.

没必要和不讲道理或专横跋扈的老板发生激烈冲突，尤其是在你确信自己的工作岌岌可危的情况下。你可以采取一些小步骤来试探对方的反应，并阐明自己的立场。例如，金可以打破她一贯对肯百依百顺的习惯，告诉他自己有重要的安排，在某个特定时间无法赴约。她或许会惊讶地发现，肯愿意与她合作，而不是与她作对。如果你坚持立场，开始维护自己的权益，一些最霸道的老板也会屈服。矛盾的是，他们反而会更加尊重你。

As soon as you decide to derive what benefit you can from a difficult situation, you’ll notice your stress level dropping. Remember that you’re protecting your integrity by taking care of yourself and making choices that are part of a clear strategy, rather than responding out of fear.

一旦你决定从困境中汲取益处，你就会发现压力水平有所下降。记住，你通过照顾好自己、做出符合清晰策略的选择（而不是出于恐惧而做出反应）来维护自己的尊严。

When You Know All You Need to Know

当你掌握了所有你需要知道的信息

Sometimes enough is enough. We’ve tried setting limits and expressing our needs to the other person, and we’ve learned that it just doesn’t do any good.

有时候，忍无可忍就是忍无可忍。我们尝试过设定界限，也尝试过向对方表达自己的需求，但我们发现这样做根本没用。

Maria tried for several months to work with Jay on rebuilding their relationship, but to no avail.

玛丽亚几个月来一直试图与杰伊重建他们的关系，但都无济于事。

You know I’ve given him every chance, Susan. We’ve talked and talked, and I asked him to come in for counseling with me, which he did exactly once. And he did agree to go to our minister with me—but he just lied the whole time he was there and charmed him to death.

苏珊，你知道我已经给了他很多机会。我们谈了很多次，我还邀请他和我一起去做心理咨询，但他只去了一次。他也同意和我一起去见牧师——但他全程都在撒谎，把牧师哄得团团转。

A relationship is like a pitcher of milk. Sometimes you can get it back in the refrigerator in time, but if it’s been left out too long and it goes sour, nothing will ever make it sweet again. I asked Maria if she thought that’s what had happened between herself and Jay.

一段感情就像一壶牛奶。有时候，你可以及时把它放回冰箱，但如果放得太久变酸了，就再也变不甜了。我问玛丽亚，她觉得她和杰伊之间是不是也发生了这样的事。

I’m afraid it has, and I can’t let him use me like this. Plus the kids will be stuck in this constant tension. I’m ready to snap, and when I look at them, I can see that they are too. Having a mom who’s this unhappy is bad enough, but what kind of role model is a father who lies and philanders?

恐怕就是这样，我不能让他这样利用我。而且孩子们也会一直生活在这种紧张气氛中。我感觉自己快要崩溃了，看着他们，我知道他们也一样。有个这么不快乐的妈妈已经够糟糕了，可一个满口谎言、到处拈花惹草的父亲，又能给孩子树立什么样的榜样呢？

I won’t lie to you, Susan. I’ve looked at this situation every possible way to find a way to keep the family together. It’s agonizing for me to have to take this step—I feel like I’m cutting off my arm. But I’ve realized that in the long run, this is the best thing I can do for the kids too. My life will be better, and in the long run their lives will be better too. When I calm myself down, I can see that the greatest detriment to them would be living with a father like Jay and a bitter, unhappy mother who played the martyr for them. We all need to get this poison out of our lives. It’s the only way any of us can heal.

苏珊，我不会骗你。我已经从各个角度考虑过这个问题，想尽一切办法维系这个家庭。做出这个决定对我来说无比痛苦——感觉就像要砍掉自己的一条胳膊。但我意识到，从长远来看，这对孩子们来说也是最好的选择。我的生活会因此变得更好，从长远来看，他们的生活也会因此变得更好。冷静下来之后，我明白对他们来说最大的伤害莫过于和杰伊这样的父亲，以及一个总是扮演受害者、怨恨不已的母亲生活在一起。我们都需要摆脱这种毒害。这是我们每个人疗愈的唯一途径。

I reassured Maria that from everything I’ve seen in my work with families, there’s no question that she had chosen to do what was best for her children. Parents often believe that they have to stay together “for the sake of the kids,” but I’ve found that it’s far more traumatic and destructive for children to be exposed to daily doses of hostility and despair between miserable parents than to experience the clean break of a divorce.

我向玛丽亚保证，根据我以往与家庭打交道的经验，毫无疑问，她所做的选择对孩子来说是最好的。父母常常认为他们必须“为了孩子”而维持婚姻，但我发现，对孩子而言，每天忍受痛苦父母之间的敌意和绝望，远比经历彻底的离婚更具创伤性和破坏性。

Maria had found the wisdom that would help her begin to find peace. What was left for her now was to stand by her decision.

玛丽亚找到了能帮助她获得内心平静的智慧。现在她所要做的就是坚持自己的决定。

Standing Up for Your Own Truth

捍卫你自己的真理

Roberta also concluded that a break was necessary. She couldn’t continue to stay in contact with her family.

罗伯塔也得出结论，她需要休息一段时间。她无法继续与家人保持联系。

I need them to accept and believe what I’m telling them — that my father abused me when I was a child. There’s no point in my putting down conditions for our relationship, because I’ve got years of history with these people and I know what they’ll do. They won’t accept the truth of my childhood, and they say I’m crazy unless I go along with their version. You’ve seen them for yourself, Susan, and we both know they are closed and joined together in this campaign, and I can’t give them what they want, which is agreeing to their version of reality. At least I can’t give it to them if I’m going to stay sane. So I guess it’s what you always told me — it’s them or my mental health. And I’m choosing my mental health.

我需要他们接受并相信我所说的——我小时候父亲虐待过我。我没必要为我们的关系设定条件，因为我和这些人相处多年，我知道他们会怎么做。他们不会接受我童年的真相，除非我接受他们的说法，否则他们就会说我疯了。苏珊，你亲眼见过他们，我们都知道他们在这件事上沆瀣一气，我不可能满足他们的要求，接受他们编造的现实。至少，如果我想保持理智，就不能让他们接受。所以我想，就像你一直跟我说的那样——要么选择他们，要么选择我的心理健康。而我选择我的心理健康。

Roberta decided to let her family know of her decision in a meeting with me at the hospital, a very safe environment. She had the hospital staff, a therapist and the enormous support of her whole environment to help her through a difficult time. When she had presented her decision to her family, she felt lighter, freer and saner, despite their criticisms.

罗伯塔决定在医院与我见面，告知家人她的决定。医院是一个非常安全的环境。医院的医护人员、心理咨询师以及周围所有人的巨大支持，都帮助她度过了这段艰难时期。尽管家人有所批评，但当她向他们坦白自己的决定后，她感到轻松、自由和理智。

If, like Roberta, you are dealing with abuse issues or have a history of depression or emotional fragility and have made a decision to disconnect, at least for the time being, from certain people in your life, it’s important that you have a support system in place. If you don’t have a therapist, you will want to enlist the help of people you know are really on your team—a spouse, close friend or sibling. Inform these people of your decision and let them know that you’ll be needing their help and support at this critical time of your life.

如果你像罗伯塔一样，正在经历虐待问题，或者有抑郁症或情绪脆弱的病史，并且决定至少暂时与生活中的某些人断绝联系，那么建立一个支持系统就至关重要。如果你没有心理咨询师，你需要寻求那些真正支持你的人的帮助——比如配偶、挚友或兄弟姐妹。把你的决定告诉他们，让他们知道在这个人生的关键时刻，你需要他们的帮助和支持。

There are few things more stressful than making a major life decision. Ambivalence, uncertainty, self-doubts and high anxiety are all perfectly normal mental and emotional states at these times. But keep reminding yourself that you are now being proactive instead of reactive. That in itself will help diminish the stress.

人生中没有什么比做出重大决定更让人压力山大了。此时此刻，矛盾、不确定、自我怀疑和高度焦虑都是完全正常的心理和情绪状态。但要不断提醒自己，你现在是在积极主动地应对，而不是被动反应。这一点本身就能帮助你减轻压力。

Keep using your power statement—“I can stand it”—and continue to visualize yourself moving out of the turbulent realm of emotion and becoming an observer. Both techniques will provide calm and stability during a difficult time. In addition, there are wonderful stress-reducing activities available for all of us. Meditation, yoga classes, dance classes, participating in sports and hobbies, spending time with people you have fun with—all get the endorphins flowing to increase pleasurable feelings and diminish the uncomfortable ones. And, of course, there are many good, inexpensive professional resources that you can take advantage of during this time if you need extra support.

继续使用你的自信宣言——“我能承受”——并持续想象自己从情绪的漩涡中抽离出来，成为一个旁观者。这两种方法都能帮助你在困境中保持平静和稳定。此外，我们每个人都可以参与一些绝佳的减压活动。冥想、瑜伽、舞蹈、运动和爱好、与志同道合的人共度时光——所有这些都能促进内啡肽的分泌，从而增加愉悦感，减轻不适感。当然，如果你需要额外的支持，也可以利用许多优质且价格合理的专业资源。

No matter what kind of decision you have to make, use the techniques in this chapter to stop in the midst of pressure, center yourself, and observe what’s happening and what’s being asked of you. When you make your decision based on criteria that are your own rather than those of the blackmailer, you have dealt a crippling blow to the emotional blackmail cycle. Now let’s put your decision into action.

无论你需要做出什么样的决定，都要运用本章的技巧，在压力之下停下来，让自己冷静下来，观察正在发生的事情以及对方的要求。当你基于自身而非勒索者的标准做出决定时，你就给了情感勒索的恶性循环以致命一击。现在，让我们把你的决定付诸行动。

# ↩

10

Strategy

战略

All the preparation you’ve done has been leading you here, to that moment when you tell the blackmailer your decision. I know the conflicting emotions going on inside you—the dread, the apprehension and the anxiety that so often accompany behavioral change.

你所做的所有准备都是为了让你走到今天这一步，走到你向勒索者坦白决定的这一步。我知道你内心的复杂情绪——恐惧、忧虑和焦虑，这些情绪常常伴随着行为的改变。

Now I’d like to give you some powerful strategies for stating your case and holding your ground, no matter how the other person reacts. When you practice and use the four core strategies I’ll show you in this chapter, I guarantee that you’ll change the power balance in the relationship. These strategies—nondefensive communication, making an ally out of an adversary, bartering and using humor—are the most effective tools I know for ending emotional blackmail.

现在我想教你一些强有力的策略，无论对方作何反应，都能让你清晰地表达自己的观点并坚持立场。当你练习并运用我将在本章介绍的四个核心策略时，我保证你会改变这段关系中的权力平衡。这些策略——非防御性沟通、化敌为友、以物易物以及运用幽默——是我所知的终结情感勒索最有效的工具。

I wish I could stand by your side as you tell the blackmailer your decision, but I can’t. What I can do is give you a script to learn, hold on to and fall back on when you deal with emotional blackmail.

我多么希望能够站在你身边，陪你向勒索者表明你的决定，但我不能。我能做的，是给你一份应对情感勒索的策略，让你学会运用，并在需要时可以依靠。

Please note: If you are living with or involved with someone you feel is volatile and potentially dangerous, do not inform them in advance of your plans to leave them. Protect yourself and get out. If there’s a history of physical abuse in the relationship, this is a dangerous time for you. Go someplace safe and get help, if not from family then from a shelter. Don’t go alone. Let women’s services help you, and take good care of yourself. It would be unrealistic and irresponsible of me to tell you that these strategies will work with a physically abusive person.

请注意：如果您与某人同住或交往，而您认为此人情绪不稳定且可能具有危险性，请不要提前告知对方您的离开计划。保护好自己，离开这段关系。如果这段关系中存在身体虐待史，那么现在对您来说非常危险。前往安全的地方寻求帮助，如果家人无法提供帮助，可以去庇护所。不要独自前往。让妇女服务机构帮助您，并好好照顾自己。如果我告诉您这些策略对付有身体虐待倾向的人会有效，那是不现实也不负责任的。

STRATEGY 1: NONDEFENSIVE COMMUNICATION

策略一：非防御性沟通

As we’ve seen, other people have gotten their way by yelling, sulking, playing victim, threatening and blaming. And we’ve responded by doing the best we could, using the tools we had to work with, to erect a barrier between ourselves and the feelings of fear, obligation and guilt that their behavior stirred up in us.

正如我们所见，有些人通过大喊大叫、闷闷不乐、装可怜、威胁和指责来达到目的。而我们则尽我们所能，运用我们所掌握的手段，在我们自己和他们行为在我们心中激起的恐惧、责任感和内疚感之间筑起一道屏障。

  • We’ve argued against their descriptions of us. We say: “I am not being selfish. You’re being selfish. How can you say that about me? I do everything for you. How about the time when . . .”
    我们反驳了他们对我们的评价。我们说：“我并不自私，是你们自私。你们怎么能这样说我？我所做的一切都是为了你们。想想上次……”
  • We’ve tried to read their minds when they’re suffering. We say: “Please tell me what’s wrong. What have I done? Come on, tell me what I can do to make you feel better.”
    我们试着去了解他们痛苦时的感受。我们会说：“请告诉我你哪里不舒服。我做错了什么？来吧，告诉我我该怎么做才能让你感觉好一些。”
  • We’ve tried to buy their approval in the hope that they will stop being upset with us. We say: “Well, if it upsets you that much, I can change my plans/skip my class/not take that job/not see that friend . . .”
    我们试图用金钱收买他们，希望他们不再生我们的气。我们说：“好吧，如果这让你这么生气，我可以改变计划/翘课/不去那份工作/不去见那个朋友……”
  • We’ve tried explaining, contradicting, apologizing, trying to get them to see things our way. We say: “Why can’t you be reasonable? Can’t you see how wrong you are? What you want is ridiculous/crazy/irrational/insulting . . .”
    我们已经尝试解释、反驳、道歉，试图让他们理解我们的想法。我们说：“你们为什么就不能讲点道理呢？难道你们看不出自己错得有多离谱吗？你们的要求简直荒谬/疯狂/不理智/侮辱人……”

The problem with responses like these is that they are defensive and actually raise the emotional intensity of the situation. Our attempts to protect ourselves provide the fuel.

这类回应的问题在于，它们带有防御性质，实际上会加剧局势的情绪紧张程度。我们试图保护自己的行为反而火上浇油。

What would happen if the sparks of the other person’s blame, threats and negative labels fell on damp ground? What would happen if you didn’t try to change the other person but instead changed the script? What if you responded to their pressure with statements such as:

如果对方的指责、威胁和负面标签像火花一样落在潮湿的地面上会发生什么？如果你不试图改变对方，而是改变对话的走向又会发生什么？如果你用以下这些话来回应他们的压力，又会发生什么？

  • I’m sorry you’re upset.
    很抱歉你感到难过。
  • I can understand how you might see it that way.
    我能理解你为什么会那样想。
  • That’s interesting.
    那很有意思。
  • Really?
    真的吗？
  • Yelling/threatening/withdrawing/crying is not going to work anymore and it doesn’t resolve anything.
    大喊大叫/威胁/退缩/哭泣都行不通了，也解决不了任何问题。
  • Let’s talk when you’re feeling calmer.

    And the most nondefensive response of all:


    等你冷静下来我们再谈。而最不带防御性的回应是：
  • You’re absolutely right [even if you don’t mean it].
    你说的完全正确（即使你并非真心这么想）。

These phrases are the core of nondefensive communication. Memorize them and add some of your own. Repeat them aloud until they feel comfortable. If you can, practice with a friend. It’s important to make these phrases a part of your vocabulary and keep them at the ready. Do not defend or explain your decision or yourself in response to pressure.

这些短语是有效沟通的核心。记住它们，并添加一些你自己的短语。大声重复练习，直到感觉自然流畅。如果可以，最好和朋友一起练习。重要的是将这些短语融入你的词汇库，并随时准备使用。不要在压力下为自己的决定或自身辩解或解释。

I know these phrases will feel awkward to you at first. Few of us have experience with answering another person’s barrage with a short, unemotional sentence or two. Don’t be too concerned if you find yourself tempted to elaborate on them—just don’t do it.

我知道这些话一开始会让你觉得别扭。我们当中很少有人有过用一两句简短、不带感情色彩的话来回应别人连珠炮似的说辞的经验。如果你很想详细解释，也别太担心——千万别这么做。

Nondefensive communication will work with anyone at any point in the blackmail transaction. I’ve taught it to thousands of people and used it in my own life for many years. That doesn’t mean I found it easy at first, and it certainly doesn’t mean that I get it right every time. I had the same butterflies in my stomach and the same pounding heart that almost everyone experiences, and I still get them sometimes. But I promise you that each time you use this strategy and the others I’m going to show you, it gets easier. As many startled blackmailers have discovered, without fuel from the target, the blackmail attempts that worked so well in the past fizzle.

在勒索过程中的任何阶段，对任何人采取不设防的沟通方式都有效。我教过成千上万人这种方法，自己也实践多年。但这并不意味着我一开始就觉得容易，当然也不意味着我每次都能成功。我和几乎每个人都会经历的那种紧张不安、心跳加速的感觉一样，现在偶尔还会这样。但我保证，你每次使用这种策略以及我接下来要展示的其他策略，都会变得更加轻松。正如许多受惊的勒索者所发现的那样，如果没有目标的“燃料”，过去屡试不爽的勒索手段也会失效。

Presenting a Decision Nondefensively

以非防御性方式提出决定

Josh knew that to regain his self-respect, salvage his relationship with Beth and create the possibility of having a real relationship with his father, he had to stop sneaking around and tell him of his plans to marry Beth. I encouraged him to bite the bullet and break the news to both of his parents together, to ensure that his mother would hear his decision from him directly instead of through his father’s filters. “I like the idea of using this nondefensive stuff,” he said, “but you’re going to have to help me because I don’t know what to say or how to set things up.”

乔什知道，为了重拾自尊，挽救与贝丝的关系，并创造与父亲建立真正关系的可能性，他必须停止偷偷摸摸，直接告诉父亲自己打算和贝丝结婚。我鼓励他鼓起勇气，同时告诉父母这个消息，确保母亲能直接从他口中听到这个决定，而不是通过父亲的转述。“我喜欢这种不设防的做法，”他说，“但你得帮帮我，因为我不知道该说什么，也不知道该如何安排。”

We started with some ground rules for presenting his decision. “First,” I told him, “you have to set it up so that you feel as comfortable as possible and the other person can be a receptive listener.” In presenting an important decision to another person, you want to give yourself every advantage. That means not trying to initiate a discussion when the other person is tired or stressed out or when the kids are running around the house.

我们先定了一些提交决定的基本原则。“首先，”我告诉他，“你得尽量营造一个让你感觉舒适的环境，让对方能够认真倾听。” 在向他人提交重要决定时，你要尽可能地为自己创造有利条件。这意味着不要在对方疲惫、压力大，或者孩子在家跑来跑去的时候发起讨论。

With a husband or partner, let them know you want to talk, and pick a quiet, uninterrupted time. Take the phone off the hook. If you are not living with the other person, say you want to talk, and set a time and a place. Be sure a pick a meeting place where you’re at ease. Remember that turf has energy, and it’s important not to choose a place that’s filled with ghosts of your past, or memories that will make you feel less than equal to the person you’re talking to as soon as you walk in the door.

如果是和丈夫或伴侣谈话，先告诉对方你想谈谈，然后选择一个安静、不受打扰的时间。把电话听筒拔下来。如果你和对方不住在一起，就说你想谈谈，并约定时间和地点。务必选择一个让你感到自在的地方。记住，地盘是有能量的，所以不要选择一个充满过往阴影或让你一进门就感觉不如对方的地方。

“I can call them and invite them over for coffee and dessert one evening at my place,” Josh said, “but I know it’s a hassle for them, and there are two of them, just one of me. I think I’ll be OK going over there.”

“我可以打电话邀请他们晚上来我家喝咖啡吃甜点，”乔什说，“但我知道这对他们来说很麻烦，而且他们有两个人，我只有一个人。我想我过去应该没问题。”

I asked Josh if there might be a lot of old memories at his parents’ house—pictures or objects that might evoke his childhood. “Oh, no,” he said. “It’s not where I grew up. They’ve moved into a condo, and it’s more like a hotel than our old house. Look, they’re not abusive. They’re just being narrow-minded.”

我问乔什，他父母家会不会有很多旧物件，比如照片或照片，能唤起他的童年回忆。“哦，没有，”他说。“那不是我长大的地方。他们搬进了公寓，那里更像酒店，而不是我们以前的房子。你看，他们不是虐待我，他们只是思想狭隘。”

Once you’ve specified a time and place, turn your attention to precisely what you’ll say. I suggested to Josh that he start by asking his parents to hear him out without interrupting or contradicting him, and letting them know that when he was done, they could say whatever they wanted. Then he could present his decision. Working together, Josh and I designed the following dialogue.

确定好时间和地点后，就要仔细斟酌你要说的话。我建议乔什先请父母耐心听他把话说完，不要打断或反驳，并告诉他们，等他说完后，他们可以畅所欲言。然后他就可以正式宣布自己的决定了。我和乔什一起设计了以下对话。

Dad and Mom, I need you to sit down and hear me out. This is not easy for me to say. I’ve given this a lot of thought, and because I love and respect you, I want to be honest with you and stop the unpleasantness that’s been going on between us. I want you to know that I have made a decision to marry Beth. I’m very ashamed of the fact that I’ve not been truthful with you about this for the past several months. I’ve not done it because I’m scared of you. I’m scared of your anger and disapproval. I’m scared to death right now.

爸爸妈妈，请你们坐下来听我说。这对我来说并不容易。我反复思考过，因为我爱你们、尊重你们，所以我想对你们坦诚相待，结束我们之间不愉快的局面。我想让你们知道，我已经决定要和贝丝结婚。过去几个月我一直瞒着你们，我为此感到非常羞愧。我之所以没有这么做，是因为我害怕你们。我害怕你们的愤怒和反对。我现在真的非常害怕。

Josh accomplishes a lot at the outset. He lays down his conditions for the meeting. He expresses his feelings, both those surrounding the situation and the ones coming up in the present. He acknowledges his earlier dishonesty and his desire to end it. And he announces his decision.

乔什一开始就做了很多事。他提出了会面的条件。他表达了自己的感受，包括对现状的担忧和对当下局势的思考。他承认了自己之前的欺骗行为，并表示想要结束这种行为。最后，他宣布了自己的决定。

I need you to know that there’s nothing you can say or do that’s going to change my mind. It’s my decision, and it’s my life. I’m about to find out whether being right and getting your way is more important to you than having a relationship with me. I hope to God it isn’t. I’m sorry I didn’t fall in love with a nice Catholic girl. No, dammit, I’m not sorry! And you can either accept this and be part of my new family, or you can decide not to. I love you, Dad and Mom, and I’d suggest that you take some time to decide what you want to do.

我需要你们明白，无论你们说什么做什么，都无法改变我的想法。这是我的决定，这是我的人生。我即将明白，对你们来说，坚持己见、随心所欲是否比与我建立关系更重要。我向上帝祈祷，希望答案是否定的。我很遗憾没能爱上一个善良的天主教女孩。不，该死的，我一点也不遗憾！你们要么接受这一切，成为我新家庭的一份子，要么就选择不接受。爸爸妈妈，我爱你们，我建议你们花些时间好好想想自己到底想做什么。

Josh continues to stand by his decision, giving his parents a choice of accepting it—or not. Finally, he offers a suggestion: that they not respond instantly but consider what he’s said.

乔什依然坚持自己的决定，让父母自己选择接受还是不接受。最后，他提出一个建议：他们不要立即回应，而是认真考虑一下他的话。

Anticipating Their Answers

预判他们的回答

I encouraged Josh to practice his speech as though he were an actor memorizing his lines. You can do this with another person, talk to an empty chair, or talk to a photo of the other person. It will probably feel strange, but the more you practice, the more confident you’ll feel when it comes time to sit down with a real person who has masterfully pressured you in the past.

我鼓励乔什像演员背台词一样练习演讲。你可以对着另一个人练习，也可以对着空椅子练习，或者对着对方的照片练习。一开始可能会觉得有点奇怪，但练习得越多，真正面对一个曾经让你压力倍增的真人时，你就会越自信。

If you have a number of conditions to present to the other person, it’s OK to make notes on a piece of paper and refer to them, letting the other person know that that’s what you’re doing. But please practice saying your lines aloud—not just in your head. The preparation will give you a tremendous boost.

如果你有很多条件要向对方说明，可以把它们记在纸上，并在需要时提及，同时也要让对方知道你在做什么。但请务必大声朗读你的陈述——不要只是在心里默念。充分的准备会让你事半功倍。

“I’m happy to practice,” Josh said, “but I’m not worried that much about getting through what I have to say. What I’m worried about the most is what they’re going to say. It’ll be bad enough just having to see my father at a slow boil across the table from me.”

“我很乐意练习，”乔什说，“但我并不太担心自己能不能把要说的话表达清楚。我最担心的是他们会说什么。光是看着我父亲在桌子对面慢慢生气就够难受的了。”

I helped Josh ease his anxiety about his parents’ response by role-playing with him and letting him practice answering the questions and comments he feared the most. Again, you can do this with a friend, or by yourself.

我通过和乔希角色扮演，让他练习回答他最害怕的问题和评论，帮助他缓解对父母反应的焦虑。你也可以和朋友一起做，或者自己一个人做。

“Which reaction do you think will be the hardest for you, Josh?” I asked.

我问：“乔希，你觉得哪种反应对你来说最难接受？”

“From my father I think it’ll be ‘You know this means I can’t help you with your business anymore.’”

“我觉得我父亲会说：‘你知道这意味着我不能再帮你打理生意了。’”

“And your answer?”

“你的答案是什么？”

“Fuck you! I don’t need your money!”

“去你的！我不需要你的钱！”

“Well, I think we can find something a little less provocative.”

“嗯，我想我们可以找一些不那么具有挑衅性的东西。”

“OK. How about ‘I’m sorry you feel that way. I’ve made my decision.’”

“好吧。那不如这样说：‘很抱歉你这么想。我已经做出决定了。’”

We practiced, as you might want to, with a whole series of potential replies.

我们像你一样，练习了一系列可能的回复。

Susan (as Josh’s father): “We just can’t support this marriage. I’m hurt and shocked that you lied to me.”

苏珊（扮演乔希的父亲）：“我们实在无法支持这段婚姻。你竟然对我撒谎，我既伤心又震惊。”

Josh: “I’m not proud of lying to you, Dad. I was afraid. I’m sorry you feel the way you do, but I’m going to marry Beth.”

乔什：“爸爸，我并不为对您撒谎感到骄傲。我当时很害怕。我很抱歉您这样想，但我还是要娶贝丝。”

Susan: “What will your mom say?”

苏珊：“你妈妈会怎么说？”

Josh: “I’ll bet the first thing out of her mouth is ‘What’ll happen when you have children? Will they go to Catholic school? Will you raise them in the church?’ We’re not even married yet, but Mom’s always thinking ahead.”

乔什：“我敢打赌，她开口第一句话就是‘等你有了孩子怎么办？他们会上天主教学校吗？你会让他们在教会里长大吗？’我们甚至还没结婚，但妈妈总是想得太远了。”

Susan: “And you’ll tell her . . .”

苏珊：“你会告诉她的……”

Josh: “Mom, we’ll raise them with a lot of love and we’ll teach them to be good human beings.”

乔希：“妈妈，我们会用爱抚养他们，我们会教他们成为善良的人。”

Susan (as Mom): “I want to know if they’ll be Catholic or Jewish.”

苏珊（扮演妈妈）：“我想知道他们会是天主教徒还是犹太教徒。”

Josh: “And I’ll say, ‘We’ll cross that bridge when we have kids, Mom, when it’s a reality. At this moment, that’s the last thing I’m worried about.’”

乔什：“我会说，‘妈妈，等我们有了孩子，等一切成为现实，我们再考虑这个问题吧。现在，这是我最不担心的事情。’”

When Josh actually presented his decision to his parents, he felt shaky and intensely nervous, but he stuck to his script, never allowing himself to be put on the defensive.

当乔什真正向父母提出他的决定时，他感到紧张不安，但他坚持自己的计划，始终不让自己陷入被动。

It wasn’t the smoothest encounter in the world. My heart was pounding so hard I was sure they could hear it, and I felt a little sick. I reminded myself to keep breathing, and I repeated “I can stand it” a few times. It helped, but none of this was easy. My father pulled out all the stops. First he said, “Why are you doing this to us? How could you hurt us like this?” I felt like he was stabbing me in the heart, but all I said was, “I’m sorry you see it that way, Dad.” He looked surprised, but he just kept going. Next it was “If you marry that girl, you’re no longer a member of this family. This is killing your mother.” And I said, “Dad, your threats are killing our relationship. I know you’re angry, and I know you’re upset.” Then he actually said something I’d prepared for: “I can’t believe you lied to me.” My answer was “I did it because I’m scared of you. It’s something I hope we can change.”

那次会面并不顺利。我的心跳得厉害，感觉他们都能听到，而且我有点恶心。我提醒自己要深呼吸，还反复说了几遍“我能忍受”。这确实有点用，但这一切都不容易。父亲使出了浑身解数。他先是说：“你为什么要这样对我们？你怎么能这样伤害我们？” 我感觉他像是在用刀刺我的心脏，但我只是说：“爸爸，我很抱歉你这么想。” 他看起来很惊讶，但还是继续说了下去。接着他说：“如果你娶了那个女孩，你就不是我们家的一员了。这会害死你妈妈。” 我说：“爸爸，你的威胁正在毁掉我们的关系。我知道你很生气，也知道你很难过。” 然后，他竟然说出了我预料之中的话：“我真不敢相信你竟然骗了我。” 我的回答是：“我这么做是因为我害怕你。我希望我们能改变这种状况。”

Nothing seemed to be working for him, so he switched to “After everything your mother and I have done for you . . . ,” and I said, “Dad, I’m very grateful for everything, but my gratitude does not extend to allowing you to choose who I marry.” His last-ditch attempt was to compare me to my brother, who married Catholic and had lots of nice little Catholic kids. I said, “Dad, I can’t be like Eric because I’m not Eric, I’m me.”

他似乎什么方法都不管用，于是改口说：“你妈妈和我为你做了这么多……”我说：“爸，我很感激你们所做的一切，但这并不意味着我可以任由你们决定我嫁给谁。”他最后的挣扎是拿我和我哥哥比较，我哥哥娶了个天主教徒，生了很多可爱的天主教孩子。我说：“爸，我不可能像埃里克那样，因为我不是埃里克，我是我。”

At that point, I saw he was sputtering and running out of things to say, so I did what you suggested. I said that it sounded like he needed time to think.

那时，我发现他说话断断续续，好像快要没话可说了，所以我就按你说的做了。我说，听起来他需要时间思考一下。

The last thing Dad said to me was, “You’re asking me to handle a lot. I have rules and values and beliefs that mean a lot to me, and I don’t know whether I can accept your decision or not.” I got up to go and they walked me to my car. I rolled down the window and Dad said, “Well, I always taught you to stand up for yourself, but I didn’t mean for you to do it with me.” And he kind of smiled, and I drove off.

爸爸最后跟我说的话是：“你让我承担这么多。我有很多原则、价值观和信仰，这些对我来说非常重要，我不知道我能不能接受你的决定。” 我起身要走，他们送我到车旁。我摇下车窗，爸爸说：“我一直教导你要维护自己的权益，但我没想到你还要为了我的权益挺身而出。” 他微微一笑，我开车离开了。

Josh had faced his worst fear, which was displeasing his parents. And guess what? Nobody died. The building didn’t tumble down. The world did not come to an end. It was not an enjoyable experience for him, but it left him feeling relieved and filled with self-respect.

乔什面对了他最害怕的事情——惹父母不高兴。你猜怎么着？没人死。楼没塌。世界末日也没到来。对他来说，这当然不是一次愉快的经历，但却让他感到如释重负，也让他重拾了自尊。

“I feel like I’ve grown 10 feet!” Josh told me.

“我感觉自己长高了10英尺！”乔什告诉我。

He had reclaimed integrity.

他重拾了正直。

In real life, with real people, emotions and interactions are complex, especially in a family; there are rarely Hollywood endings. I’d love to report that Josh’s family decided to embrace his new wife, but that wasn’t the case. Josh’s father decided that he didn’t want to lose his son, but so far he has not truly accepted Beth or been loving toward her. Josh has sadly realized that he doesn’t want a total break with his parents, but he needs to cut back on the amount of time they spend together because of the tension between them. His fervent hope is that they will soften their attitudes at some point, perhaps when there are grandchildren—and I hope so too. But even if they don’t, Josh has done the healthy thing. His self-respect and integrity are intact, and he’s far more able to live with himself than he was when he was being untruthful to his parents and betraying his commitment to Beth.

现实生活中，人与人之间的情感和互动是复杂的，尤其是在家庭中；很少有好莱坞式的完美结局。我很想说乔什的家人接受了他的新婚妻子，但事实并非如此。乔什的父亲不想失去儿子，但他至今仍未真正接受贝丝，也没有对她表现出任何爱意。乔什悲哀地意识到，他并不想与父母彻底断绝关系，但由于彼此间的紧张关系，他不得不减少与他们相处的时间。他衷心希望父母的态度能在某个时候有所缓和，也许等到有了孙辈——我也希望如此。但即便他们最终没有改变，乔什的做法也是明智的。他的自尊和正直得以保留，而且与之前对父母撒谎、背叛对贝丝的承诺相比，他现在更能坦然面对自己。

In some instances, parents and others close to us do come around. The important thing is what you do about you, and who you are when it’s time to take a stand.

在某些情况下，父母和其他亲近的人最终会理解你。重要的是你如何应对，以及在需要表明立场时你是怎样的人。

Handling the Most Common Responses

应对最常见的回应

Because you know the other person so well, you won’t have much trouble anticipating the kinds of responses he or she will volley back after you present your decision. But because most of us are so unpracticed in using nondefensive communication, we may not be too quick on the comeback, especially when we try to choose words that will dampen the emotion of the exchange.

因为你对对方非常了解，所以你很容易就能预料到对方在你提出决定后会作何反应。但由于我们大多数人都不擅长使用非防御性的沟通方式，我们可能反应不够迅速，尤其是在试图选择能够缓和交流情绪的措辞时。

Don’t worry about being quick—you have all the time you need to think, and it’s a good idea to allow a little silence to settle around the other person’s words before you speak. The important thing is to resist the tendency to fall back on old patterns because you feel anxious and don’t know what to say. So I’d like to give you some specific ways to answer the most common types of responses. I can’t emphasize too strongly how important it is to practice saying these statements until they feel natural to you.

别担心反应不够快——你有充足的时间思考，最好在对方说完话后稍作沉默再开口。重要的是，要克服因为焦虑不知所措而退回到旧模式的倾向。因此，我想给你一些应对最常见反应的具体方法。我必须强调，反复练习这些表达方式至关重要，直到它们成为你的自然反应。

How to respond to the other person’s:

如何回应对方的：

1: Catastrophic predictions and threats. Punishers and self-punishers may try pressuring you to change your decision by bombarding you with visions of the extreme negative consequences of doing what you’ve decided to do. It’s never easy to resist the fear that their bleak vision will come to pass, especially when the theme they’re pounding home is “Bad things will happen—and it’ll be your fault.” But hold your ground.

1：灾难性的预测和威胁。惩罚者和自我惩罚者可能会试图通过不断渲染你已决定之事的极端负面后果来迫使你改变主意。要抵挡住他们阴暗预言成真的恐惧绝非易事，尤其当他们反复强调“坏事会发生——而且都是你的错”时。但请坚持你的立场。

When they say:

当他们说：

  • If you don’t take care of me, I’ll wind up in the hospital/on the street/unable to work.
    如果你不照顾我，我最终会进医院/流落街头/无法工作。
  • You’ll never see your kids again.
    你将再也见不到你的孩子了。
  • You’ll destroy this family.
    你会毁了这个家庭。
  • You’re not my child anymore.
    你不再是我的孩子了。
  • I’m cutting you out of my will.
    我要把你从遗嘱中除名。
  • I’ll get sick.
    我会生病的。
  • I can’t make it without you.
    没有你我做不到。
  • I’ll make you suffer.
    我会让你付出代价。
  • You’ll be sorry.
    你会后悔的。

You say:

你说：

  • That’s your choice.
    这是你的选择。
  • I hope you won’t do that, but I’ve made my decision.
    我希望你不会那样做，但我已经做出了决定。
  • I know you’re very angry right now. When you’ve had a chance to think about this, maybe you’ll change your mind.
    我知道你现在很生气。等你冷静下来仔细想想，或许你会改变主意。
  • Why don’t we talk about this again when you’re less upset.
    等你情绪平静下来，我们再来谈这件事吧。
  • Threats/suffering/tears aren’t going to work anymore.
    威胁、痛苦和眼泪都不管用了。
  • I’m sorry you’re upset.
    很抱歉你感到难过。

2: Name-calling, labeling, negative judgments. It’s the most natural reaction in the world to want to defend yourself when someone starts calling you names, but it’s likely to set you up for a pointless “I am not!”/“You are too!” exchange. Instead, take a deep breath and let your feelings of fear, obligation and guilt natter away in your stomach as you move into your head. Remember that for the purposes of presenting and standing by your decision, what’s most important is not how you feel but what you say. We are changing behavior first, and later on, we’ll turn our attention to what’s going on inside you.

2：辱骂、贴标签、负面评判。当有人开始辱骂你时，想要为自己辩护是最自然的反应，但这很可能让你陷入毫无意义的“我不是！”/“你也是！”的争论。相反，深呼吸，让你的恐惧、责任感和内疚感在心中慢慢消散，然后进入你的思考。记住，为了表达和坚持你的决定，最重要的不是你的感受，而是你的表达。我们首先要改变的是行为，之后才会关注你内心的变化。

When they say:

当他们说：

  • I can’t believe you’re being so selfish. This isn’t like you.
    我简直不敢相信你竟然这么自私。这不像你。
  • You’re only thinking of yourself. You never think about my feelings.
    你只想着你自己，从来没考虑过我的感受。
  • I really thought you were different from the other women/men I’ve been with. I guess I was wrong.
    我真的以为你和其他我交往过的女人/男人不一样。看来我错了。
  • That’s the stupidest thing I’ve ever heard.
    这是我听过最愚蠢的话。
  • Everyone knows that children are supposed to respect their parents.
    人人都知道孩子应该尊重父母。
  • How can you be so disloyal?
    你怎么能如此背信弃义？
  • You’re just being an idiot.
    你真是个白痴。

You say:

你说：

  • You’re entitled to your opinion.
    你有权发表你的意见。
  • I’m sure that’s how it looks to you.
    我相信你也是这么看的。
  • That could be.
    有可能。
  • You may be right.
    你说的或许有道理。
  • I need to think about this more.
    我需要再仔细考虑一下。
  • We’ll never get anywhere if you keep insulting me.
    如果你继续侮辱我，我们永远也达不到任何结果。
  • I’m sorry you’re upset.
    很抱歉你感到难过。

3: The deadly whys and hows. The other person may demand explanations from you and want a rationale for your decision. You may be thinking that this is your big chance to say all the things you’ve wanted to say about how hurt you’ve been, how thoughtless they’ve been, how you’re mad as hell and you’re not going to take it anymore. They’re offering you the perfect opening to lay out an elaborate defense. Don’t do it!

3：致命的追问。对方可能会要求你解释，并想知道你做出决定的理由。你或许会觉得这是个绝佳的机会，可以把所有想说的话都说出来，比如你有多受伤，他们有多不体贴，你有多么愤怒，以及你再也无法忍受。他们给了你一个完美的开端，让你精心准备一套辩解。千万别这么做！

Stay focused on your purpose. You’re presenting your decision—period. Don’t get caught up in the content of your disagreement if you want to stop the blackmail process. Your disagreement is really not over where to take the vacation or whether you’ll do a favor. It’s about a pattern of behavior in which the other person needs to get his or her way and you consistently give in. Because you’re serious about breaking that pattern, don’t argue, don’t explain, don’t defend, and don’t answer a why with a because.

专注于你的目标。你只是在陈述你的决定——仅此而已。如果你想阻止对方的勒索行为，就不要纠结于争论的内容。你们的分歧并非在于去哪里度假，或者你是否愿意帮忙。而是关于一种行为模式：对方总是想方设法满足你的需求，而你却总是妥协。既然你真心想要打破这种模式，那就不要争辩，不要解释，不要辩解，也不要用“因为”来回答“为什么”。

Instead, when they say:

相反，当他们说：

  • How could you do this to me (after all I’ve done for you)?
    你怎么能这样对我（在我为你做了那么多之后）？
  • Why are you ruining my life?
    你为什么要毁了我的生活？
  • Why are you being so stubborn/obstinate/selfish?
    你为什么这么固执/顽固/自私？
  • What’s come over you?
    你怎么了？
  • Why are you acting like this?
    你为什么这样？
  • Why do you want to hurt me?
    你为什么要伤害我？
  • Why are you making such a big deal out of this?
    你为什么把这件事看得这么重？

You say:

你说：

  • I knew you wouldn’t be happy about this, but that’s the way it has to be.
    我知道你不会高兴的，但事情必须如此。
  • There are no villains here. We just want different things.
    这里没有坏人，我们只是想要不同的东西。
  • I’m not willing to take more than 50 percent of the responsibility.
    我不想承担超过50%的责任。
  • I know how upset/angry/disappointed you are, but it’s not negotiable.
    我知道你很生气/失望/难过，但这没有商量的余地。
  • We see things differently.
    我们看待事物的方式不同。
  • I’m sure you see it that way.
    我相信你也是这么想的。
  • I’m sorry you’re upset.
    很抱歉你感到难过。

Handling Silence

处理沉默

But what about the person who blackmails through anger that is expressed covertly through sulks and suffering? When they say nothing , what can you say or do? For many targets, this silent anger is far more maddening and crazy-making than an overt attack.

但如果有人用暗地里发泄愤怒，比如闷闷不乐、默默承受痛苦，以此进行勒索呢？当他们什么也不说的时候，你又能说什么、做什么呢？对许多受害者来说，这种无声的愤怒远比公开的攻击更令人抓狂、更让人崩溃。

Sometimes it seems as if nothing works with this kind of blackmailer, and sometimes nothing does. But you’ll have the most success if you stick to the principles of nondefensive communication and stay conscious of the following do’s and don’ts.

有时候，对付这类勒索者似乎什么方法都无效，有时确实如此。但如果你坚持非防御性沟通的原则，并注意以下几点，就能取得最大的成功。

In dealing with silent blackmailers, don’t :

应对沉默勒索者时，切勿：

  • Expect them to take the first step toward resolving the conflict.
    期待他们率先采取行动解决冲突。
  • Plead with them to tell you what’s wrong.
    恳求他们告诉你到底出了什么问题。
  • Keep after them for a response (which will only make them withdraw more).
    不断追问他们的回应（这只会让他们更加退缩）。
  • Criticize, analyze or interpret their motives, character or inability to be direct.
    批评、分析或解读他们的动机、性格或不善于直言的原因。
  • Willingly accept blame for whatever they’re upset about to get them into a better mood.
    主动承担他们不高兴的原因，以此来让他们心情好转。
  • Allow them to change the subject.
    允许他们转换话题。
  • Get intimidated by the tension and anger in the air.
    被空气中弥漫的紧张和愤怒气氛吓倒了。
  • Let your frustration cause you to make threats you really don’t mean (e.g., “If you don’t tell me what’s wrong, I’ll never speak to you again”).
    让你的沮丧导致你发出一些你其实并不真心的威胁（例如，“如果你不告诉我发生了什么事，我以后再也不会跟你说话了”）。
  • Assume that if they ultimately apologize, it will be followed by any significant change in their behavior.
    假设他们最终道歉，之后他们的行为将会发生重大改变。
  • Expect major personality changes, even if they recognize what they’re doing and are willing to work on it. Remember: Behavior can change. Personality styles usually don’t.
    即使他们意识到自己的行为并愿意改正，也要做好性格发生重大变化的心理准备。记住：行为可以改变，但性格类型通常不会改变。

Do use the following techniques:

请使用以下方法：

  • Remember that you are dealing with people who feel inadequate and powerless and who are afraid of your ability to hurt or abandon them.
    记住，你面对的是一群感到自卑、无力，并且害怕你伤害或抛弃他们的人。
  • Confront them when they’re more able to hear what you have to say. Consider writing a letter. It may feel less threatening to them.
    等他们更容易听进去你的话时再和他们沟通。可以考虑写信，这样他们可能感觉不那么具有威胁性。
  • Reassure them that they can tell you what they’re angry about and you will hear them out without retaliating.
    让他们放心，他们可以告诉你他们为什么生气，你会认真倾听，不会报复。
  • Use tact and diplomacy. This will reassure them that you won’t exploit their vulnerabilities and bludgeon them with recriminations.
    运用策略和外交手段。这将让他们放心，你不会利用他们的弱点，也不会用指责和攻击来重创他们。
  • Say reassuring things like “I know you’re angry right now, and I’ll be willing to discuss this with you as soon as you’re ready to talk about it.” Then leave them alone. You’ll only make them withdraw more if you don’t.
    说些安慰的话，比如“我知道你现在很生气，等你准备好了，我很乐意和你谈谈。”然后就别打扰他们。如果你不这样做，只会让他们更加疏远你。
  • Don’t be afraid to tell them that their behavior is upsetting to you, but begin by expressing appreciation. For example: “Dad, I really care about you, and I think you’re one of the smartest people I know, but it really bothers me when you clam up every time we disagree about something and just walk away. It’s hurting our relationship, and I wonder if you would talk to me about that.”
    不要害怕告诉他们他们的行为让你感到难过，但首先要表达你的感激之情。例如：“爸爸，我真的很关心你，而且我认为你是我认识的最聪明的人之一，但是每次我们意见不合时，你都沉默不语，然后走开，这真的让我很困扰。这正在损害我们的关系，我想知道你是否愿意和我谈谈这件事。”
  • Stay focused on the issue you’re upset about.
    专注于让你感到不安的问题。
  • Expect to be attacked when you express a grievance, because they experience your assertion as an attack on them.
    当你表达不满时，要做好遭到攻击的准备，因为他们会将你的说法视为对他们的攻击。
  • Let them know that you know they’re angry and what you’re willing to do about it. For example: “I’m sorry you’re upset because I don’t want your folks to stay with us when they’re in town, but I’m certainly willing to take the time to find a nice hotel for them and maybe pay for part of their vacation.”
    让他们知道你理解他们的不满，并说明你愿意如何解决。例如：“我很抱歉您不高兴，因为我不想让您的父母来城里时住在我们家，但我很乐意花时间帮他们找一家不错的酒店，或许还可以帮他们支付一部分度假费用。”
  • Accept the fact that you will have to make the first move most, if not all, of the time.
    要接受这样一个事实：大多数时候，甚至所有时候，你都必须迈出第一步。
  • Let some things slide.
    有些事就睁一只眼闭一只眼吧。

These techniques are the only ones that have a chance to interrupt the pattern that’s so typical of a silent, angry blackmailer, the cycle that goes “Look how upset I am, and it’s all your fault. Now figure out what you did wrong and how you’re going to make it up to me.” I know how infuriating it is to have to be the rational one when you feel like strangling the other person, but it’s the only way I know to create an atmosphere that will allow change to take place. Your hardest job will be to stay nondefensive and to convince the quietly angry person that it’s OK for them to be angry when they’ve spent a lifetime believing just the opposite.

只有这些技巧才有机会打破沉默而愤怒的勒索者典型的模式——“你看我多生气，都是你的错。现在想想你做错了什么，该怎么补偿我。”我知道，当你恨不得掐死对方时，还要保持理性是多么令人恼火，但这是我所知的唯一能创造改变氛围的方法。你最难的是保持不设防，并让那个默默愤怒的人明白，即使他们一生都坚信愤怒是理所当然的，他们也可以生气。

Feeling Furious but Staying Calm

内心愤怒，但保持冷静

We’ve talked a lot about dealing with the blackmailer’s anger, but how do you stay nondefensive when your own anger is welling up inside you? Allen, whose ex-wife, Beverly, was using their children as pawns in her punitive dealings with him, expressed this frustrating double bind during one session.

我们已经讨论了很多关于如何应对勒索者的愤怒，但是当你自己的愤怒在心中翻腾时，如何才能保持不设防呢？艾伦的前妻贝弗利利用他们的孩子作为惩罚他的筹码，艾伦在一次咨询中表达了这种令人沮丧的两难境地。

I took the kids camping last week, and when I got them back she started screaming because they were dirty and tired. They had a great time, but she said I pushed them too hard. Then she said that if I couldn’t take better care of them, she’d see about getting my visitation rights cut down. I know it was a mistake, but I just blew up at her and we started screaming at each other like a couple of lunatics. But she made me furious. How dare she threaten to keep me from seeing my kids? What the hell do I do now?

我上周带孩子们去露营，接他们回来的时候，她就开始大吼大叫，说孩子们又脏又累。孩子们玩得很开心，但她说我让他们太累了。然后她又说，如果我不能好好照顾他们，她就要想办法减少我的探视权。我知道我做错了，但我当时真的对她发火了，我们俩像疯子一样互相吼叫。她把我气疯了。她怎么敢威胁要不让我见孩子？我现在该怎么办？

There are situations for which we have no magic solutions. Beverly had been deeply hurt by the divorce, and since her attacks on Allen had escalated after he remarried, it was obvious that the only way he could change the way she was feeling was to be miserable himself. But he could certainly change whatever he might have been doing to increase the tension.

有些情况我们没有灵丹妙药。贝弗莉深受离婚之苦，艾伦再婚后她对他的攻击更是变本加厉，显然，他要想改变贝弗莉的感受，唯一的办法就是让自己也痛苦起来。但他当然可以改变自己那些加剧紧张关系的行为。

“I know how furious you are,” I said, “but you’re just going to have to learn to cool it. You’re getting pretty good at using nondefensive communication with Jo, so why don’t you try some with Beverly? The hardest thing to do is to act calm while you’re feeling homicidal.”

“我知道你有多生气，”我说，“但你必须学会冷静下来。你和乔沟通时已经很擅长用不带防御性的语气了，为什么不也试试和贝弗莉沟通呢？最难的就是在恨不得杀人的时候还要保持冷静。”

“You’ve got me well trained, Susan,” he said with a grin. “I know you’re going to say that the only person I can change is myself.”

“苏珊，你把我训练得很好，”他笑着说。“我知道你会说我唯一能改变的人只有我自己。”

“Right,” I answered. “Basically, your job is to zip your lip no matter how irrational she’s being and, depending on the situation, to say things like ‘I’m sorry you’re upset about the camping trip, but they really had a great time. Would you feel better if next time I plan something like this I explain to you before we leave what we’ll be doing and what to expect?’ You’ve also told me she doesn’t have the boys ready when you come to pick them up and sometimes they’re not even there. That’s infuriating, but as the custodial parent she has a lot of leverage, and you have to find a way to accept that or you’ll be in a constant state of rage and bitterness.

“没错，”我回答道。“基本上，无论她多么不讲道理，你都得忍住不说话。根据情况，你可以说些类似这样的话：‘很抱歉你对露营旅行感到不高兴，但孩子们玩得真的很开心。下次我再安排类似的活动时，如果我在出发前跟你解释一下我们的行程安排和注意事项，你会不会感觉好一些？’你也跟我说过，你来接孩子的时候，她没把孩子们准备好，有时候他们甚至都不在家。这确实很让人恼火，但作为监护人，她有很多话语权，你必须学会接受这一点，否则你会一直处于愤怒和怨恨之中。”

“Again, go back to some of those calm and calming phrases. Instead of ventilating your anger, take a deep breath and say, ‘I’d really appreciate it, Beverly, if you’d have the kids ready when I get there. Is there anything I can do to make it easier for you?’ I can’t predict how she’ll respond, but I promise you’re going to feel a lot less victimized.”

“再说一遍，用一些冷静平和的话语。不要发泄你的怒气，深呼吸，然后说：‘贝弗利，如果你能在我到的时候把孩子们准备好，我会非常感激的。有什么我可以帮你的吗？’我无法预测她会如何回应，但我保证你会感觉自己不再那么受害者了。”

STRATEGY 2: ENLISTING THE BLACKMAILER AS AN ALLY

策略二：争取勒索者成为盟友

When emotional blackmail reaches an impasse, it’s often helpful to shift the conversation by involving the other person in your problem-solving process. Asking for help, suggestions or information can open up possibilities you hadn’t considered, and it’s only human nature that other people will be happier to help carry out a decision if they’ve participated in making it than if they haven’t. If you approach the other person with curiosity and a willingness to learn, you can rapidly change the tone of an exchange that’s begun to deteriorate into attacks and defenses.

当情感勒索陷入僵局时，让对方参与到解决问题的过程中，往往能有效地转移话题。寻求帮助、建议或信息可以让你发现之前未曾考虑过的可能性。人之常情是，如果别人参与了决策过程，他们自然会更乐意帮忙执行。如果你以好奇心和学习的态度与对方交流，就能迅速扭转局面，避免陷入互相攻击和防御的泥潭。

The following questions can help cut through a lot of animosity and tension:

以下问题有助于消除许多敌意和紧张气氛：

  • Can you help me understand why this is so important to you?
    你能帮我理解一下为什么这件事对你如此重要吗？
  • Can you suggest some things we can do to solve the problem?
    您能否提出一些解决问题的建议？
  • Can you help me find some things we can do to make our relationship better?
    你能帮我想想我们可以做些什么来改善我们的关系吗？
  • Can you help me understand why you are so angry/upset?
    你能帮我理解一下你为什么这么生气/难过吗？

In addition, I recommend what I call the Wonder Tool, which sounds like something that ought to be advertised on an infomercial. Actually, it’s a strategy of encouraging the other person to imagine with you what change might feel like or how a problem might be solved.

此外，我还推荐一种我称之为“神奇工具”的方法，听起来像是电视购物广告里才会出现的噱头。实际上，这是一种策略，它鼓励对方和你一起想象改变会带来怎样的感受，或者问题会如何解决。

Bring out the Wonder Tool with statements such as:

用以下语句展现神奇工具的功能：

  • I wonder what would happen if . . .
    我想知道如果……会发生什么。
  • I wonder if you can help me find a way to . . .
    我想知道你是否能帮我找到一种方法……
  • I wonder how we can do this better/make this work.
    我想知道我们如何才能做得更好/让这件事成功。

To wonder with someone is to unlock the imagination and even a sense of playfulness—nondefensiveness at its most enjoyable. People don’t enjoy being attacked, but they’re often willing to help someone solve a problem.

与人一起探索未知，能激发想象力，甚至唤起玩乐之心——这是最令人愉悦的无防备状态。人们不喜欢被攻击，但他们往往乐于助人解决问题。

Listening for Solutions

倾听解决方案

Allen’s relationship with Jo was far less complex than his relationship with Beverly, since Allen and Jo loved each other and wanted to stay together. But Allen struggled to find a way to deal with his new wife’s neediness. After trying for several days to tell her that for the sake of his business, he was going to have to spend some time away from her, he came in to see me, looking for help to find a solution.

艾伦和乔的关系远比他和贝弗莉的关系简单得多，因为艾伦和乔彼此相爱，也想继续在一起。但艾伦却难以应对新婚妻子的依赖。他连续几天试图告诉乔，为了生意，他必须暂时离开她一段时间，但最终还是来找我，希望我能帮他找到解决办法。

I don’t know what I can do to keep her from freaking out when I take my trip up north. It’s just not going to work for me to say, “I don’t care how you feel. I don’t care how upset you are. I have to take this trip.” Then I’ll not only have the trip to worry about but a crying wife to boot.

我不知道该怎么做才能让她在我去北方旅行时不至于崩溃。如果我说“我不在乎你的感受，我不在乎你有多难过，我必须去”，那肯定行不通。那样的话，我不仅要担心旅行，还要面对一个哭泣的妻子。

I told Allen that he might be able to take some of the stress out of presenting his decision to Jo by asking her what would reduce her fears of being left alone. I reminded him that it wasn’t his job to fix Jo or deal with the early traumas in her life that had made her so dependent. She had to do that herself so that their marriage could be a partnership rather than a parent-child relationship. Meanwhile, though, he could make her an ally. We practiced how he might use “I wonder” and “I need to understand what I can do” to get Jo to participate in supporting his decision rather than pressuring him to change it.

我告诉艾伦，他可以问问乔，怎样才能减轻她害怕被抛弃的恐惧，这样或许能帮他减轻向乔解释决定时的压力。我提醒他，他没有义务去改变乔，也没有义务去处理她早年生活中那些让她如此依赖他的创伤。这些都需要她自己去面对，这样他们的婚姻才能成为伙伴关系，而不是父母与孩子的关系。与此同时，他可以争取乔的支持。我们练习了他如何运用“我想知道”和“我需要了解我能做些什么”这样的表达方式，让乔参与到支持他的决定中来，而不是强迫他改变主意。

“OK,” Allen said. “How about ‘Jo, I need to take a trip to San Francisco for a few days, and before you get upset, I wonder if you can help me understand why you get so neurotic when I step away for two seconds.’”

“好吧，”艾伦说，“不如这样说：‘乔，我需要去旧金山出差几天，在你生气之前，我想问问你能不能帮我理解一下，为什么我离开你两秒钟你就会这么神经质。’”

“No, Allen. We’re not trying to label anyone here, just get information. She might have suggestions for improving things, so ask her. How about ‘Jo, I have to go up north for a few days on a business trip. I know you get worried when we have to be apart, but this is an important trip, and I wonder what I can do to make you feel better about my going.’”

“不，艾伦。我们不是要给任何人贴标签，只是想了解情况。她或许能提出一些改进建议，所以问问她吧。比如，你可以这样说：‘乔，我得去北方出差几天。我知道我们分开的时候你会担心，但这趟出差很重要，我想知道我该怎么做才能让你安心些。’”

By putting his dilemma to her in this way, Allen would be acknowledging Jo’s feelings. He would not be calling her names, nor would he be leaving the door open to the possibility of his not going.

艾伦这样向乔表达自己的困境，就是在体谅她的感受。他既没有辱骂她，也没有留下自己不去的后路。

It was a lot smoother than I thought it would be. I said what we worked on, and as soon as I asked what would make her feel less anxious about the trip she said, “Take me with you.” I told her I wouldn’t have a problem with that, but I also said that it was going to be a work trip, not a vacation, and she’d probably be by herself a lot since I had so many meetings to go to. At first she said that was fine, she likes hotels, but later she said she’d thought it over, and she’d be more comfortable at home. So it became her choice to stay behind. She just wanted me to call her every evening. God, it was such a relief. We’ve never worked anything out that way before — it’s always been all or nothing.

比我想象的顺利得多。我跟她说了我们之前商量的事情，然后我问她怎样才能减轻她对这次旅行的焦虑，她立刻说：“带我一起去吧。” 我告诉她我没问题，但我也说了这是一次出差，不是度假，而且因为我有很多会议要开，她可能大部分时间都会一个人待着。一开始她说没问题，她喜欢住酒店，但后来她说她仔细想了想，觉得待在家里更舒服。所以最后她决定留在家里。她只希望我每天晚上给她打个电话。天哪，真是松了一口气。我们以前从来没有这样解决过问题——总是要么全盘接受，要么全盘否定。

What had changed was Allen’s decision to do what he needed to do and to work with Jo to take her feelings into account. Together, they’d found a mutual solution that Allen might have overlooked or been reluctant to suggest if he hadn’t been willing to ally with Jo instead of fighting with her.

改变的是艾伦决定去做他必须做的事，并且愿意与乔合作，顾及她的感受。他们共同找到了一个双方都能接受的解决方案，如果艾伦不愿意与乔结盟而不是与她对抗，他或许会忽略这个方案，或者根本不愿提出这个方案。

Asking the Boss for Help

向老板寻求帮助

Kim used a variety of nondefensive techniques to let her boss, Ken, know that she wanted him to stop using negative comparisons and that she needed to cut back her workload to protect her health. She especially liked the idea of enlisting him as an ally because, as she put it,

金运用多种非防御性技巧，让她的老板肯明白，她希望他停止使用负面比较，并且她需要减少工作量以保护自己的健康。她尤其喜欢争取肯作为盟友的想法，因为正如她所说，

I’m not in a position to lay down the law and impose my will, but I can do what we’re all supposed to do around here — be a good team player. I used to think that just meant do whatever anyone asks, no matter what the cost, but I’ve begun to think of it more as real teamwork, doing the best I can, pitching in when we’re in a crunch and easing off when I need to for my life and my health.

我没有资格立规矩、强加意志，但我可以做我们在这里都应该做的事——做一个优秀的团队成员。我以前认为这意味着无论付出什么代价都要照做，但现在我开始把它理解为真正的团队合作，尽我所能做到最好，在关键时刻挺身而出，在需要为了我的生命和健康而休息的时候适时放手。

Kim also wanted to put an end to Ken’s pressure tactics, and we came up with this way of approaching him:

金也想结束肯的施压策略，于是我们想出了以下应对方法：

Ken, you may not be aware of it, but I’ve noticed that you compare me to Miranda very consistently. In the past, it’s been a really effective way to get me to go above and beyond, but it’s not going to work anymore. I’ll give you 110 percent and do as much as I can without injuring myself, because I want to and because I really like this job. I’m glad you respect me, and I certainly respect you. But please stop playing good kid/bad kid with me. We’re two adults. You’re not my father, and I’m not your daughter. I’m three years older than you are, for god’s sake. And Miranda’s not my sister, so I’m busting up this dysfunctional family.

肯，你可能没注意到，但我一直觉得你总是拿我和米兰达比较。以前，这招确实能激励我更加努力，但现在不管用了。我会付出百分之百的努力，尽我所能做到最好，只要不伤到自己，因为我真的想做，也真的很喜欢这份工作。我很感激你尊重我，我也非常尊重你。但请不要再跟我玩“好孩子/坏孩子”的游戏了。我们都是成年人。你不是我父亲，我也不是你女儿。看在上帝的份上，我比你大三岁。米兰达也不是我妹妹，所以我才要拆散这个不和睦的家庭。

For Kim, as for anyone who is fluent on paper but whose words seem to fail them when they’re face-to-face with someone, it was vital to practice. She rounded up a friend to listen and role-play with her, practiced aloud in the car, got help from her husband—and went in knowing her lines cold.

对金来说，就像对任何一个书面表达流畅但面对面交流时却词不达意的人一样，练习至关重要。她找了个朋友来听她练习角色扮演，在车里大声练习，还请丈夫帮忙——最终，她对所有台词都烂熟于心。

STRATEGY 3: BARTERING

策略三：以物易物

When you want another person to change his or her behavior, and at the same time you acknowledge that you need to make changes of your own, a barter may be in order. Most of us have been making trades since we were kids—two superhero comics for a book, my tuna sandwich for your peanut-butter-and-jelly—giving up something to get something of equal value. The great thing about bartering to reduce emotional blackmail is that it eliminates the idea that the burden of change rests entirely on one person. In bartering, there’s no giving without getting. There are no losers.

当你希望他人改变行为，同时又意识到自己需要做出改变时，以物易物或许是个不错的选择。我们大多数人从孩提时代就开始进行交易——两本超级英雄漫画换一本书，我的金枪鱼三明治换你的花生酱果冻三明治——用一部分换取等值的东西。以物易物减少情感勒索的妙处在于，它消除了“改变的责任完全落在一个人身上”的想法。在以物易物中，付出必有回报，没有输家。

I saw the power of barter to shake people out of an emotional blackmail impasse when a couple, Matt and Amy, came into my office a few years ago. Amy was furious with Matt for ignoring her.

几年前，一对夫妇马特和艾米来到我的办公室，我亲眼见证了以物易物如何帮助人们摆脱情感勒索的僵局。艾米因为马特忽视她而非常生气。

He treats me like I’m invisible. He gets up, goes to work, comes home for dinner and hardly talks, then sits in front of the television until it’s time for bed. He hasn’t touched me in weeks, and I have never felt more lonely in my life.

他把我当空气一样看待。他起床上班，回家吃晚饭，几乎不说话，然后就坐在电视机前直到睡觉时间。他已经好几个星期没碰过我了，我这辈子从未感到如此孤独。

Matt, for his part, said the issue was really Amy’s weight:

马特则表示，真正的问题在于艾米的体重：

This is not the woman I married. I think her hobby is eating , and I think you can see that she’s gotten pretty large as a result. I just don’t find that too appealing. She says I’m acting like I’m not attracted to her and she’s right — I’m not. Not when she weighs this much. I’m not going to pretend that it doesn’t make any difference to me.

这已经不是我娶的那个女人了。我觉得她最大的爱好就是吃，而且你也看得出来，她因此变得很胖。我实在欣赏不来。她说我表现得好像对她没感觉，她说得对——我的确没感觉。她这么胖，我怎么可能喜欢她？我不会假装这对我来说无关紧要。

Matt and Amy’s relationship had deteriorated to “If you don’t find a way to be more loving, I’m going to leave” on her part and “If you don’t lose weight, I’m going to continue to punish you by withdrawing” on his part. They didn’t put these threats into words, but they didn’t need to—their behavior made their feelings as clear as if they’d been shouted through a PA system.

马特和艾米的关系恶化到艾米威胁说：“如果你再不变得更爱我，我就离开你”，而马特则威胁说：“如果你不减肥，我就要继续疏远你来惩罚你”。他们没有把这些威胁说出口，但其实根本不需要——他们的行为已经把彼此的感受表达得淋漓尽致，就像用扩音器大声喊出来一样。

Amy was eating because she felt neglected, and Matt said he was neglecting her because she was eating so much. They were stuck, and blaming each other for their unhappiness. So I set up a barter: Amy would start a diet tomorrow, and Matt would put aside half an hour after he got home each night to talk with her and re-establish contact. Of course, Amy didn’t lose weight overnight, and Matt didn’t turn into Mr. Communication immediately, but they were able to make significant progress toward breaking out of their stalemate—and, ultimately, mending their relationship.

艾米因为感觉被冷落而暴饮暴食，而马特则说她吃得太多，所以他才冷落了她。他们陷入了僵局，互相指责对方造成了彼此的不快乐。于是我提出了一个交换条件：艾米从明天开始节食，而马特每天晚上回家后抽出半小时和她谈谈，重新建立联系。当然，艾米不可能一夜之间瘦下来，马特也不可能立刻变成沟通高手，但他们确实在打破僵局方面取得了显著进展——最终，他们的关系也得到了修复。

No one likes to look or feel as though they’re giving in, and our distaste for one-sided solutions holds most people back from taking the first step toward resolving a dispute. But bartering creates a win-win situation that’s easy for everyone to accept. It also cuts through another dynamic that keeps us from working out problems with someone else—the feeling that they’ve done us wrong, we’re mad about it, and they need to suffer. We won’t give an inch because they need to be punished more. But somehow, the sense of getting something from the other person lets us put our resentments aside more easily.

没有人喜欢看起来像是在让步，或者感觉自己像是在让步，我们对单方面解决方案的反感也阻碍了大多数人迈出解决争端的第一步。但以物易物却能创造一个双赢的局面，让每个人都能轻松接受。它还能打破另一种阻碍我们与他人解决问题的心理——那种“对方亏待了我们，我们为此感到愤怒，他们应该受到惩罚”的感觉。我们寸步不让，因为他们觉得应该受到更大的惩罚。但不知何故，从对方那里获得一些东西的感觉，却能让我们更容易地放下怨恨。

Bartering is a particularly effective strategy because it allows each party to get something they want without the blaming and attacking that is so typical of most conflicts.

以物易物是一种特别有效的策略，因为它可以让每一方都得到自己想要的东西，而不会像大多数冲突那样互相指责和攻击。

Eliminating the Impasse

打破僵局

Bartering allowed Lynn and Jeff to put down the pressure tactics that each had directed at the other. They agreed that at bottom, the unresolved issue in their marriage was the disparity in their financial resources, something that Lynn, in particular, still had problems accepting. But as they sat in my office and talked with each other, they began to see each other as humans again instead of just objects of anger. Each came with a peace offering, and they did their best to be as nondefensive as they could. Lynn began:

以物易物让琳恩和杰夫放下了彼此施加的压力。他们一致认为，婚姻中悬而未决的问题根源在于经济资源的差距，琳恩尤其难以接受这一点。但当他们坐在我的办公室里交谈时，他们开始重新将彼此视为人，而不是愤怒的对象。两人都提出了和解的方案，并尽力做到不带任何防备。琳恩开口说道：

I know this money thing is something I need to work on some more. I thought it was OK with me, and we made an agreement when we got together that I wouldn’t hold it over you and treat you like a kid getting an allowance or something. So I’m going to honor that agreement. What I need from you, Jeff, is a promise that when something comes up, like buying you a new truck, we’ll look at the finances together and make a decision based on what we think we can afford. In other words, no more pressure that you’ll disappear if you don’t get what you want. I need to understand why you leave without telling me where you’re going when you know it makes me so crazy.

我知道我在金钱方面还需要多加努力。我原以为我做得还不错，而且我们刚在一起的时候也约定好，我不会拿钱来要挟你，也不会把你当成拿零花钱的小孩。所以我会信守这个约定。杰夫，我需要你承诺，以后如果有什么事，比如我想给你买辆新卡车，我们会一起看看财务状况，根据我们各自的承受能力来做决定。换句话说，别再给我施加压力，说如果得不到你想要的就会消失。我需要明白，你明知道这会让我抓狂，为什么还要一声不响地离开。

Jeff answered:

杰夫回答道：

Sometimes I feel so angry when I have to beg for something I need that I feel like I have to get out of the house or I’ll do something I’ll regret. I have to let off steam, and when I take off, I don’t know how long it’ll take to cool down. I don’t even know where I’m going half the time.

有时候，当我需要什么东西却不得不苦苦哀求时，我会感到非常愤怒，感觉必须离开家，否则我会做出让自己后悔的事情。我必须发泄一下，而一旦离开家，我不知道要多久才能冷静下来。很多时候，我甚至不知道自己要去哪里。

Lynn responded:

琳恩回应道：

I know how angry my attitude toward money has made you. I apologize for that, and I promise to work on it. I know if we keep talking about this, instead of my holding in my feelings and then taking them out on you, we can resolve the money issue. But I need you to at least tell me you’re leaving instead of storming out, and I need you to give me some kind of time frame about when you’ll be back. I know you don’t always know, but please try. And when you do know, you can call me and let me know where you are and when you’ll be back. It’ll make me feel a lot better.

我知道我对金钱的态度让你很生气。我为此道歉，并保证会改正。我知道如果我们继续沟通，而不是我把情绪憋在心里最后发泄在你身上，我们就能解决金钱问题。但我需要你至少告诉我你要离开，而不是拂袖而去。我需要你告诉我大概什么时候回来。我知道你有时可能不确定，但请尽量告诉我。当你确定了之后，可以打电话告诉我你在哪里，什么时候回来。这样我会安心很多。

Jeff said:

杰夫说：

You know I love you and I’m not going anywhere for long. But if it’ll help I’ll be specific about where I’m going and for how long. And maybe it’s time to rethink the finances. I want to look at them together with you — I’m better with money than you think—and I know there are things I can do to make money on the side. I’ve been thinking about training horses around the valley, but I was so angry at you I didn’t even want to mention it. I thought you’d make fun of me because I’m still not going to make as much as you do—probably ever.

你知道我爱你，我不会离开太久。但如果这样对你有帮助，我可以具体说说我要去哪里，待多久。也许是时候重新考虑一下财务状况了。我想和你一起看看——我比你想象的更会理财——我知道我可以做一些兼职来赚点外快。我一直在考虑在山谷附近训练马匹，但我当时太生你的气了，甚至都不想提这件事。我以为你会嘲笑我，因为我赚的钱永远也比不上你——可能永远也比不上。

Jeff and Lynn still had a lot of talking, listening and negotiating to do, but by using barter they had laid the groundwork for doing that.

杰夫和琳恩仍然有很多话要说，有很多话要听，还有很多谈判要做，但通过以物易物，他们已经为此奠定了基础。

Actions, Not Words

行动胜于言辞

Sherry, whose boss and lover, Charles, threatened to fire her when she decided to end their romantic involvement, decided that she’d ask three things of him in a barter that had advantages for both of them: Nonnegotiable was that under no circumstances was she willing to sleep with him any longer. That was a matter of basic integrity. But she did offer to stay at her job until she’d finished the projects she was working on and had helped Charles hire and train her replacement.
