当潜意识抗拒健康的改变时，我发现用比喻和故事来引导它，比传统的谈话疗法更有效。为了帮助简做到这一点，我让她写一个关于她和妹妹关系的童话故事。“那肯定会是个格林童话，”她讽刺地说。“那我该怎么做呢？”

I told her she could write anything she wanted but to use fairy tale language and images, write the story in the third person, and give it, if not a happy ending, at least a hopeful ending.

我告诉她，她可以写任何她想写的东西，但要使用童话般的语言和意象，用第三人称来写这个故事，即使不能给它一个快乐的结局，至少也要给它一个充满希望的结局。

The story Jan wrote is very special, and I’d like to share it with you:

Jan写的故事非常特别，我想和你们分享：

Once upon a time there were two little princesses. One was the king’s favorite and her closets were filled with beautiful clothes and jewels. She rode around in a golden coach, and she only had to wish for something to have it. The other little princess was the queen’s favorite. This princess was smart and brave, but it seemed there was nothing left for her, for her sister had told lies to the king to make the poor princess look bad in his eyes. So the poor little princess wore clothes cast off by her spoiled sister, and when she asked the king for toys or for carrots to feed her pony (she only had a pony instead of a coach), he told her: “Apprentice yourself to a tradesman in town,” the king’s fancy way of saying “Get a job!” So the poor little princess went to work for the town jeweler, who taught her to make beautiful things, and who praised her talent and industry.

从前，有两个小公主。一个是国王最宠爱的公主，她的衣橱里塞满了漂亮的衣服和珠宝。她乘坐着金马车，只要许愿就能得到想要的东西。另一个小公主是王后最宠爱的公主。这位公主聪明又勇敢，但似乎什么都没有留给她，因为她的姐姐为了在国王面前丢脸，对国王撒了谎。于是，可怜的小公主只能穿她那娇生惯养的姐姐脱下的衣服。当她向国王要玩具或胡萝卜喂她的小马（她只有一匹小马，没有马车）时，国王却对她说：“去城里找个工匠当学徒吧。” 国王这番话其实就是委婉地说：“去找份工作吧！” 于是，可怜的小公主就去城里的珠宝商那里当学徒。珠宝商教她制作精美的饰品，并称赞她的才华和勤劳。

When the princesses grew up, the spoiled princess married a toad who didn’t care that she couldn’t cook or work. Oh, the toad was handsome enough, but he was a wastrel and a ne’er-do-well. He loved her for her riches, which he wanted to invest in swamp real estate. Soon, all the spoiled princess’s jewels were gone, and she and the toad were forced to go begging. This was a great humiliation for the spoiled princess.

公主们长大后，那位娇生惯养的公主嫁给了一只癞蛤蟆，癞蛤蟆根本不在乎她不会做饭也不会干活。哦，这癞蛤蟆长相还算不错，但他是个游手好闲、游手好闲的家伙。他爱上公主，是因为她家财万贯，他想把这些钱投资到沼泽地的地产上。很快，公主所有的珠宝都花光了，她和癞蛤蟆被迫流落街头乞讨。这对娇生惯养的公主来说，无疑是莫大的耻辱。

In the meantime, the poor little princess had worked hard and made a great success of her life. The kindly town jeweler had let her take over his shop when he got too old to run it, and she was famous for making the kingdom’s most beautiful crowns and rings. She had her own jewelry franchise, Princess Jewelry, and she was proud of all she’d worked to make. The only sadness in her life was the memory of how her father and her sister had treated her when she was little.

与此同时，可怜的小公主辛勤工作，取得了巨大的成功。善良的镇上珠宝商年老体衰后，将店铺交给了她经营。她以制作王国中最精美的皇冠和戒指而闻名。她拥有了自己的珠宝连锁店——“公主珠宝”，并为自己的一切成就感到自豪。她生命中唯一的悲伤，是小时候父亲和姐姐对待她的方式。

So when the selfish princess came to her door and pleaded with her to give her some jewels so she could keep the royal carriage from being repossessed and her castle from going into foreclosure, the hardworking princess was faced with a terrible dilemma. “Please help me,” the selfish princess pleaded. “I know I’ve never been nice to you at all, but if you just give me some of what you’ve worked so hard to earn, I’ll be as close as a sister should be.”

所以，当那个自私的公主来到她家门口，恳求她给她一些珠宝，好让她保住皇家马车不被收回、城堡不被取消抵押赎回权时，勤劳的公主陷入了进退两难的境地。“请帮帮我，”自私的公主哀求道，“我知道我以前对你不好，但如果你能把你辛辛苦苦挣来的东西分给我一些，我就会像亲姐妹一样和你亲近。”

The hardworking princess wanted to believe her, and she wanted very much to have her sister in her life. But her sister had never been good to her, and the hardworking princess was worried that she hadn’t changed at all. To sort out her troubled thoughts, she went for a walk in the woods and came to a crystal-clear pool. She sat there, gazing at her reflection and asking it, “What should I do? What should I do? I know my sister will waste whatever I give her, but how I would love to have a sister’s love!” As she spoke, one of her tears fell into the pool, and when the water stilled again, she saw that her reflection had been replaced by the reflection of her best friend.

勤劳的公主很想相信她，她非常渴望拥有妹妹。可是妹妹从来没对她好过，公主担心妹妹一点都没变。为了理清思绪，她去树林里散步，来到一个清澈见底的水潭边。她坐在那里，凝视着自己的倒影，喃喃自语道：“我该怎么办？我该怎么办？我知道妹妹会浪费我给她的一切，但我多么渴望拥有姐妹的爱啊！”说着，一滴眼泪落入了水潭。当水面再次平静下来时，她发现自己的倒影已经变成了她最好的朋友的倒影。

“You have a sister,” the reflection said. “I love you and care for you as your blood sister never did, and you will always have family like me.”

“你有个妹妹，”倒影说道。“我爱你，关心你，就像你的亲妹妹从未做过的那样，你永远都会有像我这样的家人。”

The hardworking princess knew that this was so, and when she returned home, she told the spoiled princess, “You can’t have the jewels from my shop. You’ve never had a gift that you didn’t lose in the swamp. I wish we could have been close, but we’re not, and maybe we’ll never be. The jewels can’t change that.”

勤劳的公主明白这一点，回到家后，她对娇生惯养的公主说：“你不能拿走我店里的珠宝。你从来没有收到过一件礼物，最后都丢在了沼泽里。我希望我们能亲近一些，但我们不是，也许永远也不会是。这些珠宝也改变不了这一点。”

Jan said writing the story was very powerful for her:

简说，写作这个故事对她来说意义非凡：

I really saw the truth. My sister’s never going to change. A thousand dollars can’t come close to fixing what’s wrong. From the time we were little, Carol tried to take things and lied about me and tried to get me in trouble with Mother and Dad. I’ve never had a close relationship with her, and I probably never will. But I felt so much better when I found myself writing about real sisters. My two closest friends are closer than family, closer than my own sister could ever be. So I haven’t lost anything—except a load of guilt.

我终于看清了真相。我妹妹永远不会改变。一千美元也弥补不了我们之间的问题。从我们小时候起，卡罗尔就总是想方设法拿走我的东西，编造关于我的谎言，还想方设法让我和爸妈闹矛盾。我和她从来没有过亲密的关系，以后可能也不会了。但是，当我开始写关于真正姐妹的故事时，我感觉好多了。我最亲密的两个朋友比家人还亲，比我亲妹妹还要亲密。所以，我并没有失去什么——除了满满的愧疚感。

Putting the story in the third person gave Jan some needed emotional distance, so she could see her relationship with her sister with real clarity. And using the fairy tale form frees up the imagination, with all its creativity and humor—a powerful weapon against guilt. Imagination is as light as guilt is heavy, and it leavens our darkest feelings.

用第三人称叙述故事让简与妹妹保持了必要的距离，使她能够更清晰地看待自己与妹妹的关系。而童话故事的形式则解放了想象力，使其充满创造力和幽默感——这是对抗内疚的有力武器。想象力轻盈如羽，与沉重的内疚形成鲜明对比，它能抚慰我们最黑暗的情感。

I encourage you to write your own fairy tale to gain a deeper perspective about a relationship that’s making you feel guilty. It’s especially effective to write about family members, but you can also write about a friend or lover (“Once upon a time there lived a king and a queen. The king used to go into the forest to sulk if he didn’t get his way . . .”). I think you’ll be surprised and pleased at what your story can reveal to you, and how much clarity it can give you about a situation in which you’ve been blinded by guilt.

我鼓励你写一个属于你自己的童话故事，以便更深入地了解一段让你感到内疚的关系。写关于家人的故事尤其有效，但你也可以写关于朋友或爱人的故事（“从前，住着一位国王和一位王后。如果国王的要求得不到满足，他就会独自到森林里生闷气……”）。我相信你会惊喜地发现，你的故事能揭示出很多东西，也能让你从内疚的蒙蔽中解脱出来，看清事情的真相。

I know I’ve thrown a lot of information and a lot of work at you in this chapter, and some of it may stir up some strong emotions. You might feel sadness at the loss of safety in a relationship or inevitable anger at a blackmailer for pushing you around and at yourself for giving in so consistently. This work may even activate some unfinished business from your childhood.

我知道这一章里我塞给你很多信息和很多工作，其中一些内容可能会引发你强烈的情绪。你可能会因为失去一段安全感而感到悲伤，或者对勒索者百般刁难、对自己屡次妥协而感到愤怒。这项工作甚至可能会触动你童年时期一些未了的心结。

Be kind to yourself, and pay attention to your feelings and what they’re telling you. If you feel yourself becoming overwhelmed, some brief counseling might be appropriate at this time, or you might want to seek extra support from someone close to you. Remember, you don’t have to do everything in the next twenty-four hours. Go at your own pace, and pick those exercises and assignments that apply to you. I promise you that it will be well worth the effort.

善待自己，留意自己的感受以及它们传递的信息。如果你感到压力过大，不妨考虑接受一些简短的心理咨询，或者寻求亲近之人的额外支持。记住，你无需在接下来的24小时内完成所有事情。按照自己的节奏，选择适合自己的练习和作业。我保证，这一切的努力都将是值得的。

# ↩

Epilogue

结语

Changing your behavior is not a linear process, and it’s not instantaneous. As you make the skills you’ve learned an integral part of your life, you’ll find that you won’t get it right all the time. You may falter, you may get scared, you’ll try and sometimes you’ll fail—everyone does. But you’ll continue to learn from both your triumphs and your mistakes.

改变行为并非一个线性过程，也并非一蹴而就。当你将所学技能融入生活后，你会发现自己不可能总是做得完美。你可能会犯错，可能会感到害怕，你会尝试，有时也会失败——每个人都会经历这些。但你会从成功和失败中不断学习。

Remember, what you’re doing is like climbing a mountain except that no one ever gets to the top. No one is so articulate and anxiety-free that they can always come up with exactly the right words to deflect another person’s pressure and threats. Be gentle and forgiving with yourself. As you work your way up this mountain of change, you’ll probably glance up and think “Oh god, I’ve still got so far to go!” But turn around for a moment and look down to the place you started. You’ll see how far you’ve come.

记住，你现在做的就像攀登一座山，只不过没有人能真正到达顶峰。没有人能言善辩、毫无焦虑，总能找到恰到好处的措辞来化解他人的压力和威胁。请善待自己，宽容自己。当你努力攀登这座变革之山时，你可能会抬头望向山顶，心想：“天哪，我还有好远的路要走！” 但请稍作停留，回头看看你出发的地方。你会看到自己已经走了多远。

THE MIRACLE OF CHANGE

变革的奇迹

Once you stop waiting for other people to change and start working on your own behavior, miracles really can happen. Using just one of your new tools will send ripples of change through any relationship. Look at what happened with Liz and Michael.

当你不再等待别人改变，而是开始改变自己的行为时，奇迹真的会发生。仅仅运用你新掌握的其中一项技能，就能在任何关系中引发连锁反应。看看莉兹和迈克尔的例子就知道了。

“Can you believe how different Michael is?” Liz asked me one day. “I really didn’t think we were going to make it.”

“你能相信迈克尔变化有多大吗？”有一天，莉兹问我。“我真没想到我们能成功。”

“But who changed first?” I asked.

“但是谁先改变的呢？”我问。

“I guess I did,” she said. “I had my doubts when you said that’s how it works, but I can see that if I’d kept doing what I’d always done, we never would have survived.”

“我想我的确做到了，”她说。“你告诉我事情就是这样运作的时候，我还有些怀疑，但我现在明白了，如果我一直像以前那样做，我们肯定活不下去。”

Liz smiled broadly as she opened her purse and took out a folded piece of paper. “It’s a letter Michael wrote for his therapy, and he asked me to show it to you.”

莉兹咧嘴一笑，打开钱包，拿出一张折叠的纸。“这是迈克尔为他的心理治疗写的一封信，他让我拿给你看。”

It was quite a letter!

这封信真是够特别的！

To the blackmailer inside me:

致我内心的勒索者：

Hello.

你好。

I need to have some words with you. I would like your undivided attention to a matter of great importance to me.

我需要和你单独谈谈。有一件对我来说非常重要的事情，希望你能全神贯注地听我说。

You have been the cause of a lot of trouble for me for quite some time now. I didn’t really have any idea as to what was going on until Liz and John [Michael’s therapist] pointed you out. Many things are much more clear to me now, and you and I are going to have this out right now.

你给我惹了不少麻烦，已经持续很久了。直到莉兹和约翰（迈克尔的心理医生）指出你，我才恍然大悟。现在很多事情我都明白了，我们俩现在就要好好谈谈。

I’m hurting right now because of the tension and unhappiness I have caused because of you. When I think of how close I came to losing everything I love because I stupidly believed that I could feel like a real powerful and in-charge guy by bullying my wife to do whatever I wanted her to do and by punishing her if she didn’t, I am appalled and very angry at you.

我现在很痛苦，因为你给我带来了紧张和不快。想到我差点失去所有我爱的东西，就因为我愚蠢地以为，通过欺凌妻子，让她做任何我想让她做的事，或者如果她不听话就惩罚她，我就能觉得自己是个真正有权有势的人，我就感到震惊和愤怒。

I am astonished at the scope of my insensitivity. To think that I have looked my wife in the eye and been mean, demeaning and emotionally cruel and thought I was righting some wrong fills me with grief for hurting her, for lost moments, for lost love, for acting exactly the opposite of how I feel, for not respecting and honoring the most important of all things, human dignity and individuality.

我对自己如此麻木不仁感到震惊。想到我曾直视妻子的眼睛，对她恶语相向、贬低她、冷酷无情，还以为自己是在纠正什么错误，我就感到无比悲痛，因为我伤害了她，失去了那些美好的时光，失去了爱，我的所作所为与我的内心感受截然相反，我没有尊重和珍视最重要的东西——人的尊严和个性。

I want you to know, Mr. Blackmailer, that there is no place inside of me for your way. I am not willing to compromise about this. It’s not OK with me anymore.

勒索者先生，我要让你明白，你的方式在我心中没有立足之地。我不会在这件事上妥协。我再也无法容忍这种行为了。

I know it won’t be easy. There are a lot of things still to learn, a lot of habits to break, a lot of fears of looking weak to overcome. But I have done hard things before that didn’t mean as much to me as this, and I will do this, too. Your days are done, and this day and the next are something new.

我知道这并不容易。还有很多东西要学，很多习惯要改，很多害怕显得软弱的恐惧要克服。但我以前也做过一些艰难的事情，它们对我来说意义远不及这件事，而这件事我也一定能做到。你过去的日子已经过去，今天和明天都是崭新的一天。

Good-bye.

再见。

—Michael

——迈克尔

Like most blackmail targets, Liz had put her faith in complying, believing that she could buy stability by giving in to Michael’s demands. She had no way of knowing that she was only reinforcing the behavior in Michael that was tearing them apart. Once she changed her responses to him, she opened the door to the closeness they both craved.

和大多数被勒索的对象一样，莉兹也抱着顺从的心态，相信只要满足迈克尔的要求就能换来稳定。她丝毫没有意识到，自己这样做只会加剧迈克尔的不良行为，最终导致两人关系破裂。当她改变了对迈克尔的态度后，她打开了通往两人都渴望的亲密关系的大门。

“All I can say is, if this can happen, then I do believe in miracles,” Liz said. “I have Michael back—and I have myself back, too.”

“我只能说，如果这都能发生，那我相信奇迹，”莉兹说。“迈克尔回来了——我也找回了自己。”

I can’t guarantee that if you do this work you will always be rewarded with a dramatic response like Michael’s from the blackmailers in your life. But even if the people around you change very little, you will be different and the world will look different to you. You will know that any relationship that can only survive if you remain a compliant target of emotional blackmail is not a relationship that will nourish your well-being.

我无法保证你这样做之后，身边那些勒索者一定会像迈克尔那样做出戏剧性的回应。但即便你周围的人变化不大，你也会变得不同，你眼中的世界也会有所不同。你会明白，任何一段只能靠你继续顺从地接受情感勒索才能维系的关系，都无法滋养你的身心健康。

COMING HOME

回家

A wonderful sense of normalcy and balance returns when you are able to cut through the FOG and interrupt emotional bullying. The confusion and self-reproach that were so much a part of your feelings and self-image lift, and in their place comes a new sense of confidence and self-respect.

当你能够拨开迷雾，摆脱情感霸凌时，一种美妙的正常感和平衡感就会回归。曾经深深困扰你、影响你自我认知的困惑和自责会消散，取而代之的是全新的自信和自尊。

With every step you take to learn and use skills that will disarm your emotional blackmailers, you will be restoring the very core of your being—your integrity. That precious wholeness you mourned for was never really lost—just misplaced.

你每迈出一步，学习并运用那些能解除情感勒索者的技巧，你都将重塑你存在的本质——你的正直。你所哀悼的那份珍贵的完整，从未真正失去——只是暂时错放了而已。

It has been waiting for you.

它一直在等你。

作者简介

SUSAN FORWARD, P H .D., is an internationally acclaimed therapist, lecturer, and author. Her books include the #1 New York Times bestsellers Men Who Hate Women and the Women Who Love Them and Toxic Parents , as well as Obsessive Love , Betrayal of Innocence , and Money Demons . She lives in Los Angles, California.

苏珊·福沃德博士是一位享誉国际的治疗师、讲师和作家。她的著作包括荣登《纽约时报》畅销书榜首的《恨女人的男人和爱他们的女人》和《有毒的父母》，以及《痴迷的爱》、《背叛纯真》和《金钱恶魔》。她现居加利福尼亚州洛杉矶。
